title: Sean Payton: We're preparing for Patrick Mahomes at his best
summary: Throughout the offseason program and training camp, all indications have been that Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes would be ready to play Week 1 against the Broncos — despite suffering a torn ACL in December.
full_text: Throughout the offseason program and training camp, all indications have been that Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes would be ready to play Week 1 against the Broncos — despite suffering a torn ACL in December. While Kansas City has not made an official announcement that Mahomes will be behind center, Denver head coach Sean Payton is treating that as a given this week. "I’m going to probably say the same for Bo [Nix] — you’ve seen enough things where he’s going to be 100 percent and we’re preparing for him at his best," Payton said in his Wednesday press conference, via transcript from the team. "We know how talented he is, and I’m sure he’s attacked the rehab the way Bo has with completely different injuries. That’s kind of our approach to it.” Mahomes has historically fared quite well against the Broncos, with the Chiefs going 13-2 against them in his 15 starts. But Denver has also played him tough, as the quarterback has thrown for 21 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in those matchups. That’s a significant contrast to his numbers against the division-rival Raiders (36 TDs, five INTs) and Chargers (28 TDs, eight INTs). The Broncos and Chiefs will cap Week 1 with Monday Night Football from Arrowhead Stadium.
author: Myles Simmons

title: 49ers, Rams taking opposite approaches to longest road trip in NFL history
summary: The 49ers are already in the air aboard their 16-hour flight to Melbourne, Australia, for a game against the Rams that won't kick off for another seven and a half days.
full_text: The 49ers are already in the air aboard their 16-hour flight to Melbourne, Australia, for a game against the Rams that won't kick off for another seven and a half days. They want plenty of time to adjust to Melbourne time after the longest road trip in NFL history. The Rams are taking a very different approach. Although Rams coach Sean McVay has declined to discuss the team’s travel plans , they're reportedly leaving on Wednesday, September 9, which will mean landing less than 24 hours before kickoff: The game kicks off at 8:35 p.m. Eastern on Thursday, September 10, which is 10:35 a.m. on Friday, September 11, in Melbourne. The Rams think delaying international travel for as long as possible the smart approach, and there's some precedent to suggest they're right: Last year the Rams didn't arrive in London for their game against the Jaguars until the day before, and they proceeded to destroy the Jaguars, who have long-established London travel plans of arriving days in advance. The NFL requires teams traveling to games to put enough of a buffer into their travel plans to ensure that even if there are flight delays, the game itself won't be delayed. The Rams are cutting it about as close as the NFL will let them. But as the NFL continues to push international expansion, the league might love to see the Rams successfully pull off long road trips in a short time: If teams can show they don't need a lot of time to adjust before and after road games, that lends credence to the NFL's stance that the league could successfully put teams overseas on a permanent basis, with long road trips in both directions not compromising the quality of the competition.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Report: George Kittle, Nick Bosa will travel to Australia
summary: The 49ers hope to have both players in the lineup against the Rams.
full_text: 49ers tight end George Kittle's chances of playing in Week 1 are going up. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Kittle will travel to Australia with the team ahead of their matchup with the Rams in Melbourne. Kittle has practiced the last two days and, per the report, is trending in the right direction to play. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier this week that he'd prefer not to take Kittle to Australia if it looked like he would not be ready to play on the Achilles he tore in January. Making the trip doesn't guarantee he'll be in the lineup, but it is certainly a good sign. Rapoport reports that defensive end Nick Bosa will also travel with the team on Wednesday. Bosa did not practice for much of training camp as he recovers from a torn ACL, but General Manager John Lynch said on Tuesday that he'll be ramping up his work with an eye toward playing in the opener.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders officially name Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback
summary: Cousins will officially begin the season as Las Vegas' QB1 over rookie Fernando Mendoza.
full_text: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak didn't delay naming a QB1 any longer when he walked to the podium for his Wednesday press conference. “Kirk’s going to be the starting quarterback,” Kubiak said to begin his media session. Kubiak added that Cousins did not participate in Wednesday’s practice as a rest day. The Raiders had telegraphed that move throughout the offseason, with the team’s brass repeatedly saying that the idea was to let No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza grow and learn before seeing the field. To that end, Cousins’ rest day was an opportunity for Mendoza to get reps with the first-team offense. “Live reps are the best medicine, so that was very helpful for him,” Kubiak said. While it may seem like Cousins became the starter by default, Kubiak noted how impressed he’s been with the veteran quarterback’s work. “He’s played really good football,” Kubiak said. "I’m really happy with all three of our quarterbacks. Kirk’s had a really good offseason, really good camp. And he’s earned it. “I think [competition] made Kirk better, it made Aiden [O’Connell] better, it made Fernando better. That’s the nature of the position — it’s the most competitive position in the free world. And those guys all improved the roster through their play this offseason.” The Raiders will open the 2026 season against the Dolphins on Sept. 13.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Fernando Mendoza is first No. 1 QB since Baker Mayfield who won't start Week 1
summary: The Raiders naming Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback to open the 2026 season was hardly a surprise.
full_text: The Raiders naming Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback to open the 2026 season was hardly a surprise. While Las Vegas had been projected to draft Fernando Mendoza at No. 1 overall for months, the team's brass had said publicly that its preference was for a rookie quarterback to sit and learn behind a veteran. But now that it's official, Mendoza has become a member of a rare group of quarterbacks from recent years. Mendoza is the first quarterback since Baker Mayfield in 2018 not to start Week 1 after being selected at No. 1 overall. Mayfield's situation was not particularly unusual at the time, as Jared Goff had been through the same thing in 2016. But since then, Kyler Murray (2019), Joe Burrow (2020), Trevor Lawrence (2021), Bryce Young (2023), Caleb Williams (2024), and Cam Ward (2025) have all been their respective club’s Week 1 starter after being selected at No. 1 overall. Since Matthew Stafford was selected at No. 1 overall in 2009, only Goff, Mayfield, and Mendoza have started the season as QB2. Sam Bradford (2010), Cam Newton (2011), Andrew Luck (2012), and Jameis Winston (2015) all started the season opener. Mayfield made it into a game by Week 3, taking over for an injured Tyrod Taylor to lead the Browns to their first victory since 2016 with a 21-17 victory over the Jets. He took over as Cleveland’s starter the following week. It took longer for Goff to ascend to QB1 for the Rams in 2016, as he began his tenure as Los Angeles’ starter in Week 11 with a 14-10 loss to Miami. Mendoza's development will remain a priority for the Raiders, even as he won't receive starters' reps in the regular season. " Early work, late work. More meetings ," Kubiak said on Wednesday. "Plenty of time on the field between drills with [QBs] coach [Mike] Sullivan and [offensive coordinator] coach [Andrew] Janocko. Every player that is not starting the first game, that is helping us on the look team, we’re just trying to find every edge we can find to continue to get him better and his teammates better." Aside from those selected at No. 1 overall, there are plenty of QBs who haven't started early and ended up being successful. "I think there are so many examples both ways," Kubiak said. "I think the most important thing with the quarterback room or any other position is to build competition within the room. That makes players so much better faster than coaching, when they have a guy in front of them that they can look up to and see how something’s done — that’s going to accelerate their growth." We’ll see when Mendoza becomes Las Vegas’ starter. If Cousins plays well and the Raiders are winning, that might not be until 2027. But history suggests Mendoza will be on the field sooner or later as a rookie.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Falcons GM Ian Cunningham: We haven't made QB decision for Week 1 yet
summary: “Ultimately, when the coaches are ready, when the players are ready, we will make that decision,” Cunningham said.
full_text: The Raiders named Kirk Cousins their Week 1 starting quarterback on Wednesday, but his former team has not made the same call. Falcons General Manager Ian Cunningham said "not yet" when asked at a press conference if the team has made a choice between Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa for their game against the Steelers. “Ultimately, when the coaches are ready , when the players are ready, we will make that decision,” Cunningham said. Penix was cleared for football activities after recovering from a torn ACL over a week ago, but did not play in the team's final preseason game. That lack of work was mitigated by Tagovailoa's ups and downs while in game action last month. Tagovailoa also dealt with a back injury early in camp and the extended looks that Jack Strand and Cooper Rush received over the summer resulted in them making the cut to the 53-man roster as well. Cunningham said that having Strand and Rush provides "a little bit of an insurance policy" and that seems wise given the injury histories of the other two quarterbacks. That only leaves the decision of who they'll be insuring on September 13.
author: Josh Alper

title: Robert Saleh on facing Jets: We want to win Week 1, I don't hold grudges
summary: The first game of Robert Saleh's second run as an NFL head coach comes against the team that gave him his first shot at the job.
full_text: The first game of Robert Saleh's second run as an NFL head coach comes against the team that gave him his first shot at the job. Saleh's Titans will host the Jets on September 13 and that will make the first time Saleh has faced the Jets since they fired him early in the 2024 season. During a press conference this week, Saleh said that any of his personal feelings about the way things ended are not going to be on his mind heading into the game. "New York is still a special place ," Saleh said. "Gave me my first opportunity as a head coach. Our desire to win Week 1 and beat the Jets is because it's Week 1 and nothing more. I am forever grateful for all the opportunity that they gave. I don't hold grudges." The Titans have ex-Jets like Jermaine Johnson and John Franklin-Myers on the roster, but Saleh said he's not worried about their ability to "keep the main thing the main thing" when facing their former team. Given how recent seasons have gone for both clubs, the chance to get to 1-0 should offer ample incentive outside of the shared history that will be in the air.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Burrow: Bengals have brought in the right guys to chase goal of winning a Super Bowl
summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow thinks this year's additions on defense make Cincinnati a Super Bowl contender.
full_text: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow thinks this year's additions on defense make Cincinnati a Super Bowl contender. And wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase agrees. Burrow appeared on Chase’s podcast and the two of them discussed how excited they are about this year's defense. "I just want to win this year," Burrow said. "I just want to win. The rest will take care of itself. I think we'll break a bunch of records eventually, but I think we're going to have a really good team that has a chance to win every game that we step foot on the field for. I don't know about you, but I could really feel it in my bones, in my soul in OTAs this year, different from years past. Where we brought in a lot of the right guys, a lot of the right people with the right mindsets to go and chase this goal of winning a Super Bowl and winning as many games as we can and being the best possible team that we can. I felt it from our D-line. I felt it from our defense. Our offense has the same guys as years past, so we felt that for the last couple years, as good as we've been. But these veteran guys that we brought in on defense to be able to help our younger guys." Chase compared this year's Bengals to the 2021 team that lost Super Bowl LVI to the Rams. "I can feel it too. The fact that our defense talks a little trash, I like that," Chase said. "That's what we need. It feels like 2021 all over again, with the guys talking trash, because we had a lot of guys who talked on defense." Burrow repeatedly used the word "excited" when discussing the aggressive move the Bengals' front office made to trade the No. 10 overall pick in the draft to the Giants for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence. "I'm just excited to see Dexter out there. I'm excited to see big Dex out there," Burrow said. "I'm excited to see Dex in uniform. I'm excited to see what he can do for us. That's not something we've done in the past, trade a first-round pick for a player like that. I know the fans were excited, I'm just as excited." Burrow is heading into his seventh year with the Bengals, and they've only made the playoffs twice. He believes this is going to be a big year. If it's not, some big questions are going to be raised about the direction the franchise is heading in.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ravens GM Eric DeCosta: "No indication" how long Rashod Bateman investigation will take
summary: Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman was arrested in June after allegedly breaking the windshield and windows of a car with his child and the child's mother inside, but he was not placed on paid leave by the NFL ahead of the cut to 53 players last weekend.
full_text: '' Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman was arrested in June after allegedly breaking the windshield and windows of a car with his child and the child's mother inside, but he was not placed on paid leave by the NFL ahead of the cut to 53 players last weekend. That leaves Bateman available to the Ravens as the league’s investigation into the matter plays out. On Wednesday, Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta said that he doesn't know the timeline for that process. "It's obviously something that we're very disappointed about that we have to deal with these kind of things ," DeCosta said, via the team's website. "We knew about it right away. We contacted the league right away. The league has been doing an investigation, as well I suppose the authorities. In these matters we just kind of sit back and wait for the league and the authorities to tell us what's going on. I have no indication how long that's going to take." Bateman is coming off of a disappointing 2025 season and the team was banking on a rebound before news of the arrest came to light. If he's not going to be around to provide it, the Ravens will need one or more of their other receivers to step up quickly as a complement to Zay Flowers in the offense.
author: Josh Alper

title: MarShawn Lloyd: I'm ready for anything the Packers give me
summary: The NFL's decision to put running back Josh Jacobs on paid leave has opened a big door for MarShawn Lloyd in Green Bay.
full_text: The NFL's decision to put running back Josh Jacobs on paid leave has opened a big door for MarShawn Lloyd in Green Bay. Lloyd enters the season as the Packers' No. 1 back and it's unclear when Jacobs will be back in the picture for the NFC North team, so the 2024 third-round pick will have a chance to make his case for an even longer run in the job. There hasn't been much evidence of his fitness for the role because injuries have kept him off the field for all but one of the games the Packers have played the last two years, but Lloyd says that he's prepared for all that comes with the job. "I'm ready to play as much as they want me to play," Lloyd said, via the team's website. "I'm excited. It's a dream come true playing for the Packers, so however much carries I get, however much they put me in the game, I'm ready to go." Lloyd will get a chance to prove his point about his readiness and the Packers will need him to be right for their offense to reach a high level out of the gate this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Former NFL CB Alphonso Smith Jr. dies at 40
summary: Alphonso Smith Jr., a former NFL cornerback and the 37th overall pick in the 2009 draft, has died.
full_text: '' Alphonso Smith Jr., a former NFL cornerback and the 37th overall pick in the 2009 draft, has died . He was 40. Via TMZ, Smith died by suicide at a Florida housing community on Wednesday. Before his passing, Smith posted a troubling message on Facebook that made his struggles clear. Drafted by Denver, Smith was traded to the Lions in 2010. He played through 2012, appearing in 42 regular-season games with 11 starts. Smith spent four years at Wake Forest. He was a consensus All-American in 2008. He was inducted into the Wake Forest Sports Hall of Fame in 2022. We extend our condolences to Smith's family, friends, teammates, and coaches.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers DE Sam Okuayinonu not on team flight to Australia, questionable with foot injury
summary: The 49ers are on their way to Australia, but defensive end Sam Okuayinonu is not with them.
full_text: The 49ers are on their way to Australia, but defensive end Sam Okuayinonu is not with them. Shortly before departure, the 49ers announced that Okuayinonu would not be on the team flight to Melbourne for next week's game against the Rams. Okuayinonu has a foot injury. Ordinarily, when a player doesn't make a team flight, that means he's not going to play in the game, but the 49ers are currently classifying Okuayinonu as questionable. Depending on how his foot responds to treatment in the coming days, it's possible that he'll fly to Australia separately. Okuayinonu is an important part of the 49ers' defense: Last year he started 12 games in the regular season and both playoff games. This year he's expected to be a backup but get plenty of snaps in the defensive line rotation, if he's healthy. The 49ers' other players, including tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa, are on the plane. Kittle and Bosa are both rehabbing from injuries and there were concerns that they might not be ready for Week One, but from all indications they're both ready to go against the Rams. The 49ers are flying to Australia a full week early to adjust to the time change and prepare on-site. The Rams are not arriving in Australia until the day before the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lamar Jackson on Ravens' new offense: Defenses aren't prepared for what's in store
summary: "I just can't wait to showcase it," Jackson said. "I don't believe a defense is prepared for what's in store for them."
full_text: '' The Ravens have a new head coach in Jesse Minter, and a new offensive coordinator in Declan Doyle, and quarterback Lamar Jackson says opposing defenses don't know what's going to hit them when the season starts. Jackson told Adam Schein that he's excited to unleash an offense that hasn't been seen before. "I just can't wait to showcase it," Jackson said. "I don't believe a defense is prepared for what's in store for them." Doyle was the Bears' offensive coordinator last year, but in Chicago, head coach Ben Johnson implements the offensive system and calls the plays. Minter has a defensive background, and this is Doyle's first opportunity to run an offense. Jackson said it's an exciting scheme. "It's a lot of moving parts, it's guys flying around," Jackson said. "Everything you need in an offense, play action, dropbacks, run game, everything you need in an offensive system." Jackson didn't play at all in the preseason, so we haven't seen what the new offense looks like in his hands. We'll see it in Indianapolis next Sunday, when the Ravens open the regular season against the Colts.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Hall moves past training camp incident with Quinshon Judkins
summary: Browns defensive tackle Mike Hall and running back Quinshon Judkins had a bit of a dust up in training camp, with the incident apparently causing Hall to miss nearly three weeks of practice.
full_text: Browns defensive tackle Mike Hall and running back Quinshon Judkins had a bit of a dust up in training camp, with the incident apparently causing Hall to miss nearly three weeks of practice. Cameras captured an aggressive block by Judkins on a stumbling Hall. Rumors flew that there was more to it than that; neither the team nor Hall's agents provided answers in response to inquiries from PFT as to whether the rumors had any merit. Regardless, Hall met with reporters on Wednesday and said that the incident is in the past. "Yeah, I mean, we're teammates at the end of the day, so, I mean, it's just a little, you know, mishap on the field," Hall said. "But other than that, you know, he's my brother, at the end of the day, he's still my teammate. So we were getting ready to play Jacksonville and that's what I'm worried about." Hall was asked whether he has spoken to Judkins in an effort to clear the air. "Yeah, like I said before, he's my teammate, so I mean, got to talk to him at some time," Hall said. "But we're getting ready for Jacksonville and that's all I'm worried about." If there was anything more to it, the Browns successfully kept it from getting out. And Hall seems to be over it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Georgia A.G. urges SEC to take significant action against LSU, if it uses former NFL players
summary: On Thursday, the legal battle over the SEC's attempt to ban former NFL players returns to court.
full_text: On Thursday, the legal battle over the SEC's attempt to ban former NFL players returns to court. The situation has stirred very strong feelings. Via Amanda Christovich of Front Office Sports , Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr has urged the SEC to react harshly, if LSU follows through on its plan to play players who hope to return to college after offseason and preseason stints in pro football. “If LSU does in fact roster one or more pro athletes or demonstrates concrete plans to do so, we would strongly encourage the SEC to take all measures available to address this conduct, up to and including suspending and/or removing LSU from the Conference," Carr wrote in a Wednesday letter to the SEC. “College sports are for college athletes only, and we are grateful that the SEC has taken swift action to maintain that standard," Carr added. "However, rules cannot be ignored or twisted to benefit one coach, one institution, or one program, and we refuse to stand by while that happens." Carr's message comes amid reports of internal chatter regarding the potential taking of "extreme measures" against LSU, up to and including expulsion. The issue ultimately will be decided by the courts. For players who are seeking retroactive application of the NCAA's new five-year rule, none of this is their fault. The system has made the mess — and the system keeps making things messier. Possibly with the goal of making it so messy that Congress will clean it all up. Regardless, the stakes are potentially high. And even if the SEC doesn't follow through on threats to remove LSU from the conference, the situation could spawn the kind of hard feelings that may prompt LSU to eventually look elsewhere. Hey, maybe the Big Ten would like to establish a foothold in the Deep South.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Cardinals have "movement" in talks with WR Michael Wilson
summary: The Cardinals and the representation for wide receiver Michael Wilson have negotiated a contract extension for awhile.
full_text: The Cardinals and the representation for wide receiver Michael Wilson have negotiated a contract extension for awhile. Just when it appeared Wilson would enter the season in the final year of his rookie deal, comes word that the sides have made progress. Josh Weinfuss of ESPN reports that there has been "movement" in negotiations and "something could come down in the next day or so." Wilson caught 85 passes for 1,113 yards and seven touchdowns over his first two seasons. The Cardinals wide receiver had 78 receptions for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns last season. Wilson's 593 routes for the season were the third-most in the NFL. He spoke about his contract earlier this offseason, saying "ultimately that stuff is going to take care of itself."
author: Charean Williams

title: Jed York, 49ers' brass are making plans in advance of potential suspension
summary: With 49ers owner Jed York facing a potential suspension as a result of his recent no-contest plea on charges arising from a recent prostitution arrest in Ohio, the powers-that-be are making plans now in the event York isn't available later.
full_text: With 49ers owner Jed York facing a potential suspension as a result of his recent no-contest plea on charges arising from a recent prostitution arrest in Ohio, the powers-that-be are making plans now in the event York isn't available later. "Let's have conversations beforehand so that we know exactly where his wishes are," G.M. John Lynch recently told Tim Kawakami of The TK Show , via 49ersWebZone.com. "And you can't do that for everything because issues come up, like [the] trade deadline. You don't know until you know, and there's so many factors that go into that. But we’ll be prepared for everything because we've put in the work, we've put in the communication beforehand." Even without a suspension, the dynamic has changed. York moved from California to Youngstown. He's not around like he used to be. "If he's not going to be here, Jed, we've got to talk on a regular basis," Lynch said. "He knows that, we know that, we've done that. Now, to the regularity that we normally do, because conversations kind of come up organically, no, but it's probably led to a lot more scheduled meetings where, in the past, it was more organic. "Yesterday morning, [coach] Kyle [Shanahan] and I were on a Zoom with Jed and had a great discussion about a variety of things. And so that communication is critical, I think, to keep everybody on the same page. And Jed, he's been a great sounding board over the years. He trusts us." It's not ideal, and it illustrates the value of having ownership who is in the building every day — but who doesn't excessively meddle in the football operation. It appears that the 49ers had found a sweet spot previously, when York lived and worked in the area. Now, it's different. He's not there on a regular basis. And, if/when he's suspended, Lynch and Shanahan won't have access to York at all (absent burner phones). Whether that makes this better or worse won't be known until it happens. For now, the only certainty is that it is, and will be, different.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brad Holmes: Long-term plans for Sam LaPorta, Brian Branch haven't changed
summary: Brian Branch, Jack Campbell, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta are the four remaining members of the Lions' 2023 draft class still in Detroit.
full_text: Brian Branch, Jack Campbell, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta are the four remaining members of the Lions' 2023 draft class still in Detroit. General Manager Brad Holmes has made clear his desire to keep them "around for a long time." Campbell has signed a four-year, $81 million extension, and Gibbs signed a three-year, $67.5 million extension. The Lions continue to work on deals for LaPorta and Branch. "We still want to keep those guys around; those plans haven’t changed ," Holmes said Wednesday, via Richard Silva of The Detroit News . "There's a couple factors that we've still got to sort through. But in terms of us wanting those guys around? Absolutely. Hopefully, we can get that done." Branch (Achilles) and LaPorta (back) had their 2025 seasons cut short by injury. The defensive back will miss at least the first four games on the reserve/PUP list, while the tight end was fully cleared before training camp. Since taking over in 2021, Holmes has signed nine of his draft picks to multi-year extensions. The Lions have committed more than $1 billion in total contract value for extensions for Jared Goff, Campbell, Gibbs, Derrick Barnes, Kerby Joseph, Aidan Hutchinson, Alim McNeill, Penei Sewell, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.
author: Charean Williams

title: Police make arrest in attempted break-in at Saquon Barkley's home
summary: In July, someone attempted to break in to Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's Philadelphia-area home.
full_text: '' In July, someone attempted to break in to Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's Philadelphia-area home. Police have made an arrest in the case. Via NBC10, authorities have taken 24-year-old Jabir Parker into custody in connection with multiple crimes , including the incident at Barkley's residence. Parker faces charges in connection with two home invasions and the attempted break-in of a third in Montgomery and Chester counties. In the first two, Parker allegedly stole nearly $800,000 worth of jewelry. The attempted break-in is reportedly the one that targeted Barkley's home. Parker was arrested on Tuesday. Authorities used "geo-fencing" to place Parker's phone at each of the three scenes. They also found a recording of Parker's voice on a nanny cam. He was allegedly in contact with a getaway driver at each of the incidents. Parker faces multiple felony counts. He has been jailed on $1 million bail. He's scheduled to appear in court on September 10.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Rodgers is in a four-quarterback room for the first time
summary: The Steelers kept four quarterbacks, declining to expose Will Howard or Drew Allar to the waiver wire.
full_text: '' The Steelers kept four quarterbacks, declining to expose Will Howard or Drew Allar to the waiver wire. Aaron Rodgers, now in his 22nd season, has never experienced a four-quarterback room. "I was thinking it was a possibility , but I don't think I've been on a roster with four quarterbacks," Rodgers said Wednesday, via Brooke Pryor of ESPN. "Obviously when you do that, you're taking away a spot from another place in the team. But at the same time, if the best 53 are going to make it -- and not saying they did -- I think those four are part of the best 53." The four quarterbacks on the active roster, which include veteran Mason Rudolph, also is a first for coach Mike McCarthy. This season is unique for the Steelers with Rodgers in his final season, leaving the team with an uncertain future at the position. Rudolph, Howard and Allar could compete for the job in 2027. "I'm happy for all those guys," Rodgers said. "Obviously looking to the future, those other three guys are going to have a chance when I'm done. And with the growth you saw with Will and obviously with Drew being drafted so far, but also playing well in camp, I'm not surprised at all and I'm excited about those guys' future." The Packers had a plan with 2020 first-round pick Jordan Love sitting behind Rodgers for three seasons before taking the reins. The Jets had no plan behind Rodgers and started Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor and Brady Cook last season before trading for Geno Smith to start this season. The Steelers drafted Howard in the sixth round in 2025 and Allar in the third round in 2026. Rodgers watched Howard and Allar on television from his home as they played the third preseason game against the Bills last weekend. "I thought the entire camp, it was never too big for them," Rodgers said. "They looked really comfortable out there, and I thought they did a lot of good things moving to football, being efficient. "There's learning experiences, but you look at my first preseason, it was not pretty at all. I didn't play good until about the second half of the fourth preseason game. So, they're definitely ahead of where I was at, and mentally, they're grasping the offense and the checks and the cans, and I'm really proud about those guys." Rodgers, drafted in the first round in 2005, went 20-of-37 for 172 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in four games in his first preseason.
author: Charean Williams

title: Eric DeCosta "optimistic" about a deal for Lamar Jackson before March
summary: The Ravens quarterback has two seasons left on his deal, with a cap hit of $84.340 million for 2027.
full_text: '' The Ravens have talked about signing Lamar Jackson to an extension since January. The quarterback, who serves as his own agent, has made it clear he wants a new deal. Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta said Wednesday that he’s “optimistic” about getting a contract extension completed with Jackson before March. "I'm optimistic. I feel good about it," DeCosta repeated, via video from Jamison Hensley of ESPN. DeCosta declined to reveal further detail, citing the unique negotiations with Jackson, who doesn’t have an agent. "I really don't like to get into details," DeCosta said. "I'm not going to talk about it specifically. I think Lamar and I have a pact. As you all know — I've said it probably 50 times — we're not going to talk about business publicly. It's a different type of negotiation, because it's a different type of negotiation with Lamar." Jackson's five-year, $260 million contract has two years remaining, with an $84.340 million cap hit for 2027. The two-time MVP was the highest-paid player in the NFL when he signed his deal in 2023. His annual average of $52 million now ranks 11th in the NFL.
author: Charean Williams

title: RB Jonathon Brooks out of practice with soreness, but Panthers unconcerned
summary: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks remained out of practice on Wednesday, but head coach Dave Canales is unconcerned that Brooks' injury will keep him out of the season opener.
full_text: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks remained out of practice on Wednesday, but head coach Dave Canales is unconcerned that Brooks' injury will keep him out of the season opener. "I'm very optimistic he’ll be available for Week 1," Canales said Wednesday, via ESPN's Mike Kaye. Brooks is dealing with "soreness" Canales revealed Tuesday, but Canales would not specify the location of Brooks' discomfort. Brooks has undergone back-to-back ACL surgeries on his right knee, but he participated in all of training camp and two preseason games this summer. He played 17 snaps in the preseason. He tore his right ACL against the Eagles in December 2024, a season after tearing it while playing for the University of Texas. Brooks missed all of the 2025 season. In the three games he played as a rookie in 2024, Brooks had 12 touches for 45 yards. Brooks is expected to complement Chuba Hubbard, with journeyman AJ Dillon also on the active roster. Trevor Etienne is on injured reserve with a designation to return as he works his way back from an ankle injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on Kyle Van Noy signing: Veteran presence at a premium position
summary: The Vikings picked up one of the top veteran free agents still on the market this week when they signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to their practice squad.
full_text: The Vikings picked up one of the top veteran free agents still on the market this week when they signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to their practice squad. Van Noy isn't coming off his best season, but he had 12.5 sacks for the Ravens in 2024 and he's been a productive player in a number of different defensive schemes over the years. That includes stints playing for Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores in both New England and Miami, which is something General Manager Nolan Teasley called a "component" of why the team was interested in signing him. "Veteran presence at a premium position ," Teasley said at a press conference. "He fits well into the system because of the way that he rushes and the way that we rush. It's really a team component from that standpoint. Then he brings, again, experience and leadership. So, really, really lucky to have a player of his caliber join us." The Vikings were short on experience behind Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel before they moved to add Van Noy. If he can provide production to go with that experience, the move will be an early win in Teasley's tenure.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Bosa says he felt great at practice, expects to play vs. Rams in Australia
summary: "Today was a great day," Bosa said.
full_text: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa returned to practice today , and afterward he said he thinks he'll be good to go for next week's regular-season opener against the Rams in Australia. Bosa said he felt great on the practice field and feels confident that he should be out there for Week One. "Today was a great day," Bosa said. Bosa, who suffered a torn ACL last season and was dealing with pain in his injured knee over the summer, said recovery has been hard but he felt good on the practice field. "It was a long road. There was some stuff I dealt with, with the patellar tendon, and I kind of ramped it up a little too fast with the football a month ago, and they told me to back off, so I've just been trying to get as strong and confident as I can," Bosa said. When healthy, Bosa has been one of the best defensive ends in the NFL. A healthy Bosa could give the 49ers' defense a huge boost against the Rams next Thursday night.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Eric DeCosta: Marlon Humphrey didn't have a great year last year, will have one this year
summary: Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta is expecting a bounce-back year from cornerback Marlon Humphrey.
full_text: '' Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta is expecting a bounce-back year from cornerback Marlon Humphrey. DeCosta noted today that Humphrey is heading into the final year of the five-year, $97 million contract extension he signed in 2020, and the Ravens are expecting Humphrey to play very well in a contract year — after he fell short of expectations last year. "He's in the last year of his deal," DeCosta said. "I would say that he's been a historic Raven in many ways. Multi-time All-Pro, highly competitive Pro Bowler, a leader here. I think he's gonna have a great year. Had a great year a couple years ago. Didn't have his best — he would say, I think he has said, he didn't have a great year last year. I feel confident he's going to rebound and have a great year this year." It's rare in the NFL for a player to actually play out a full five-year contract extension the way Humphrey is going to this year. Humphrey's cap hit this year is more than $26 million, and the Ravens could have saved most of that by cutting him. But DeCosta thinks Humphrey is going to give the Ravens their money's worth this season. "Corners are hard to find, veteran corners who have played at a very high level are hard to find, and we're excited to see him play this year," DeCosta said. If Humphrey can return to All-Pro form, that would mean a lot to the Ravens' defense — and mean a lot for the next contract he'll sign, in 2027.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NBA imposes unprecedented punishment on Clippers for Kawhi Leonard salary-cap circumvention
summary: The L.A.
full_text: The L.A. Clippers were safe. Until they weren't. In one of the most stunning examples of ESPN-on-ESPN crime on record, Shams Charania of ESPN reports that the NBA has levied unprecedented punishment on the L.A. Clippers for salary-cap circumvention in connection with Kawhi Leonard: Five first-round picks and a $30 million fine to owner Steve Ballmer. The NBA also has suspended Ballmer and others. The report comes only a few weeks after ESPN reported that the NBA has no evidence of salary-cap circumvention by the Clippers as to Leonard. The only way to harmonize the two reports is this — the NBA must have found a shitload (technical term) of evidence since August 17. It's the harshest cap penalty ever levied, in any sport. The NFL hasn't issued one in years (except for a " clerical payroll error " by the 49ers in 2024). Most recently, the NFL fined the Broncos a total of $1.918 million and stripped them of two-third round draft picks for a series of salary-cap violations in the 1990s. Before that, the NFL penalized the 49ers for a cap violation in 2000, taking a fifth-round pick in 2001 and a third-round pick in 2002; the league also fined former 49ers (then Browns) president Carmen Policy $400,000, and it fined 49ers vice-president Dwight Clark $200,000. That same year, the Steelers were fined $150,000 for a self-reported salary-cap violation. (Thanks to Team PFT for doing the research on this.) All of those examples pale in comparison to what the NBA has done to the Clippers. And it all traces to the reporting of Pablo Torre, whose efforts secured a Pulitzer Prize for Pablo Torre Finds Out . (After ESPN's August 17 report, some were suggesting it should be rescinded.) That's the true value of modern sports journalism. At a time when most are chasing transactional nuggets that will inevitably be announced (sometimes only minutes after the exclusive report), the best stuff to chase is the stuff they don't want anyone to know about. But for Pablo, the Clippers' infraction never would have been discovered.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys sign QB Joe Milton to practice squad
summary: The Cowboys wanted Joe Milton back on the practice squad, and on Wednesday, they made that happen.
full_text: The Cowboys wanted Joe Milton back on the practice squad, and on Wednesday, they made that happen. The team announced it has signed the quarterback. He will serve as the third quarterback behind Dak Prescott and Sam Howell, who are on the 53-player roster. Howell beat out Milton for the backup job to Prescott. Milton served as the No. 2 last season. In three preseason games, Milton completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He added 12 carries for 14 yards and a rushing touchdown. The Cowboys traded a fifth-round pick to New England for Milton in the 2025 offseason, and he served as Prescott's backup last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Xavier Worthy: When it's time to play, we'll be ready
summary: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid hasn't set anything in stone regarding quarterback Patrick Mahomes's availability for their Monday night game against the Broncos in Week 1, but all indications are that he'll be in the lineup.
full_text: '' Chiefs head coach Andy Reid hasn't set anything in stone regarding quarterback Patrick Mahomes's availability for their Monday night game against the Broncos in Week 1, but all indications are that he'll be in the lineup. Assuming that's the case, the biggest question will be whether his lack of work in the preseason and the long layoff since he tore his ACL last year will have any negative impact on the offense. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy said at a Wednesday press conference that Mahomes's "will and want to" will help ensure that the team doesn't hit any rough patches. “Me and Pat, we've kind of been working this offseason and obviously the timing and stuff you need to work on. . . . I feel like when it's time to play, we'll all be ready,” Worthy said. Reid also had a press conference on Wednesday and said only that Mahomes will keep practicing in the days leading up to the opener. The Chiefs will practice once more this week and then reconvene on Monday to begin their final preparations for Denver.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mason Rudolph is happy Myles Garrett has left the AFC North
summary: Defensive end Myles Garrett and quarterback Mason Rudolph became forever linked in NFL lore on the night of November 14, 2019, when Garrett ripped away Rudolph's helmet and struck him over the head with it.
full_text: Defensive end Myles Garrett and quarterback Mason Rudolph became forever linked in NFL lore on the night of November 14, 2019, when Garrett ripped away Rudolph's helmet and struck him over the head with it. Rudolph, who is still with the Steelers after a one-year break with the Titans, explains that he, and his team, are happy that Garrett has been traded out of the division, from Cleveland to the Rams. Via Steelers Depot , Rudolph said this in an appearance on teammate Cam Heyward's Not Just Football podcast: "As a Pittsburgh Steeler, I'm thrilled that he is no longer in the AFC North. I think [coach] Mike McCarthy's fired up about that, I think [offensive coordinator] Brian Angelichio is fired up about that. I know our tackles are fired up about that. . . . And the top of my frontal lobe , yes." If the season goes as planned, Rudolph wouldn't have been on the field at the same time as Garrett. And Pittsburgh won't see Garrett at all in 2026, unless both teams make it to the Super Bowl. That destination is far more likely for one team than it is for the other.
author: Mike Florio

title: Wilson's 2027 NFL Draft big board: Dante Moore over Arch Manning as eight QBs crack preseason top 50
summary: Despite the hype, this year's QB class may look more like 2025 and 2026 than the 2024 group that produced six top-12 picks
full_text:
The 2027 NFL Draft class enters the season with plenty of hype, especially at quarterback, but the strength of this group goes well beyond the most important position. My preseason top 50 features both bona fide difference-makers and depth to make this class really, really fun.
The 2027 quarterback class has been called loaded for so long that it already feels like settled fact. It isn't. There are recognizable names, former five-star recruits and the physical tools to understand the excitement, but this isn't the 2024 class. Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye, Michael Penix Jr., J.J. McCarthy and Bo Nix were among the first 12 selections that year, and you could argue that all but McCarthy consistently flashed first-round potential during their final college seasons.
Right now, much of the optimism surrounding the 2027 class remains based on what these quarterbacks could become .
Dante Moore and Arch Manning enter the season at Nos. 1 and 4 on my board, and Julian Sayin has already played like a first-rounder in stretches. But meaningful questions remain throughout the class. Manning must make his late-2025 improvement the weekly standard. Sayin needs to become more effective outside structure, and gambling violations cost Brendan Sorsby his final college season.
Jayden Maiava , Darian Mensah , Trinidad Chambliss and CJ Carr all have early-round ability, but each still needs to build on a promising 2025 season. At this point, that makes this group look closer to the 2025 and 2026 classes -- a few strong candidates surrounded by some projections -- than what we saw in 2024.
And quarterback isn't the only reason this class has a chance to be deep. Eight QBs made this initial top 50, but so did seven wide receivers, six edge rushers and five defensive linemen. Jeremiah Smith remains the headliner at receiver because there really isn't much he can't do, but Cam Coleman isn't far behind — and better quarterback play at Texas could unlock an even bigger season (I'm half-joking, half-serious here).
Meanwhile, on the other side of the ball, Colin Simmons and Dylan Stewart enter the season as the two best edge prospects in the country. The interior group may be just as fun; Will Echoles has violent hands, terrific balance and a pass-rush plan from wherever he lines up. Justin Scott may not have the same flashes, but he keeps showing up to tape because he's strong, smart and relentless. That's the larger theme beyond all the quarterback hype: premium-position talent runs throughout this Top 50.
Want more on the 2027 class? Check out our "With the First Pick" summer scouting series for every position: QB ( Nos. 1–5 | Nos. 6–10 ) | RB | WR | TE | OL | DL | EDGE | LB/DB .
Dante Moore is a consistently composed, accurate passer from a clean pocket, one of the best deep-ball passers in college football , and can make something out of nothing without looking to run at the first sign of trouble. The biggest concern is how he responds when defenses disguise pressure and coverages after the snap. He'll need to clean that up, but the arm talent, anticipation and pocket presence give him the highest ceiling in the class.
There really isn't much Jeremiah Smith cannot do. He wins at all three levels, catches everything away from his body and is a problem after the catch because of his strength and contact balance. Maybe he can improve as a blocker, but you're not taking him with a top-5 pick because he's the next coming of Hines Ward.
Me and @RanCarthon talked about our favorite comp for Jeremiah Smith (and it isn't Julio Jones): pic.twitter.com/FDOORWT2Rj
Long, physical and comfortable playing on an island, Leonard Moore has the recovery speed to stay in phase on vertical routes and the instincts to make plays in zone looks. He also tackles like a safety. My comp for him is Patrick Surtain II. And the comp from my co-host on With the First Pick , former Titans GM Ran Carthon? Jalen Ramsey.
Arch Manning 's best stretches show why he has been viewed as a potential top pick. He can throw with anticipation, push the ball downfield and create outside structure, while his size, speed and athleticism make him a legitimate part of the running game. He also became much more comfortable as 2025 progressed. The evaluation remains uneven, however. His feet and internal clock can become hurried, leading to routine misses and poor decisions, and he must prove the late-season improvement represents his new baseline rather than another temporary stretch.
The first-step explosiveness immediately gets your attention, but Colin Simmons is more than a speed rusher. He has the twitch, power and urgency to take over games against SEC competition. The next step is producing that same level of disruption every week.
At 6-foot-5, Dylan Stewart uses his length and overpowering strength to set the edge, then surprises offensive tackles with how suddenly he can collapse the pocket. The physical tools are obvious. Now he needs to turn them into more consistent week-to-week production.
Will Echoles plays with a low center of gravity, violent hands and some of the best balance in the class. He can win with quickness or power and already has a legitimate pass-rush plan. He occasionally gets too high against double teams, but that feels like nitpicking at this point.
At 6-foot-7, Trey'Dez Green is an obvious mismatch who moves like a much smaller receiver. He can win vertically, make defenders miss and contribute as an inline blocker. The concerns are focus drops — fix that and the Kyle Pitts comparisons will get louder and more frequent.
We talked our favorite draft-eligible tight ends heading into the college football season and I asked @RanCarthon a very simple question: Can LSU's Trey'Dez Green be a top-10 pick by the time it's all said and done? pic.twitter.com/8lndtxPWHg
For a tackle with Jordan Seaton 's enormous frame, the movement skills are fun to watch. He anchors against power, mirrors in pass protection and can overwhelm defenders in space. After transferring from Colorado, the remaining question is how quickly everything comes together at LSU.
The fun part with Cam Coleman is watching a big, physical receiver run routes and change direction like a much smaller player. He has terrific contact balance, punishes defensive backs after the catch and has never fumbled in college. More consistent quarterback play could unlock another level. Ran's comp is a fun one: George Pickens.
The five-star tools started turning into consistent production in 2025, when David Stone led SEC defensive tackles in pressures. His size, power and athleticism make him a problem in one-on-one situations. Now, finishing more of those pressures with sacks is the next step.
Few receivers in this class get in and out of breaks as suddenly as Ryan Coleman-Williams , and his track speed allows him to stack cornerbacks down the field. He plays bigger than his thin frame at the catch point, but nine drops and a lack of functional strength cannot be ignored, especially after a down sophomore campaign.
Julian Sayin is an incredibly patient and accurate pocket passer who consistently works through his progressions and gives receivers YAC opportunities with ball placement and timing. He has the touch to make throws at all three levels, and his arm looked better in person at the Ohio State pro day last spring than it sometimes appeared on tape. The questions come when the play moves beyond structure. Sayin can be a half-tick late on intermediate throws, needs to throw with more anticipation and is considerably less comfortable when forced to create on the move.
We're going to be talking a lot about Julian Sayin this fall. He's QB3 on our @NFLDraftCBS summer scouting rankings. One of the biggest obstacles for him will be  overcoming the "Ohio State QB" stigma and how that has translated to the NFL in recent years. https://t.co/epgicpimOP pic.twitter.com/pHmG3aGSEZ
Jadan Baugh looks like a power back until he makes a…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Rams' bold Australia plan could change how NFL teams travel, but the 49ers aren't buying it
summary: Los Angeles is set to arrive Down Under less than 24 hours before kickoff for its Week 1 matchup with San Francisco
full_text:
I don't want to say that we should all start taking international travel tips from the Los Angeles Rams , but we all might want to start taking international travel tips from the Los Angeles Rams.
When it comes to taking an international trip, there's one opponent almost no one has figured out how to beat -- and that's jet lag. A trip to Europe can be absolutely miserable for the first 24 hours because you can't stay awake during the day and can't fall asleep at night, but that's nothing compared to what the Rams and 49ers will deal with this week when they head to Australia.
Both NFL teams are based in the Pacific Time Zone, and they'll travel to Melbourne, which has a 17-hour time difference from California. The game between the 49ers and Rams kicks off at 10:35 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 11, in Australia, which will actually be a Thursday night kickoff (8:35 p.m. ET/5:35 p.m. PT) in the United States.
This could be a game where the team with the better travel plan actually gains an edge, which makes things interesting because the 49ers and Rams have two completely different philosophies for how they're going to handle the trip.
The 49ers, who left for Melbourne on Wednesday , will arrive in Australia a week before kickoff so they can acclimate to the time change. The Rams, well, they'd prefer not to acclimate to anything.
The Rams have put together an unconventional travel plan that NFL teams might look to copy ... but only if it works.
Based on how the Rams have played in international games under Sean McVay, it sure feels like they've cracked the code on international travel, which might explain why McVay has been so secretive about their travel plans to Australia.
Over the past month, McVay has been asked numerous times what the team's itinerary is going to look like, and he always finds a way to duck the question. McVay has offered only one hint about the team's travel plan , and that came back in July when he said the travel schedule for Australia would look similar to what the Rams did for London in 2025.
"It'll be a similar approach, and really the goal for us is to try to keep guys in as close to a rhythm and routine as possible," McVay said. "This is new to us, even going this far."
Last year, it felt like the Rams revolutionized international travel in the NFL when they became the first team ever to arrive in London just one day before their game . They landed in England on a Saturday, and the plan worked because they ended up destroying the Jaguars 35-7 on Sunday.
If the Rams stick to a similar plan, they'll arrive in Australia the day before the game. According to ESPN , the Rams are planning to leave Los Angeles on Wednesday, Sept. 9. When the Rams travel for a normal road game, they like to arrive in the road city the evening before the game, and that appears to be the plan here. If they leave L.A. at 9 a.m. PT, the flight is about 16 hours, so they'd arrive in Melbourne around 6 p.m. on Thursday, just 16.5 hours before kickoff.
Arriving in Australia less than 24 hours before kickoff might sound risky, but it's hard to argue with the Rams' philosophy because it's worked so well. Under McVay, the Rams are 3-0 both straight up and against the spread in international games, outscoring their opponents 92-17.
Some teams will spend the entire week abroad when they play an international game, but the Rams have always kept their trips short since hiring McVay in 2017.
The decision to go with their unprecedented plan for London last year was definitely risky because they were playing a Jaguars team that has played more games in England than anyone. If anyone knows how to handle the travel for a London game, it's the Jags, but the Rams destroyed them anyway.
It worked last year, but London only has an eight-hour time difference from Pacific Time. This is more than double that.
For Los Angeles, there are multiple advantages to showing up in Melbourne the day before the game.
For one, the Rams won't really have to adjust to Australian time. When the game kicks off at 10:35 a.m. in Melbourne, it's going to feel more like 5:35 p.m. PT to them. For the 49ers, who are spending the week in Australia, it's actually going to feel like a 10:35 a.m. start. NFL teams simply aren't accustomed to kicking off that early, but for the Rams, it won't feel like 10:35 a.m. since their bodies will still be on Pacific Time.
The Rams' travel schedule should also set them up well for Week 2. With the 49ers spending the week in Australia, it's going to take them multiple days to readjust to Pacific Time once they return to the United States. That could impact their preparation for Week 2, although that might not matter since San Francisco will face a Miami Dolphins team that's expected to be one of the worst in the NFL.
On the Rams' end, they'll likely get home from the game on Friday night, Sept. 11, and at that point, they won't have to readjust for Week 2. The Rams will keep their body clocks on Pacific Time while they're gone, so they should be in good shape heading into their second game. It also helps that the NFL scheduling office did the Rams a favor for Week 2: They don't play until Monday night, so they'll get an extra day of rest before facing the Giants at SoFi Stadium.
Surviving the flights to and from Australia might end up being one of the biggest challenges for both teams. Back in February, Matthew Stafford half-jokingly said he was worried about how his back would hold up on the long trip.
"Seems like a long flight and I hope my back's not too sore afterwards," Stafford said.
Feel like surviving the flight to Australia is going to be half the battle for the Rams and 49ers. Matthew Stafford back in February, "I hope my back isn't too sore afterwards." #Rams #49ers #Australia pic.twitter.com/vwu6ClqJOF
The 49ers decided not to copy the Rams' travel strategy, mostly because they don't think it will work for a trip this long. They decided not to travel the week of the game because they didn't think it would give them enough time to acclimate to the time difference.
"Usually when you travel with a [16]-hour flight, you don't want to get there the day before because you lose like a whole day there or two and you're just messed up," 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said this offseason.
If Shanahan and the 49ers are right, the Rams' plan to arrive in Melbourne one day before the game could backfire.
"The people we've talked to, you don't feel normal until like the third or fourth day," Shanahan said. "So, we'd like to go out seven days early. But since it takes a day and a half to travel there, we're going to go nine."
The 49ers left for Australia on Wednesday (Sept. 2) and will arrive on Friday (Sept. 4).
According to 49ers general manager John Lynch, the team spoke with multiple experts before deciding to head to Australia a week before the game.
"We didn't really focus on what the Rams were doing," Lynch told KNBR on Tuesday, via 49ers Web Zone . "We focused on doing a study from every angle, from talking to sports science people, from talking to sleep experts."
The NFL probably likes the fact that the 49ers are leaving earlier, especially since it's the league's first game ever in Melbourne. The NFL is trying to grow the game abroad, and having a team spend an entire week in a country that's never hosted a regular-season game certainly helps.
For San Francisco, the decision to leave early was a no-brainer.
"It became clear to us ... that the best logistics for this trip, to put our players in the best position for success, not only down in Australia, but for the rest of the year, [involved leaving early]," Lynch said.
As you can see, these two teams couldn't disagree more on the optimal travel plan for this game. There will probably be a lot of curious teams around the NFL tuning in to see how each club plays, especially early in the game.
The NFL is a copycat league, and if the Rams steamroll the 49ers, there's a good chance you'll start to see other teams…
author: John Breech

title: Renner's 2027 NFL Draft scouting series: Arch Manning tops QB rankings, another passer draws Drake Maye comp
summary: Manning leads a talented quarterback class that also features Drew Mestemaker, Dante Moore and Trinidad Chambliss
full_text:
The 2027 draft class certainly has talent on paper, but will it come to fruition when spring rolls around?
Oregon's Dante Moore returning to school this year when all signs pointed to him being a likely first-round pick may be the start of a trend. All but two quarterbacks in the top 10 below have eligibility remaining beyond this fall. With NIL "salaries" for college quarterbacks sometimes outweighing those of quarterbacks taken outside the top 10 of the NFL Draft , it's no longer an obvious choice to make the jump as soon as possible.
So while there look to be numerous first-rounders on paper right now, a strong class at other positions may convince some quarterback prospects to exhaust their eligibility.
Positional rankings: IOL • S • LB • DT • TE • OT • RB • CB • EDGE • WR • QB
Note: ⭐️ represents each player's 247Sports star rating as a high school recruit
Even if you take away the name and focus on the game, Arch Manning is still the No. 1 prospect in this class. What gets underrated when discussing the Texas quarterback is just how physically gifted he is. Take away the mental side of the game that having the last name Manning might give him a leg up on and focus purely on what Manning can do physically -- and he is still the best in the class. He has a truly freakish combination of speed and arm talent.
Arch Manning reached 21.7 mph, the fastest max speed by a QB this season recorded by us. #ReelSpeed https://t.co/kBJlPEmz28 pic.twitter.com/gZTbAW9ytO
Then there's the pocket presence, eye manipulation and touch throws that only come from being in a quarterback factory from the time he was born. It's truly all there for him to join the ranks of his uncles someday.
Elite Pocket Movement from Arch Manning 🎯 pic.twitter.com/V0YWo2atBM
Now it's just about poise and consistency. It's easy to kill him for some of the ugly tape he put out early last year, but at the same time, he was in a pressure cooker unlike anything a college quarterback had ever experienced.
I want to preface this by saying I know this is incredibly lofty, and I'm not putting this career arc on him at all: When I watched Drew Mestemaker for the first time last year at North Texas , it was the same feeling I had watching Drake Maye in his first year starting at North Carolina .
From the big frame to the effortless arm talent to the legit wheels they keep under wraps until needed, there are a lot of physical similarities. It's the way they play the position, though, that really jumped out to me. Both are feel quarterbacks while still being technically sound. They are not robots playing the position but athletes who find answers that suit each unique situation.
pic.twitter.com/dQ7bX2k3T5
Now, there's a lot less polish on Mestemaker's tape than there was on Maye's, and with good reason. Mestemaker was in his first year as a starter in either college or high school. That inexperience is what makes him so intriguing as a prospect. If he could lead college football in yards per attempt the first time he was given the reins, it's scary to imagine how high his ceiling could be in the coming years.
Dante Moore was stellar in his first action at Oregon, showing a much more polished game in 2025 than he did in his first stint as a starter at UCLA as a freshman in 2023. From an evaluation perspective, I always give an extra bump to prospects who improve even while on the bench. That speaks to work ethic and football character.
Moore isn't all heart, though. The man has one of the cleanest throwing motions you'll ever see from a prospect.
Dante Moore dots pic.twitter.com/R0kk4FbuiL
The biggest thing I want to see Moore improve this fall is his play under pressure. He had a tendency to feel the rush too much last year and let it take him out of his progression. That's a worrisome trend that has to turn around for him to be in play for the No. 1 overall pick.
Trinidad Chambliss was spectacular filling in after starter Austin Simmons went down with an injury. He took Ole Miss and its offense to heights it never reached even with NFL draftees like Jaxson Dart and Matt Corral at the helm. You saw him light up some of the best defenses in college football last year.
pic.twitter.com/9zGG6plbwH
While he may be short, he's not small and doesn't lack arm talent. Physically, he's very similar to Baker Mayfield coming out of Oklahoma . What he'll have to shake is the stigma around short quarterbacks that's getting worse with the complex fronts in the NFL. The inconsistency from former No. 1 overall picks like Mayfield, Kyler Murray and Bryce Young may scare teams away from tabbing Chambliss as a potential franchise quarterback.
With a tight end frame, MLB closer arm strength and MLS midfielder athleticism, LaNorris Sellers is a unique specimen at quarterback. He's going to get every chance to succeed in the NFL because the ceiling is so high if he hits.
LaNorris Sellers looked like QB1 vs. Missouri pic.twitter.com/CaoLelbjil
To date, however, he's been a far more intriguing athlete than true quarterback. His accuracy and sack avoidance have not been at an NFL level. Some of that has come from a rough offensive line in front of him, but a good deal of it is his play style. His 71 sacks taken the past two seasons were the most in the FBS.
A sack rate under 5% is solid by NFL standards (nine starters achieved that last year). Well, Sellers has been almost double that for his career at 9.3%, and it's not as if it gets easier to avoid sacks in the NFL. He has to show improvement in that regard this fall with an upgraded offensive line.
CJ Carr kicks off a trio of quarterbacks in this ranking who I'd call "performance prospects." That means they don't separate themselves physically from the pack in college football, but rather through how they play the position. At a performance position like quarterback, that's not a huge knock. Joe Burrow, after all, was a performance prospect, and no Bengals fan is complaining about that.
What makes Carr a legit prospect is his level of polish after only his true sophomore season and first year as a starter. He plays with a consistent base and has exceptional throwing mechanics. It's no surprise he was the talk of the Manning Passing Academy this summer with his attention to detail.
CJ Carr | QB | Notre Dame | 6-3, 210 Efficient and poised rhythm-based distributor that continued to grow as the season progressed. Polished mechanics and has experience with exhausting progressions. pic.twitter.com/CKPL6DLBFs
To be considered in the first round when you aren't bringing high-end tools to the table, though, you have to be a better decision-maker than Carr was last season, especially when you're playing consistently ahead of the chains with Notre Dame 's elite rushing attack. His 2025 was a very encouraging first go-around, but there's obvious room for development.
In a class that has a lot of accurate quarterbacks, Julian Sayin is at the top of that list. He completed 77% of his passes last year even with a healthy 8.9-yard average depth of target. Obviously, it helps to have two top-five receivers catching passes, but Sayin spins a very catchable ball.
pic.twitter.com/jahPYHxk2x
The worry with Sayin is his athletic limitations. He's not a threat as a runner and doesn't have the arm strength to drive the ball downfield consistently. Then there's his frame, as he's much shorter and thinner than you'd want from a top prospect. Those limitations were on full display in back-to-back losses to end the season, as he took 10 sacks total against Indiana and Miami .
With three more years of eligibility left, Sayin would be wise to use as much time as he needs to develop physically before making the leap to the league.
If I did purely college quarterback rankings, Josh Hoover would be in the top five. There's so much to like about the way he plays the position. He's a loose athlete with off-platform arm talent who can create inside or outside of structure. No returning quarterback in…

title: Jets work out Justin Tucker: Eight-time All Pro accused of sexual misconduct gets look from New York
summary: The 36-year-old former All-Pro was released from the Ravens in 2025 following misconduct allegations and previously had tryouts with the Saints and Colts
full_text:
The New York Jets worked out former star kicker Justin Tucker on Wednesday, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .
Tucker, now 36, last kicked in an NFL game during the 2024 season. On Jan. 30, 2025, six different massage therapists accused Tucker of inappropriate conduct , according to reporting from The Baltimore Banner. Three more therapists came forward Feb. 1, and another seven came forward in mid-February , bringing the total up to 16 massage therapists across eight different spas in the Baltimore area.
Among the complaints, which were from incidents spanning 2012 to 2016, were accusations of Tucker exposing his genitals, brushing two massage therapists with his exposed penis and leaving a wet spot -- believed to be ejaculate -- on a massage table multiple times.
At the time, Tucker responded to the allegations on social media, saying they were "unequivocally false" and "desperate tabloid fodder." The Ravens released Tucker in May 2025, and the NFL suspended him for the first 10 games of the 2025 season for violating the league's personal conduct policy.
Tucker has had tryouts with the Saints and the Colts since but did not make it any further with either club.
Tucker was one of three kickers the Jets hosted, along with Michael Badgley and Josh Karty.
Jason Sanders beat out Cade York in a training camp kicking battle, but Sanders missed a field goal and an extra point in the preseason finale. The Jets claimed Blake Grupe off waivers and currently have Sanders on the practice squad.
Tucker was the league's best kicker for much of the late 2010s and early 2020s, making first- or second-team All-Pro teams every year from 2016-22. His 89.1% career field goal percentage ranks third all-time . He struggled in 2024, though, converting just 22 of 30 field goals. His 73% make rate was second-worst among kickers with at least 30 attempts that season.
