title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 11
summary: It is Day 11 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: IRVING, TX - OCTOBER 27: Emmitt Smith of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates the tying touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks after breaking the NFL all-time rushing record at Texas Stadium in Irving, Texas, 27 October, 2002. Smith eclipsed the mark owned by Walter Payton of the Chicago Bears of 16,726 career yards. (Photo credit should read PAUL K. BUCK/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images It is Day 11 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Get ready folks for Day 11 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a Cowboys loss that still produced one of the greatest individual moments in NFL history. The result went Seattle’s way, but the afternoon belonged to Emmitt Smith. Sunday, October 27, 2002 Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Seattle Seahawks 17, Dallas Cowboys 14 Dallas entered the game 3-4 during a difficult 2002 season, with rookie Chad Hutchinson making his first NFL start after replacing Quincy Carter. Seattle was struggling as well at 1-5, meaning the larger football world was focused less on the matchup itself and more on Emmitt Smith’s chase for the all-time rushing record. Seattle opened the scoring early in the second quarter when Shaun Alexander finished a drive with a two-yard touchdown run. Dallas went into halftime trailing 7-0, with Smith steadily accumulating yards but still short of reaching the rushing record. The Cowboys finally responded immediately after halftime. Hutchinson found former Seahawks receiver Joey Galloway for a 39-yard touchdown, tying the game at 7-7. It was one of Hutchinson’s better moments in his first start and gave Dallas some offensive life. Seattle regained the lead in the fourth quarter when Alexander scored again, this time from five yards out. Dallas was trailing 14-7 when the game’s historic moment finally arrived. Smith needed 10 more yards to pass Walter Payton when he took a handoff and gained 11 yards with 9:10 remaining. The game stopped as Smith celebrated with teammates, former Cowboys and his family after officially becoming the most productive rusher the NFL had ever seen. The moment carried extra emotion because of Smith’s admiration for Payton, who had died in 1999. Smith had spent years openly pursuing the record while maintaining enormous respect for the man whose name had occupied the top spot since 1984. Brad Sham captured the occasion on Cowboys radio with the memorable call, “Move over Sweetness, make a place for Emmitt.” Smith’s day was not finished. Dallas continued the same possession and eventually gave the ball back to him at the goal line, where he scored from one yard out to tie the game at 14-14. It was the 150th rushing touchdown of his NFL career, adding another milestone to an already historic afternoon. Smith ultimately finished with 109 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries. Unfortunately, Dallas could not complete the celebration with a victory. Seattle mounted the final scoring drive and Rian Lindell kicked a 20-yard field goal in the closing seconds, giving the Seahawks a 17-14 lead. The Cowboys were left with a frustrating defeat despite witnessing one of the most significant achievements in franchise history. This game belongs on the countdown because sometimes the result becomes secondary to the history created within it. Smith arrived in Dallas as a first-round pick in 1990, became the engine of three Super Bowl championship teams and eventually ran farther than any player who had come before him. On October 27, 2002, that remarkable journey reached its defining statistical milestone. #Cowboys vs #Seahawks 2002 Emmitt Smith All-Time rushing record Final Score: Seattle Seahawks 17, Dallas Cowboys 14 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/gEno8NI1zt — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 2, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Darren Woodson also became the Cowboys’ all-time leading tackler during the game, although his accomplishment was largely overshadowed by Smith’s NFL record. title: 3 must-win games this Cowboys season
summary: Just under two weeks stand between the Dallas Cowboys and the start of the 2026 regular season. After two disappointing seasons in which they missed the playoffs both years, offseason upgrades have given Dallas high hopes for this upcoming season. If the Cowboys are going to return to the postseason, they’ll need to take care […]
full_text: Just under two weeks stand between the Dallas Cowboys and the start of the 2026 regular season. After two disappointing seasons in which they missed the playoffs both years, offseason upgrades have given Dallas high hopes for this upcoming season. If the Cowboys are going to return to the postseason, they’ll need to take care of business in a few swing games on their difficult regular-season schedule. Here are three must-win games for the Cowboys this upcoming season. 1) Week 2 vs Washington Commanders It may seem a bit crazy to list a Week 2 matchup as a must-win, but this game absolutely falls into that category for the Cowboys. Dallas opens up the season with two divisional matchups in a row, traveling to New York to take on the Giants in Week 1 before returning home to host the Commanders. While Dallas has dominated the rivalry with the Giants in recent memory, this matchup will be much more difficult than years past. New York undoubtedly got better this offseason, and emotions will be running high as John Harbaugh makes his debut as the team’s new head coach. Dallas is favored and very well could win the game, but there is a real possibility they walk out of New York 0-1. If that happens, the Week 2 matchup against the Commanders becomes a clear must-win. Dropping to 0-2 with both losses coming to division opponents could nearly sink your season two weeks in. Even if the Cowboys beat the Giants to kick off the season, this matchup still carries plenty of weight. In that scenario, being able to go to 2-0 with two divisional wins would give Dallas a huge leg up in the division race early on. 2) Week 9 at Indianapolis Colts While a non-conference matchup in Week 9 may not figure to carry much weight, the positioning of this game in Dallas’ schedule makes it very important. After traveling to Green Bay and Philadelphia in back-to-back weeks, Dallas will face the Cardinals, Colts, 49ers, and Titans in weeks eight through eleven. If the Cowboys want any shot at making the playoffs, the games against the Cardinals and Titans should be easy wins. The 49ers will be, without a doubt, the toughest opponent of the four, and with their recent history against San Francisco, it’s easy to see Dallas dropping this one. That leaves the swing game at Indy in Week 9. With such a tough schedule to start the year, the Cowboys may need to make up some ground in their five November games. This matchup against the Colts will likely be the difference between Dallas going 3-1 or 2-2 during the easiest part of their schedule. Indianapolis’ rushing attack will make this a tough game, but if Dallas comes out with a win, it could be huge for their playoff hopes. 3) Week 17 vs New York Giants All things considered, it’s hard to see a world where the Cowboys make the playoffs without winning this Week 17 matchup against the Giants. It’s unclear just where the Giants will be in their re-build at this point in the season. Winning this game could be the deciding factor if Dallas wins the NFC East or makes the postseason in some capacity. If the Cowboys are in the playoff hunt at all, this home matchup against a divisional opponent in the second-to-last week of the regular season will carry tons of weight. Dallas needs to walk away with a win in this matchup no matter what.

title: The reasons these 3 Cowboys players were released
summary: The preseason and training camp are over for the Dallas Cowboys, and with that, the team had to make decisions on their roster. Today we’ll go over some of the more intriguing bubble players that were let go by the Cowboys. QB Joe Milton There may not be a more surprising name on this list […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 22: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys hands the ball off to Jaydon Blue #34 against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of an NFL Preseason 2025 game at AT&T Stadium on August 22, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The preseason and training camp are over for the Dallas Cowboys, and with that, the team had to make decisions on their roster. Today we’ll go over some of the more intriguing bubble players that were let go by the Cowboys. QB Joe Milton There may not be a more surprising name on this list than Joe Milton, who, by all accounts, had a great preseason. This conversation really comes down to what the Cowboys want and think of Milton. Milton finished the preseason completing 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. He showed off the cannon arm people love to bring up, which has made him an intriguing developmental quarterback since entering the NFL, including a 179-yard, two-touchdown performance against Arizona. A game in which he completed a 70-yard touchdown pass to fellow bubble player Jonathan Mingo. JOE MILTON WITH AN ABSOLUTE DIME TD TO JONATHAN MINGO pic.twitter.com/QJpeA45YqD — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) August 23, 2026 So why didn’t that translate into a roster spot? It seems the simplest answer is that the Cowboys apparently valued Sam Howell’s readiness and experience over Milton’s upside, which they still see as a project. Howell has significantly more starting experience, having started all 17 games for Washington in 2023, while Milton has only four regular-season appearances in his career. Milton’s preseason was good enough to make the decision difficult, but the Cowboys ultimately chose the quarterback they appear to trust more if Prescott misses time. That doesn’t mean Milton’s time in Dallas is necessarily over. The Cowboys have expressed interest in bringing him back to the practice squad now that he cleared waivers, although it remains unclear whether Milton would choose to return. He is currently a free agent and can sign with any team. RB Jaydon Blue Blue’s release may have been the most surprising of the Cowboys’ running back decisions. The 2025 fifth-round pick entered camp with legitimate expectations of competing for the RB2 role behind Javonte Williams. His rookie season was underwhelming as he spent most of 2025 on the bench. This preseason, Blue showed flashes of the speed and explosiveness that made him an intriguing prospect. He finished the 2026 preseason with 23 carries for 94 yards, averaging 4.1 yards per carry, while adding two receptions for 15 yards. His best performance came against Arizona, when he ran 15 times for 75 yards. Even if Dallas wasn’t simply looking for somebody to bring consistency and trust to the backfield, Blue did nothing to stand out and separate himself from the pack of running backs the Cowboys had in camp. No touchdowns and not even a single defining moment where Blue could have made the decision to let him go a tougher one. Dallas ultimately chose a different direction, claiming Emari Demercado off waivers from the Chiefs to add another experienced option behind Williams and Malik Davis, who won the RB2 spot. Blue didn’t have to wait long to find his next opportunity. Blue was signed to the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad. Philadelphia now has Blue as a developmental change-of-pace and receiving option behind Saquon Barkley and their running back group. RB Phil Mafah The Cowboys drafted Mafah in the seventh round in 2025, and he entered the 2026 offseason as one of the candidates to take over the No. 2 running back role. His size and physical running style made him an appealing complement to Williams. Mafah finished the preseason with 13 carries for 61 yards and a touchdown, averaging 4.7 yards per carry. His longest run went for 15 yards and a score against the Cardinals when he stayed calm and reversed course on a run that seemed stuffed. Those numbers, and that moment, weren’t bad, but, like Blue, they weren’t enough to separate him from the competition. #Cowboys RB Phil Mafah with an OUTSTANDING run for the touchdown. He wasn’t going to be denied. 🚫 pic.twitter.com/3EYMS6oA7T — Jadon (@thecowboysguru) August 23, 2026 Dallas ultimately kept Malik Davis and added Demercado, while Israel Abanikanda earned a spot on the practice squad. That left Mafah on the outside looking in. The biggest issue may have been that Mafah never completely forced the Cowboys to make room for him. His physical running style was intriguing, but the coaching staff ultimately decided that other backs offered more immediate value and reliability. Mafah was waived by Dallas and, as of now, was not among the Cowboys’ practice squad additions. His next opportunity could come with another team looking for running back depth.

title: Cowboys betting on 2 former Top 100 draft picks to upgrade OT depth
summary: We all know all too well that where a player is ultimately drafted, or not, doesn’t always equate to success. We’ve seen former first-round picks turn out to be absolute busts and undrafted players become superstars with the Dallas Cowboys throughout the history of the organization. We’ve also seen top drafted players who were considered […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 6: Broderick Jones #77 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Acrisure Stadium on October 6, 2024 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images We all know all too well that where a player is ultimately drafted, or not, doesn’t always equate to success. We’ve seen former first-round picks turn out to be absolute busts and undrafted players become superstars with the Dallas Cowboys throughout the history of the organization. We’ve also seen top drafted players who were considered busts arrive in Dallas and completely turn their careers around. The Cowboys are hoping Broderick Jones and Wanya Morris, both former Top 100 draft picks, fall into that category. New Cowboys OTs Broderick Jones (77) and Wanya Morris (64) pic.twitter.com/ZFH8aJer6y — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) September 1, 2026 With concerns about the overall depth at the offensive tackle position, the Cowboys went out and acquired Broderick Jones via trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jones was pick 15 in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft and has started a total of 38 games at both left and right tackle in his three seasons in Pittsburgh. While his career hasn’t panned out the way he had probably hoped so far, the change of scenery hopefully works in his favor much like it did his former Steelers teammate, George Pickens. Jones’ arrival in Dallas puts a target on the back of Dallas’ current starting RT Terence Steele. Both players have been informed the starting RT job is up for grabs and to the victor go the spoils. With the 2026 NFL season opener against the division rival New York Giants quickly approaching, it seems highly unlikely Jones will overtake Steele for the starting job right away. But, considering No. 78’s struggles, it’s not completely out of the question either. While expectations probably aren’t as high for the other OT Dallas signed the practice squad, Wanya Morris is an intriguing prospect as well. A former teammate of LT Tyler Guyton in 2022 at Oklahoma, Morris was overall pick 92 (third round) in the 2023 NFL Draft by the Kansas City Chiefs. He started a total of 15 games in his career with the Chiefs, winning a Super Bowl as a rookie, before being traded a few months ago to the Atlanta Falcons for a sixth-round pick in 2026. Morris’ time on the practice squad is insurance for Dallas’ rookie OT Drew Shelton. Shelton needs more time to develop and doesn’t look pro-ready just yet. Morris acts as a stop-gap if injury and inconsistent play plague the tackle room. The additions of both Broderick Jones and Wanya Morris show the Dallas Cowboys knew of the concerns at the OT position and went out and attempted to address the issue. They are betting they can tap into the talent that made both of these players Top 100 draft picks and reap the rewards. Under the tutelage of Kayton Adams, a highly regarded former OL coach, and Conor Riley, a highly regarded OL coach from the college ranks, big things could be on the horizon and for both of these tackle prospects. Klayton Adams with his newest project: new RT Broderick Jones pic.twitter.com/i9S3h4aD0W — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 31, 2026 Apologies for the poor quality, but here’s Cowboys offensive line coach Conor Riley working with Terence Steele (left) and new Cowboys OT Broderick Jones (right). Jones has been given #77. Brian Schottenheimer said earlier today the two are competing for the starting RT job. pic.twitter.com/azhHc5KLiv — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) August 31, 2026

title: Cowboys news: Why Dallas picked Sam Howell as their QB2
summary: The Dallas Cowboys shocked the NFL world when they decided to release Joe Milton, opting for Sam Howell as their backup to Dak Prescott. Milton shined in the preseason, outperforming most quarterbacks statistically, and showed real growth from year one to two in Dallas’ offense. So why did Dallas opt for Howell over Milton? Brian […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Sam Howell #16 of the Dallas Cowboys walks off the field after the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys shocked the NFL world when they decided to release Joe Milton, opting for Sam Howell as their backup to Dak Prescott. Milton shined in the preseason, outperforming most quarterbacks statistically, and showed real growth from year one to two in Dallas’ offense. So why did Dallas opt for Howell over Milton? Brian Schottenheimer spoke on it today during his press conference, hoping to answer the questions surrounding the move. Here is the latest news around the Dallas Cowboys. Why the Cowboys chose Sam Howell as their backup quarterback – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com At the end of the day, Howell does have more experience than Milton at the NFL level. “I think when we looked at the whole body of work, we just felt like Sam had done a little bit more in terms of executing the offense in certain areas,” Schottenheimer said. “To have Joe Milton back would be incredible, we’ll see what happens with the claims, and then see what he wants to do. We’ve shown that we know how to develop him. I think him being in this system for another year would be amazing, but I also know that he should have choices. And so, we’ll see what happens, but in terms of wanting [Milton] back, absolutely.” Joe Milton Goes Unclaimed On Waivers as Cowboys Eye QB for Practice Squad – Paul Kasabian, Bleacher Report Will the Cowboys sign Milton back to the practice squad, or will he opt to sign elsewhere? Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, both COO/co-owner Stephen Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed significant interest in having the signal-caller back in the mix via the practice squad. Jones made his remarks on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, and Schottenheimer revealed his feelings to reporters during his Tuesday press conference. Emari Demercado returns ‘home’ to Dallas, has reason to be excited with Cowboys – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys newest running back has familiarity with OC Klayton Adams. He will also be placed, once again, under the watchful eye of Klayton Adams, the former Cardinals’ offensive line coach turned Cowboys’ offensive coordinator keenly responsible for crafting the rushing attack for Brian Schottenheimer’s offense. Adams immediately called Demercado once the trade was made official, and the elation is palpable from both player and coach. “Klay’s my guy,” he said of Adams. “As soon as my agent called me and told me it was Dallas, I just immediately thought about Klayton. And then he called me. I’m super excited to work with him again. Michael Irvin giving Dallas Cowboys 10 more years to prove they’re still America’s Team – Brandon Contes, Awful Announcing To Michael Irvin’s point, a whole generation of Cowboys fans have never seen their favorite team in a Championship game. “There’s some credence to what they’re saying,” Irvin admitted. “We cannot remain America’s Team if a whole generation of Americans never see us in a championship game. And in 10 more years – the bible calls 40 years a generation – we would have missed a whole damn generation. So the time is now.” Broderick Jones ‘pumped’ for fresh start with Cowboys, reunion with George Pickens – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The former first-round pick is happy the Cowboys have a plan for him at just right tackle. It goes without saying that Jones, also making it known exactly how thrilled he is to know the Cowboys will set him at right tackle and leave him there, feels exactly the same way as Pickens. “I’m pumped up, man. I’m just pumped up, you know?” he said. “They made it clear where they want me. I just gotta do my part and show up.” Making sense of Cowboys’ surprising roster cuts ahead of 2026 season: Joe Milton, Jaydon Blue and more – Garrett Podell, CBS Sports It feels like Dallas opted for players who can contribute now rather than developmental guys. RBs Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah Now, both are gone for reasons that fall under the umbrella of “consistency” that Schottenheimer stresses his players possess. Both ended up being outworked in training camp and the preseason by undrafted veteran Malik Davis , with Davis showcasing his value not only as a runner but also on special teams. title: Evan Engram offers insight on Jaylen Waddle
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos are gearing up to take on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football to begin the 2026 regular season. Going up against a division rival on the road ups the stakes and makes their Week 1 matchup the most intriguing game of the week. In order to […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 21: Jaylen Waddle (17) of the Denver Broncos takes the field before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 21, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos are gearing up to take on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football to begin the 2026 regular season. Going up against a division rival on the road ups the stakes and makes their Week 1 matchup the most intriguing game of the week. In order to defend their AFC West Crow, it will be critical for the Broncos to take a big leap forward on offense. To help make that happen, they made a huge trade for Jaylen Waddle at the beginning of the offseason. Waddle’s a versatile player who can play inside and out. While his production dipped the last two seasons with the Miami Dolphins, he is still big-time playmaker. Since coming into the league, Waddle has been a tremendous chain mover, deep ball threat, and ranks highly with respect to yards after the catch. He has a chance to be the X-Factor for Denver’s offense this season and help them become a Top 10 unit in the National Football League. Yesterday after practice, tight end Evan Engram offered his thoughts on what Waddle has brought to the team’s dynamic on offense. “It’s a no brainer honestly. His impact that he has and the speed that he has. He’s really smart and savvy too. I think it’s going to help our offense a lot when you have to account for him every time that he is on the field. Sometimes that doesn’t even matter with his talent,” stated Engram. “We’re excited to have him. He’s had a great camp, and he’s meshed really well. He’s a great locker room guy. He’s really funny. He fits really well in with the DNA of our team, and he’s going to be a big part of our offense.” One area Waddle should provide an immediate boost is with respect to catch percentage. He figures to be one of, if not the highest volume target in Denver’s aerial attack. Last season, both Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin had issues in that regard. Both sported sub-65 percent catch rates, which is below average for top passing targets. If Denver wants to compete for a Lombardi Trophy, they have to get better on third downs, and their top pass catchers have to perform much better than that. Over the course of his career, Waddle has been nearly a 70-percent catch-rate player. His efficiency in that respect should give quarterback Bo Nix a top-flight target whether it’s on screens, operating over the middle of the field, or even on deep balls. I’m excited for the potential the Broncos’ offense has this season. In order for them to reach that, they are going to need Waddle to have an immediate impact with the team. I’m confident he will be able to do that and expect him to be a focal point of the team’s offensive gameplan for their Week 1 primetime matchup against the Chiefs. As always, thank you for reading. title: Patrick Surtain II sheds light on Bo Nix; defense’s approach to forcing more turnovers
summary: In less than two weeks, the Denver Broncos will kick off their 2026 regular season in a primetime matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football. The Broncos had a good season in 2025. Alas, the way things ended made last year’s gridiron campaigns one of the greatest ‘What If?’ seasons in franchise […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos warms up prior to a NFL preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images In less than two weeks, the Denver Broncos will kick off their 2026 regular season in a primetime matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football . The Broncos had a good season in 2025. Alas, the way things ended made last year’s gridiron campaigns one of the greatest ‘What If?’ seasons in franchise history. This season, the Broncos are running it back with a roster loaded with continuity. However, they added a few fresh faces on offense at skill positions that hopefully can elevate that unit’s play to the next level. This year’s team might mostly be the same, but their drive and determination to get better has only been amplified over the offseason. How Denver fares this year will hinge a lot on the play of third year quarterback Bo Nix. Despite being the fifth quarterback selected in his draft class, the former Auburn turned Oregon standout has arguably been the best of the bunch. In fact, his total production the past two seasons has ranked near the top of all signal callers in the National Football League. With more than 60 total touchdowns, over 7,700 yards passing, 10 game-winning drives, and 8 fourth quarter comebacks to his name, Nix’s play to date is deserving of praise. And guess what folks? He is going to get better in Year 3. Yesterday after practice, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II talked about Nix’s growth this offseason and why he is poised for a huge season. “I think his cerebral approach to the game is off the charts. I always say he’s so poised, but he’s always had that calm demeanor going into his third year just bringing all the guys together offensively and just being a tremendous leader on the team. He’s got that dog attitude to him, and that’s what you want in a quarterback,” stated Surtain. Though it won’t be all on the shoulders of Nix to get the Broncos back to the promise land. The defense is going to have to step up in a big way and get better in a few facets they struggled with in ‘25. Late last season, Head Coach Sean Payton remarked during numerous press conferences about how the Broncos’ defense needed to step up and force some big turnovers. After hearing that feedback, the defense answered the call. In multiple December games, the Broncos were able to force two turnovers. Against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Round, they were able to amass five—which played a key role in the team’s ability to advance to the AFC Championship game. That was significant progress, but consistency and improvement in that manner is an absolute must. All offseason, finding a way to create more turnovers has been a focal point of Defensive Vance Coordinator, the rest of his staff, and the players. Last year, Denver was in the bottom third of the league with respect to turnover differential— sporting a -3 . Even so, the Broncos still won 14 games last year. A lot of those being one-score games. With a gauntlet of opponents to start the season, they may have a harder time finding such luck [if you want to call it that] this year. The margin for error is seemingly quite a bit thinner this year. Surtain also gave his thoughts on the approach he and his teammates can create more turnovers. “I think it’s all about intention. It’s one thing to think about turnovers, but it’s being intentional at the same time. When you’re going to the ball, you’re intentional about stripping the ball out, about intercepting the ball. I think that’s what matters because we all have the ability. We all could get a takeaway, we all could pick the ball, but it’s all about a mindset going in towards a play and actually capitalizing on those opportunities,” remarked Surtain. There’s no doubt that coming away with more takeaways on a weekly basis will be critical for the Broncos’ chances at defending their AFC West title and making another deep playoff run to chase the franchise’s fourth Lombardi Trophy. The opportunity to put an offseason’s worth of work in focus comes up on September 14th against the Chiefs in primetime. If all goes as planned, Denver will find a way to rattle Patrick Mahomes and make some big plays that can earn them a notch in the win column to start the season.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Garett Bolles speaks on the importance of Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb
summary: One of the major storylines for Broncos Country to keep their eyes on as the regular season transpires is how this year’s offense performs. Over the past few seasons, the Broncos have ranked in the middle of the pack in most aspects on that side of the ball. In order to have a successful season […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 21: Garett Bolles (72) of the Denver Broncos walks to the sideline before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 21, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images One of the major storylines for Broncos Country to keep their eyes on as the regular season transpires is how this year’s offense performs. Over the past few seasons, the Broncos have ranked in the middle of the pack in most aspects on that side of the ball. In order to have a successful season and reach their ultimate goal, taking a big leap forward offensively is an absolute must. A key focus for the team this offseason has been consistency in the run game. To help with that, they added rookie Jonah Coleman in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Over the past few months, the offensive line has worked on their blocking techniques and some new schematic wrinkles. To bolster their passing attack, Denver swung a big trade to bring wide receiver Jaylen Waddle into the fold. Waddle’s talent and big play dynamic should increase the overall efficiency of the offense. Moreover, his presence should help open up things for other players at the position like Courtland Sutton and second-year wideout Pat Bryant—who has been touted as a potential breakout player for the franchise in ‘26. In addition to some new faces on offense, the Mile High City has a new play caller. That’ll be Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb who will be on the sidelines getting the play to Bo Nix and his teammates. Yesterday after practice, longtime left tackle Garett Bolles gave some insight on what Webb means to him and the offense. “I love him. He’s been here for years now, so nothing’s really changed. I think just the relationship status he’s had. He’s played early on, he’s played in this league just a couple years ago, then he just retired. To have him with us and to have that player-style of coaching and knows what we go through and puts us in situations. The feelings he has, the ups and downs of the games that he understands, are tremendous,” stated Bolles. Last season, many fans were perplexed by some of the offensive playcalling. There’s no doubt that Head Coach Sean Payton has a storied career as an offensive mind. During his time in New Orleans, he put together many top offenses with Drew Brees leading the way for the Saints. However, a penchant for screen plays, a lack of dedication to the run, and some puzzling situational down decisions left many fans wanting more. In a surprise move this offseason, Payton announced at the NFL Combine he would be giving up that duty and allow Webb to call the shots. Webb is considered one of the brightest young minds in football. A former third-round pick of the New York Giants in the 2017 NFL Draft, he spent six seasons in the league before retiring in 2022. In 2023, the Broncos hired him to be their quarterbacks coach, which he continued to do alongside his duties as offense’s pass game coordinator in 2025. Ascending to Offensive Coordinator just seemed like a natural progression. In the preseason, we have seen a few glimpses and early visions of things to come. Though there is no doubt a lot of what is in store for the Broncos’ offense this season has been under wraps. That’s what makes the upcoming season a bit more exciting than most. The mystery about what the Broncos’ offense will be and the heights they can reach if they put it all together. Bolles is steadfast in his belief that with Webb leading the way on offense—the best is yet to come. “I’m super grateful for him, and I think offense hasn’t skipped a beat. I think we’re just right where we need to be, and he just brings that juice that we need and that extra juice. To have a guy like that in our corner and to get us in the right situations is tremendous for us.”

title: 2026 Detroit Lions roster comparison: Are they deeper than last year?
summary: One of the biggest problems the Detroit Lions have run into in the past few years is injuries. Detroit has had terrible luck in that department, being one of the most injured teams in football for three years running. While teams can try to do everything within their power to prevent injuries—whether it be practicing […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - NOVEMBER 24: Detroit Lions Center Frank Ragnow (77) lines up over the ball as the offensive line warms up for the NFL football game between the Detroit Lions and the Indianapolis Colts on November 24, 2024, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the biggest problems the Detroit Lions have run into in the past few years is injuries. Detroit has had terrible luck in that department, being one of the most injured teams in football for three years running. While teams can try to do everything within their power to prevent injuries—whether it be practicing habits, nutrition, strength and conditioning—the only tried and true method of protecting yourself against injuries is to build the best depth you can possibly have. The Lions haven’t had horrible depth in previous years, but it can always be improved. So let’s look at Detroit’s depth players only on the 53-man roster and practice squad and see if they’re in a better spot than they were in 2025. Note: Players who started the season on IR/PUP/NFI are not included in the depth, but mentioned, if relevant. Quarterback 2026: Josh Dobbs Luke Altmyer (PS) 2025: Kyle Allen C.J. Beathard Is the depth better? No. I don’t think so. Allen was a better backup than Dobbs, as identified by the fact that Allen went quickly in free agency, while Dobbs was cut this offseason and didn’t sign anywhere until August. That said, I do like the fact that Detroit now has a developmental backup in Luke Altmyer who showed enough to potentially be a long-term reserve option. Running back 2026: Sione Vaki Jacob Saylors Jabari Small (PS*) *For the sake of what I believe will happen, I’m assuming Small is coming back to the practice squad after some roster maneuvering 2025: David Montgomery Craig Reynolds Sione Vaki Jacob Saylors Is the depth better? Without a doubt, it is not. Isiah Pacheco was already a downgrade from Montgomery, and the fact that he will now miss at least the first four games of the season will hurt even more. There is certainly hope that Vaki and Saylors are better than the 2025 versions of themselves with another year in the system, but that improvement won’t make up the gap left by Montgomery’s departure. Wide receiver 2026: Tay Martin Tom Kennedy (PS) Lucky Jackson (PS) Dominic Lovett (PS) 2025: Isaac TeSlaa (started behind Kalif Raymond) Dominic Lovett Ronnie Bell (PS) Tom Kennedy (PS) Jackson Meeks (PS) Is the depth better? Nope. Detroit went very light on wideouts in 2026, and the depth looks worse off for it. Letting Kalif Raymond walk and replacing him with Greg Dortch has already failed, as Dortch didn’t make the roster. The Lions were also victimized by a season-ending injury to rookie receiver Kendrick Law, which would make this look a little better, but as it stands for the 2026 season, the Lions’ depth is clearly not great here. Hopefully the starters stay healthy. Tight end 2026: Brock Wright Tyler Conklin Jackson Meeks Thomas Gordon (PS) 2025: Brock Wright Shane Zylstra Zach Horton (PS) Is the depth better? Yes! The 2026 Lions get their first edge from last year’s squad due almost exclusively to the addition of Conklin. That said, the evolution of Meeks also brings some additional hope. After dealing with serious injuries last year, Detroit is in a much better spot to withstand poor luck this season. Offensive line 2026: OT Larry Borom OT Devin Cochran (PS) T/G Miles Frazier G Ben Bartch C Seth McLaughlin (PS*) G/C Mason Miller (PS) *Again, I’m assuming McLaughlin returns to the practice squad 2025: OT Giovanni Manu OT Dan Skipper (PS) G Kayode Awosika G/C Kingsley Eguakun OL Mason Miller (PS) OL Trystan Colon (PS) OL Michael Niese (PS) Is the depth better? I would say yes, emphatically. Borom is a huge upgrade at OT3 over Manu. Additionally, Bartch is a significant upgrade over Awosika as the first interior offensive lineman in. The Lions’ 2026 depth would look even better if Juice Scruggs was in a reserve position rather than having to be a starter with Cade Mays out. Defensive line 2026: EDGE Derrick Moore EDGE Tyler Lacy EDGE Ahmed Hassanein EDGE Eric O’Neill DT Levi Onwuzurike DT Skyler Gill-Howard DT Mekhi Wingo EDGE Anthony Lucas (PS) DT Chris Smith (PS) DT Ben Stille (PS) DT Tyre West (PS) 2025: EDGE Al-Quadin Muhammad (Davenport wasn’t injured yet) EDGE Tyrus Wheat DT Roy Lopez DL Pat O’Connor DT Mekhi Wingo DT Chris Smith EDGE Isaac Ukwu (PS) EDGE Andre Carter (PS) DT Myles Adams (PS) DT Keith Cooper Jr. (PS) Is the depth better? I think it’s fair to say yes. While the Lions have a bunch of unknowns in Hassanein, Gill-Howard, and O’Neill, they also have significant investments in their reserves, including Derrick Moore (presumably behind DJ Wonnum) and Onwuzuruike. Last year’s squad was devastated with early injuries. Remember there was no Alim McNeill, no Onwuzurike, and soon to be no Marcus Davenport, leaving Detroit perilously thin, especially on the outside. Linebackers 2026 LB Malcolm Rodriguez (assuming Devin White starts for now) LB Jimmy Rolder LB Trevor Nowaske LB Joe Bachie (PS) LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (PS) 2025: LB Grant Stuard LB Trevor Nowaske LB Zach Cunningham LB Anthony Pittman (PS) Is the depth better? Again, I think this is a clear yes. Rodriguez brings a very capable starter (he was injured last year). Nowaske brings the same subpackage potential as last year, but with one more year of experience. Rolder brings some big potential and significant special teams skills. And Bachie and Ogbongbemiga have loads of experience both on defense and special teams. Don’t get me wrong, Stuard and Cunningham were great depth players last year, but Detroit simply has more playable talent in the linebacker room this year. Cornerback 2026: CB Ennis Rakestraw CB/NB Roger McCreary CB/NB Keith Abney CB Khalil Dorsey CB Nick Whiteside (PS) I’m assuming Christian Izien will be the primary nickel, and therefore not “depth” 2025: Rock Ya-Sin Khalil Dorsey Amik Robertson was considered the starting nickel, so is not included among the depth Is the depth better Eh… it’s a toss up. They have more bodies and more competition, but having Ya-Sin as a depth player rather than the starter is a pretty big difference. Eventually, though, the 2025 squad saw its depth decimated. They had to add Whiteside, Arthur Maulet, and Kendall Fuller to the roster to help. The depth wasn’t particularly good last year, and it’s not good this year, either. Take your pick. Safety 2026: Thomas Harper Aamaris Brown (PS) 2025: Avonte Maddox Daniel Thomas Thomas Harper Erick Hallett (PS) Loren Strickland (PS) Is the depth better? Obviously not, but that comparison will obviously change drastically when (if?) Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph return from IR. Having Chuck Clark, Avonte Maddox, and Thomas Harper in depth roles would be a phenomenal safety room, although Detroit may not have the roster spots for all of those players upon Branch’s and Joseph’s return. The 2025 depth was actually pretty impressive, and they ended up needing it. So, I still think the Lions did a pretty good job maintaining that depth in 2026, even if it’s a downgrade from last year. Overall Well, they’ve gotten worse at four positions, gotten better at four positions, and there’s one toss-up. The most positive development is that they are deeper on both sides of the trenches, which could result in this team finding its identity again in 2026. Still, there are serious concerns in Detroit’s secondary, and with the thin reserves at skill positions, time will tell.
author: Jeremy Reisman

full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16), hands the ball to running back Sione Vaki (33) at practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook . For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and this week’s question focuses on which running back will add more offensive snaps to their responsibilities now that Isiah Pacheco has been placed on injured reserve . While general manager Brad Holmes said the team is hopeful to get Pacheco back this season , losing the veteran running back for at least four games could be a big blow to the Lions’ depth. Fortunately, the Lions have improved options at the RB3 and RB4 spots, but they’ll need someone to pick up the slack and take on some RB2 duties. Wth four other running backs on the roster, who will get the majority of Pacheco’s snaps? Jahmyr Gibbs is expected to be the Lions’ “bell cow” running back this season, and he could easily be the first option to absorb more snaps. He is by far the most dynamic option of the group and would give the Lions the best chance to win whenever he is on the field. The Lions will need to give him some rest, but there’s still a world in which he gets even more reps than expected. Sione Vaki has gotten a lot of hate this offseason, but I believe a lot of that is because fans haven’t gotten a chance to see him play running back due to recent injuries and coaches’ decisions to keep him out of preseason games. However, there is one thing that has been crystal clear: ever since Pacheco was injured, it’s been Vaki who has taken the majority, if not all, of the RB2 reps in training camp practices. Jacob Saylors has been a great success story this preseason. With Gibbs, Pacheco, and Vaki not playing in the preseason, Saylors has started each game and performed very well. He’s looked decisive in his reads, strong through the hole, executed subtle moves to shake into space, and had the power to finish runs. His balanced skill set and reliability could elevate him into an RB2 role to start the season. Jabari Small is the wild card of the group because he was on the roster when the poll was published, but was waived during the voting process . There’s still a chance he could be elevated for a game or three, but the chances of him making a significant impact have been dramatically reduced. That said, Small had a very nice training camp, and when on the field (he was injured in all three preseason games), he’s shown well. It’s also worth mentioning that coach Dan Campbell noted that he and Saylors were neck-and-neck in their competition for a depth role all camp. So, in your opinion, which running back will get the majority of Pacheco’s reps? title: Detroit Lions open 2 roster spots by waiving pair of offensive players
summary: The Detroit Lions waived two players on Wednesday, creating two empty roster spots on their 53-man roster. The players they waived were running back Jabari Small and backup center Seth McLaughlin. Why did the Lions waive these two players after they made the initial 53-man roster? One theory could be that they found two new […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Jabari Small (26) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions waived two players on Wednesday, creating two empty roster spots on their 53-man roster. The players they waived were running back Jabari Small and backup center Seth McLaughlin. Why did the Lions waive these two players after they made the initial 53-man roster? One theory could be that they found two new players who are going to replace both on the roster. A more likely theory is that both Small and McLaughlin were battling injuries. And rather than waive/injury them initially and have them revert to the injured reserve, and then have to cut them with an injury settlement, the Lions opted to wait until they got healthy, waive them, and hope to bring them back on the practice squad. If that’s the true theory, then the most likely use of those two roster spots are players who are already on the practice squad. The most obvious choice is Tom Kennedy, who at this point is the presumed punt returner after the surprise release of Greg Dortch. On Wednesday, general manager Brad Holmes hinted that the wide receiver room may not stay at just four players right now. “Four (receivers) is obviously a little bit on the lighter side. That’s just where we’re at right now today, currently,” Holmes said. The other spot is a little tougher to guess. There are some talented defensive players on the Lions’ practice squad, including cornerback Nick Whiteside, and defensive linemen Chris Smith and Ben Stille. Joe Bachie is another candidate, especially if rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder isn’t ready to play in Week 1. If the Lions sign two players from the practice squad to the 53-man roster, it would obviously open spots for Small and McLaughlin to return to the practice squad, but they’ll have to clear waivers first. But let’s also keep open the possibility Detroit has found external help. Since roster cuts, the Lions have added just one player from outside the organization: Elijah Klein, an offensive lineman formerly of the Buccaneers .

title: 2026 Detroit Lions preview: Don’t sleep on these 9 players
summary: Just like that, the 2026 training camp for the Detroit Lions is over with. Despite it likely feeling like somewhat of an eternity for those in the building, it feels like it was just a few days ago that camp got underway in late July. Now we are into September, and the vast majority of […]
full_text: Just like that, the 2026 training camp for the Detroit Lions is over with. Despite it likely feeling like somewhat of an eternity for those in the building, it feels like it was just a few days ago that camp got underway in late July. Now we are into September, and the vast majority of the heavy lifting for the Lions’ roster is in the rearview mirror. As always, there were some tough decisions that had to be made regarding who was going to stick on the active roster and who would not. All in all, I believe they accomplished what Lions coach Dan Campbell set out to do earlier in the spring when he expressed a desire to get back to what they were about back in 2022 and 2023. In short, he wanted to get back to a high level of competition around the roster. They opted not to schedule any joint practices this summer, which is a changeup compared to the last several years. Campbell wanted to get their work in to prepare for the regular season, while also going about it in an intelligent manner. In this episode of, “Before the Roar,” we highlight several Lions players from both sides of the ball that could end up being big contributors at some point during the 2026 season. Players like tight end Jackson Meeks, who made the active roster despite changing positions from wide receiver over the last year. Obviously he isn’t going to be an every-down player, but because of his unique skill set, there can certainly be a role for him depending on the situation or matchup. We also discuss the potential impact of guys like Jacob Saylors, Tom Kennedy, and Jimmy Rolder—among others. You can watch the entire episode below, as well as listen wherever you get your podcasts. Please be sure to like and subscribe to the Pride of Detroit YouTube Channel . Your support helps us reach other Lions fans around the world, and we have big plans for the 2026 regular season.

title: 5 takeaways from Lions GM Brad Holmes post-cuts press conference
summary: Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes and assistant GM Ray Agnew spoke to the media on Wednesday, just days after establishing the team’s 2026 53-man roster. The topics discussed were extremely wide-ranging, so here are the five biggest takeaways from the 25-minute session. Note: I will not be including Holmes’ comments on the Terrion Arnold […]
full_text: Lions GM Brad Holmes speaks to the media on Tuesday, Jan.11, 2022, in Allen Park. Lions | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes and assistant GM Ray Agnew spoke to the media on Wednesday, just days after establishing the team’s 2026 53-man roster. The topics discussed were extremely wide-ranging, so here are the five biggest takeaways from the 25-minute session. Note: I will not be including Holmes’ comments on the Terrion Arnold situation in this article . We have a separate story for those quotes. Wide receiver room could still shift—and why they moved on from Greg Dortch The Lions professed confidence and excitement for how deep the wide receiver room was this offseason, so it was certainly a bit surprising to see them keep just four on the 53-man roster—even if they kept three more on the practice squad. Holmes admitted that’s a little light at the position, but certainly seemed to imply that there could be some shifting at that position coming. “Four is obviously a little bit on the lighter side. That’s just where we’re at right now today, currently,” Holmes said. “But I do like the different flavors in that room.” One guy Holmes was quick to mention was Tom Kennedy, who currently resides on the practice squad. It certainly sounds like he could be in for a 53-man roster elevation, especially as the most likely candidate to be the team’s punt returner. “He’s still part of our 69(-man roster) currently right now. He was able to add some special teams to his repertoire. He kind of did a little bit of that last year. But we all know the versatility that he has,” Holmes said. One player that most expected to land on the 53-man roster was Greg Dortch—who himself said he was surprised by his release. Holmes didn’t provide many details, just noting the competition in the room. “We wanted to add as much competition as possible this whole offseason,” Holmes said. “And, look, when you add as much competition as possible—I thought it was a fierce competition—it adds more discomfort, but it also entails harder decisions. So that’s really all that was.” They still expect Isiah Pacheco to play this year One surprising development from roster cuts was the placing of backup running back Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve , which will hold him out for at least four games. The news comes a week after Dan Campbell revealed Pacheco is dealing with a back injury. Holmes noted that the team is still excited to get him down the line, while not providing any sort of timeline. “He’s steadily feeling better, and he’s doing everything that he can to get back, and we’re excited to get him back when he’s healthy,” Holmes said. When asked if they still expect him back this season, Holmes said yes, but was a little more ambiguous. “Yes, that’s the hope.” Detroit could have placed Pacheco on IR at cutdowns and still would have him available to play after four games. But Holmes said the decision to wait a few days was based on the information they had at the time. “With the information that we had, that’s why we decided to do it when we did it,” he said. Happy with offensive line progress, but LG competition could be ongoing I asked Holmes about the status of the offensive line, which was obviously a priority for this team to figure out prior to the season. Holmes said he was “really excited about that group.” Specifically, he’s been very happy with the progress of rookie right tackle Blake Miller. “He’s gotten better and better and better every single day, which is kinda what we expected,” Holmes said. “So we like where he’s at.” But what was more interesting was what he had to say about the left guard position. Christian Mahogany is the presumed starter based on how things played out in training camp, but it certainly sounds like Ben Bartch could still contend for that starting position. “We all know that Christian Mahogany has starter-level ability. He’s shown that,” Holmes said. “But we wanted to increase the competition there. I know Bartch hasn’t been out there as much, but when he was out there, he was good. He performed well, he just wasn’t able to be out there as much. I would say last week, with the practices, the scrimmage, and that preseason game, he earned his spot.” Sam LaPorta, Brian Branch still part of long-term plans The Lions have previously stated their interest in getting long-term deals done with Sam LaPorta and Brian Branch. However, injuries have complicated matters—whereas Detroit has already extended Jack Campbell and Jahmyr Gibbs, two players drafted the same year. On Wednesday, Holmes reiterated that he wants both LaPorta and Branch to be part of this team’s long-term plans. “We still want to keep those guys around. Those plans haven’t changed,” Holmes said. “There’s a couple factors that we’ve still got to sort through, but in terms of us wanting those guys around, absolutely. Hopefully we can get that done.” Increasing pass rush was a clear priority… and the 1 UDFA Holmes had to have One of the most interesting takeaways from the Lions’ roster cuts was how much they prioritized pass rushers like Skyler Gill-Howard and Mekhi Wingo over space-eating run defenders like Chris Smith. That was clearly not a coincidence. On two separate occasions, Holmes reiterated that it was a specific goal this offseason to improve their pass rush. “There was an emphasis—we wanted to add more juice and more ability to get after the quarterback,” Holmes said. That was reflected at several points in the offseason. The Lions signed DJ Wonnum in free agency, drafted Derrick Moore in the second round of the NFL Draft, and they even made it a priority with their undrafted free agent period. Holmes told a story about Eric O’Neill, the only UDFA that ended up making the 53-man roster. Signing players after the draft can be a bit chaotic, with multiple people within the organization making calls to secure deals. But with O’Neill, he was one of the highest priorities, so Holmes stood right next to director of college scouting Brian Hudspeth while he talked to the defensive end. “When you get into undrafted free agency, there’s always a handful of guys that you want to make sure that you really get for various types of reasons, and Eric O’Neill was one of those guys,” Holmes said. As for what he brings to the Lions, Holmes said it was everything—from athleticism to grit. “He’s a very high-motor player. He’s very instinctive,” Holmes said. “He’s a better athlete than his numbers may indicate, and he gets the most out of himself. He’s just one of those guys that we knew he was going to fit right in here in terms of what we’re about from a culture standpoint, and he took advantage of his opportunities.”
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Lions GM Brad Holmes responds to criticism over handling of Terrion Arnold situation
summary: On Wednesday, Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes spoke to the local media for the first time since the team made the decision to cut Terrion Arnold following his arrest in connection with an incident earlier this year that resulted in eight felony charges. It was an opportunity for Holmes to face some criticism on […]
full_text: Detroit Lions executive vice president and general manager Brad Holmes speaks during media availability at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, Jan. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Wednesday, Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes spoke to the local media for the first time since the team made the decision to cut Terrion Arnold following his arrest in connection with an incident earlier this year that resulted in eight felony charges. It was an opportunity for Holmes to face some criticism on the way the Lions handled Arnold’s situation and built the cornerback room behind him. One of the main lingering questions was why the Lions’ opinion on Arnold shifted throughout the process. When his name was first connected to the incident—before his arrest—the Lions organization backed Arnold and his version of the story. “We got all the information that says he wasn’t involved,” coach Dan Campbell said during the owners’ meeting in April. “That’s what we know, that’s all we know, and that’s really all I can say. As far as I know, it’s not a big deal. It seems like he still wasn’t involved with this.” The Lions then opted to waive him days after his arrest. Holmes didn’t offer many details on what changed, simply noting that when they got more information, they made the move they felt was right. “The whole situation obviously was unfortunate. Look, the kid made a mistake,” Holmes said. “The more information that we got throughout the process, that was the result of us doing what the best and right thing was for the club, which was: move on and move forward.” The other criticism Holmes has faced is not doing enough to plan for this possibility. Detroit knew of the incident back before free agency and the NFL Combine, but it didn’t appear they did much to fortify the outside cornerback room in case Arnold would not be around. They re-signed Rock Ya-Sin and added Roger McCreary in free agency. But the only other notable addition was Keith Abney in the fifth round of the draft, and he’s more of a nickel cornerback. Holmes rejected that criticism in a bit of a contentious back-and-forth with a local reporter. Eventually, he offered the following conclusion, essentially backing the players in the building. “We like the guys we have, we like what we’ve done, and we feel good about what’s in the room,” Holmes said. What’s in the room is starting cornerback D.J. Reed and Ya-Sin. Holmes stressed his confidence in Ya-Sin, who will step in directly for Arnold this year. “Rock played really good football for us last year. He’s had a really good camp this year,” Holmes said. He also went through the depth players and explains why he’s not particularly worried there, either. With former second-round pick Ennis Rakestraw, he acknowledged an up-and-down training camp, but believes there’s been significant progress, too. “His health has been better. He’s had a chance to go out there and compete, and he’s gotten better throughout camp,” Holmes said. “He has a lot of ability. He has a lot of stuff in his body where he can play sticky. I thought his run game stuff improved. He showed that throughout the preseason, as well.” There’s also McCreary, who, while originally tagged as some help in the nickel room, has shown some promise on the outside both prior to his arrival in Detroit and during camp. “He’s played a lot of football, both inside and a little bit outside,” Holmes said. “I would actually argue that some of his stuff that he did on the outside—what he did last year on the outside—may have been a little more appealing than what he did inside at his first stop. Really like him.” While Holmes’ comments didn’t address or respond to every question and criticism around the Arnold situation, they do finally put some closure on an era that both the Lions and their fans are likely ready to move on from.

title: Discussion: What position on the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster is the strongest?
summary: On Tuesday, we discussed the biggest weaknesses on the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster. I picked the cornerback room—and a lot of you agreed—but I thought it was interesting to see how many of you were concerned about the depth at skill position. With the Lions going light on wide receiver, Isiah Pacheco’s injury, and some […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill (54) walks off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Tuesday, we discussed the biggest weaknesses on the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster . I picked the cornerback room—and a lot of you agreed—but I thought it was interesting to see how many of you were concerned about the depth at skill position. With the Lions going light on wide receiver, Isiah Pacheco’s injury , and some questions about the tight end depth (before Tyler Conklin re-signed ), it’s a fair point. Of course, most teams don’t have the crazy amount of top-end talent that the Lions do at the skill positions, either. Speaking of crazy talent, the Lions do have a fair amount of that. So today, let’s focus on the biggest strengths on the Lions’ 53-man roster and practice squad. Today’s Question of the Day is: Where is the Lions’ roster the strongest? My answer: If we’re talking about the best room from top to bottom, I think it would be hard to match the talent in the defensive line room. For one, they have a bunch of high-end talent that this regime has spent top resources on: First-round pick Aidan Hutchinson First-round pick Tyleik Williams Second-round pick Derrick Moore Alim McNeill, given a four-year $97 million contract On top of that, the Lions have plugged resources into the depth. Be it former second-round pick Levi Onwuzurike, free agent signing DJ Wonnum, or late-round picks in Ahmed Hassanein, Mekhi Wingo, and Skyler Gill-Howard, Detroit clearly has wanted to improve that room for years. There are still a lot of questions about the unit. Can McNeill return to pre-ACL surgery form? How will Moore look in his rookie season? Can Williams take a Year 2 jump? Who amongst those late-round picks will emerge as regular contributors? Plugging resources into a position doesn’t necessarily guarantee success, but the early returns from training camp have been promising, and the vision is clear. full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Anthony Campbell #60 of the Green Bay Packers tries to block a pass from Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. title: Packers sign Scott Daly to practice squad as long snapper insurance
summary: Wednesday has brought news of another turn in the Green Bay Packers’ long snapping situation. The Packers, who are heading into the regular season with Matt Orzech as the one long snapper on the 53-man roster, have added another player at the position to ensure that they have some cover if Orzech is not ready […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - DECEMBER 20: Chicago Bears long snapper Scott Daly (46) warms up before a regular season game between the Green Bay Packers and the Chicago Bears on December 20, 2025, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Wednesday has brought news of another turn in the Green Bay Packers’ long snapping situation. The Packers, who are heading into the regular season with Matt Orzech as the one long snapper on the 53-man roster, have added another player at the position to ensure that they have some cover if Orzech is not ready for week one. That player is Scott Daly, a five-year NFL veteran. Matt Schneidman has the report of Daly’s signing to the practice squad, which gives the team 16 players on that unit. Because kicker Lenny Krieg qualifies for the international roster exemption, that means the Packers have one more open slot on the practice squad . Daly’s addition gives the Packers a veteran with plenty of NFL experience — and NFC North experience in particular — if something prevents Orzech from suiting up on Sundays. He was the Detroit Lions’ long snapper from 2021 to 2023 before a knee injury knocked him out for the remainder of that campaign. He then ended up with the Chicago Bears, who employed him as their long snapper for the last two years, before spending the 2026 offseason with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who released him at final cuts on Sunday in favor of incumbent Evan Deckers. While Orzech spent the entirety of training camp on the PUP list, Cal Adomitis took every long snap in practices and games for the Packers. His efforts helped Trey Smack execute a perfect preseason, going 9-for-9 on field goals and 7-for-7 on PATs. Orzech was cleared to return to action on Sunday, the NFL’s final cutdown day, however, ensuring him a place on the 53-man roster. Notably, Adomitis has not yet signed with another team’s practice squad, meaning he would have been eligible to re-sign to Green Bay. However, it appears that the Packers preferred Daly, whose track record is slightly longer than that of Adomitis, to be their insurance policy. It is at least possible that his experience playing at Lambeau Field and Soldier Field over the last five years could play into the decision. Daly was the Bears’ snapper in 2024 when Karl Brooks blocked a last-second field goal attempt to ensure a 20-19 Packers victory at Soldier Field, but he also helped Bears kicker Cairo Santos hit all 8 field goal attempts in the three games between the two teams in the 2025 season.

title: Packers Practice Squad Tracker 2026: Follow all the reports & signings
summary: A 53-man roster isn’t the only thing that NFL teams need to decide on this week. The league’s cutdown deadline from 90 to 53 will come and go on Sunday afternoon, and on Monday it will be time for teams to begin assembling the other major piece of their rosters: the practice squad. Over the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 27: Green Bay player's helmets sit on the turf during an NFL regular season Thanksgiving Day football game between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions on November 27, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A 53-man roster isn’t the only thing that NFL teams need to decide on this week. The league’s cutdown deadline from 90 to 53 will come and go on Sunday afternoon, and on Monday it will be time for teams to begin assembling the other major piece of their rosters: the practice squad. Over the last several years, this component of the roster has expanded greatly in significance. Not long ago, teams could carry a maximum of 8 players on the practice squad, but that number has gradually increased, now doubling to 16 (plus an additional 17th spot if a team signs a player with an international roster exemption). Furthermore, a player can be elevated from the practice squad to the active gameday roster a few times per year without a full promotion to the 53, making the unit a more functional squad of backups and injury replacements. As a result, the NFL has expanded the eligibility rules for practice squads over the years as well. Now, a team can sign players with any level of experience to the squad. At least ten of the 16 spots must be taken up by players with two or fewer years of accrued NFL experience, but that leaves up to six slots that can be filled by players of any experience level. Notably, teams cannot begin signing players to the practice squad until the league’s post-roster cut waivers are processed. That will take place at 12 Noon Central Time on Monday, when waiver claims will be awarded. After that, any players who clear waivers become free agents and are eligible to sign with any team, either to a full 53-man roster spot or to a practice squad. Still, there will be reports during cutdown day on Sunday of players whom the Packers would like to bring back for the practice squad if they do clear waivers. Here, APC will keep track of those reports through Sunday, followed by the actual signings on Monday afternoon. The Green Bay Packers have used the practice squad heavily in recent years as rules have changed, often promoting players to the gameday roster to fill in for injured players or to contribute on special teams. As such, today is an important day for general manager Brian Gutekunst and his staff, who will surely be working hard to bring back several individuals whom the Packers waived as part of Sunday’s cutdown. Building out a deep squad can have a major impact on a team’s ability to withstand challenges over the course of the season, and the quality of players on that unit could be the difference between the Packers going over or under their projected win total of 9.5, which is the current number on FanDuel sportsbook . Keep it here throughout the next day or two as the squad fills out. Reports of Practice Squad Signings The following players have reportedly agreed to sign with the Packers’ practice squad. QB Kedon Slovis (formerly an Arizona Cardinal) RB Pierre Strong Jr. WR Isaiah Neyor WR Chris Hilton Jr. TE Drake Dabney OL Dalton Cooper OL Dillon Wade OL Josh Gesky DL Jaden Crumedy ED Nyjalik Kelly ED Arron Mosby LB Kristian Welch CB Domani Jackson S Murvin Kenion III K Lenny Krieg LS Scott Daly The Packers will have one more practice squad spot available after Daly’s apparent addition on Wednesday. Reported Practice Squad Targets The Packers have released the following players on Sunday, but the reports of their release have indicated that the Packers intend to or are interested in bringing them back for the practice squad if they clear waivers. OL Dylan Barrett RB Jaden Nixon (update: no longer the case ) S Mark Perry (update: no longer the case ) S Jaylin Simpson (update: no longer the case ) Packers players signed to other practice squads WR Will Sheppard, Miami Dolphins OL Darian Kinnard, New York Giants TE Messiah Swinson, Cleveland Browns CB Jaylin Simpson, Miami Dolphins CB Shemar Bartholomew, Tennessee Titans Packers releases who have yet to sign anywhere RB Jaden Nixon RB Damien Martinez WR Kisean Johnson WR Kaden Parther TE McCallan Castles (injury settlement) OL Brant Banks (visited New York Jets) OL Dylan Barrett ED Arden Walker LB TJ Quinn CB MJ Devonshire S Mark Perry LS Cal Adomitis

title: Lambeau Field to host Wisconsin hockey doubleheader in February
summary: The Green Bay Packers have been clear that they intend to find uses for Lambeau Field besides the team’s regularly scheduled home games, and for the first time since the team’s 2026 Shareholders’ Meeting in July, the legendary stadium has added a new event to its calendar. On Wednesday, the Packers announced that Lambeau will […]
full_text: February 11, 2006; Green Bay, WI, USA; Wisconsin Badgers hockey players celebrate in front of fans after defeating the Ohio State Buckeyes 4-2 in the Frozen Tundra Classic at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Photo By Jeff Hanisch-USA TODAY Sports Copyright (c) 2006 Jeff Hanisch | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Green Bay Packers have been clear that they intend to find uses for Lambeau Field besides the team’s regularly scheduled home games, and for the first time since the team’s 2026 Shareholders’ Meeting in July, the legendary stadium has added a new event to its calendar. On Wednesday, the Packers announced that Lambeau will play host to the Frozen Tundra Faceoff, a college hockey doubleheader featuring the Wisconsin Badgers men’s and women’s teams. The event is set to take place on Saturday, February 20th, just six days after Super Bowl LVIII. Game one will feature the defending national champion Wisconsin women’s team against their biggest recent rivals, the Ohio State Buckeyes, followed by the Wisconsin men taking on the University of Michigan. On the women’s side, Wisconsin and Ohio State have dominated the college hockey landscape over the last decade. The two teams have played in the national championship game each of the last four years, with Wisconsin coming out victorious three times (2023, 2025, 2026). The Badgers also have the most national championships in NCAA women’s hockey history with nine. Until recently, Wisconsin’s men’s team was mired in a long run of poor results, but the hiring of head coach Mike Hastings prior to the 2023-24 season gave the program a jolt. The 2025-26 season saw the Badger men win their first NCAA tournament game since 2010, and they eventually matched that team by reaching the national title game, where they fell 2-1 to the University of Denver. Meanwhile, Michigan has remained a consistent powerhouse program, earning the #1 overall seed in last year’s tournament and likewise falling to Denver, but doing so one round earlier in the national semifinals. This will be the second time that Lambeau Field will host a hockey game and the first in 21 years. On February 11, 2006, the Wisconsin men’s team defeated Ohio State 4-2 in front of more than 40,000 fans; the Badgers went on to win the national title that year, their most recent championship on the men’s side. The Packers announced that a ticket presale will take place on Wednesday, September 9, ahead of general public ticket sales beginning on Friday, September 11.

summary: Cutdown weekend is always a time of change and transition. For a few new members of the Green Bay Packers, that was especially true. full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Jonnu Smith #81 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs across the field during an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Houston Texans at Acrisure Stadium on January 12, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cutdown weekend is always a time of change and transition. For a few new members of the Green Bay Packers, that was especially true. Not only did the Packers trim their roster from 90 to the required 53, but they traded for two new players in the process and added a third via free agency. That’s an unusual amount of activity for a time of the year when most teams are focused on workforce reduction. We shouldn’t necessarily make too much of it; the moves for Mark Redman and Kaleb Johnson, in particular, were basically just line jumping. The Packers wanted to make sure they got exactly what they wanted, so they paid a (small) premium to land a pair of players that fit what they were looking for. But for the players involved, it had to be a head-spinning moment. One second you’re wondering if you’ll have a future in the NFL at all, and the next you’re told that not only does another team want you, they’re coming to get you right now. Turn in your playbook and get out of town, but not because you’ve been cut. You’re just on your way to the next job. It’s a rare triple win. The Packers get players they want. The player gets to keep earning money playing football. Their former team gets compensated for someone they were probably going to cut. The only real cost is a weekend of sudden travel arrangements for a couple of abruptly traded players. And also Jonnu Smith, who got to spend all of training camp hanging out at home rather than sweating on a practice field. Some guys have all the luck.
