title: Why this is Houston’s Year
summary: Nearly a decade ago I wrote about the Houston Texans entering the franchise Red Zone, a place where they were in scoring range of Super Bowl Glory. Well, that didn’t work out as expected. Obvs. From Bill O’Brien’s ascension and Jack Easterby’s Grima Wormtonguing to the throw away years of David Culley and Lovie Smith, […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Will Anderson Jr. #51 and Danielle Hunter #55 of the Houston Texans look on from the field after the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at NRG Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nearly a decade ago I wrote about the Houston Texans entering the franchise Red Zone, a place where they were in scoring range of Super Bowl Glory. Well, that didn’t work out as expected. Obvs. From Bill O’Brien’s ascension and Jack Easterby’s Grima Wormtonguing to the throw away years of David Culley and Lovie Smith, things got dark – fast. Then the sun rose over the Gulf and owner Cal McNair made 2 of the best decisions of his life: hiring Nick Caserio as general manager, and signing off on the hiring of Demeco Ryans as head coach. While it took those men a few years to rebuild what BO’B and Grima destroyed, not only did they do it, they assembled arguably the best team the Texans have ever had. "I was at Houston Texans practice the other day and their defense is humming.. The players on every single level of the ball are unbelievable.. It's incredible to watch" ~ @JJWatt #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/57NiMYh437 — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 28, 2026 Lights Out Defense It’s almost unfair how ‘Madden Cheat Code’ good the 2025 Texans defense was. And, as you can expect from Caserio and Ryans, they improved that unit this off-season. Any ranking that doesn’t have the Houston D as #1 heading into the 2026 season is immediately invalid. Will Anderson Jr. Sheldon Rankins Danielle Hunter Azeez Al-Shair Henry To’oTo’o Derek Stingley Jr. Kamari Lassiter Jalen Pitre Callen Bullock Reed Blankenship Let’s face it, every one of those players has a legit chance at landing on a Pro Bowl/All Star roster next January. The upfront pressure is sure to slow opposing running games and speed up opponents passing attacks. And when you do both, 3-and-outs and turnovers become normal expectations. Speaking of turnovers, Sting, Pitre, Bullock and Lassiter each had 4 interceptions last season. And, each of them improved in the off-season. This defense is nothing short of nightmare fuel for opposing offensive coordinators. Improved Offensive Line While rising up from the bottom of the barrel to middle of the pack isn’t all that impressive, the 2025 Texans offense was legitimately only a handful of positive plays away from a far more positive outcome. Take a little pressure off C.J. Stroud in the New England Patriots game and give Houston a +7/Pats -7. Now we’re looking at a 23-21 Houston win, not a 16-28 Pats victory. With the upgraded line, the offense should stay on the field a bit longer, score a bit more and commit a few less turnovers. All that is just enough incremental improvement to swing games in a league where margin of victory is often razor-thin. More Experienced Coaching Every day, Demeco Ryans grows as a NFL coach. And he’s already one of the best in the league. As his growth increases, his game management, situational awareness and motivational skills improve. Offensive coordinator Nick Caley was largely to blame for last year’s offensive offensiveness. However, as the season progressed, so did Caley. Word out of training camp is his communication with quarterback C.J. Stroud has also taken a quantum leap forward. Having them on the same page every moment of the game can only help. The Houston defense was really good under Demeco Ryans, but when he handed the reigns to defensive coordinator Matt Burke, it jumped from really good to great. This year, Burke seems poised to take it from great to historically dominant. Get ready to pencil them in along side the ‘85 Chicago Bears and 2000 Baltimore Ravens. C.J. Stroud Speaking of ranking lists, Houston field general C.J. Stroud has seen his name on an awful lot of “most improved” and “players to watch” lists this offseason. Actually, he probably hasn’t seen his name on those lists simply because he’s been too busy working on becoming the best Houston Texan he can be instead of reading his own press. Players, coaches and reporters have all taken notice. Between the improved offensive line and Stroud’s commitment to living up to his potential, he certainly seems poised to take this team all the way. Rumors swirl this morning that Stroud just turned down a $50 mil/year contract extension, meaning he’s confident in his own ability to earn top QB cash this year. Hopefully that’s a bet worth taking. “A lot of pressure on [C.J. Stroud]. … A lot of money on the line!” —Adam Schefter @AdamSchefter discusses the Texans setting a deadline for Stroud’s contract talks ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/aj3QIuBsNc — Get Up (@GetUpESPN) September 2, 2026 Texans schedule The NFL schedule makers were very kind to the 2026 Houston Texans, slotting them with the 26th overall hardest schedule. Houston’s upcoming opponents had a combined win percentage of .474 in 2025 according to CBS Sports. Looking over the rest of this year, there are a lot of matchups where the opponents simply don’t have enough gas in the tank to throttle past this Texans defense. title: Nick Caserio’s gamble with the Texans’ roster paid off
summary: For some teams, dwindling the 90-man training camp roster down to 53 players is surgical. For the Houston Texans’ General Manager Nick Caserio, it’s an art. It requires multiple strokes, different perspectives, and usage of every brush possible to configure the best roster possible.  It was clear from the outset of this roster cutdown period […]
full_text: For some teams, dwindling the 90-man training camp roster down to 53 players is surgical. For the Houston Texans’ General Manager Nick Caserio, it’s an art. It requires multiple strokes, different perspectives, and usage of every brush possible to configure the best roster possible. It was clear from the outset of this roster cutdown period that the Texans situation was complicated. Injuries across the depth chart made it impossible to predict who would be available to start the season. Combine that with the fact that there were 65 roster-worthy players vying for 53 spots, and there were bound to be eye-opening moved made. When the roster decisions finally came down like a scythe through a field, the Texans made a half dozen surprising cuts. Namely, keeping only three running backs, 12 offensive lineman, and multiple unknown, undrafted rookies was outright malpractice given who they waived. Those decisions led to a tidal wave of criticism and consternation by the fanbase and this writer, who were concerned that the depth of the roster was being mortgaged for unproven commodities. Those roster snubs included rookie WR Lewis Bond, LB Jamal Hill, RB Jawhar Jordan, RB Noah Whittington, CB Alijah Huzzie, and S George Odum. All except Odum were home grown players. However, only the first coat of paint had dried on the Texans roster. By weekend’s end, the Texans not only retained their priority practice squad players, but they also recouped two veterans back onto the 53-man roster. Instead of signing the top 53 players hoping the best that were cut would re-sign on the practice squad, Nick Caserio is played the system. He retained undrafted rookies Sam Hagen and Sebastian Harsh to delay them hitting the waiver wire and being picked up by other teams. Hagen ended up on the team’s injured reserve, which kept him off waivers and in the building. Caserio knew that other teams would rather pass on Houston’s injured player that were released than let go of their own players who they know more about. It’s a knowledge bias more than anything. Caserio used that to his advantage. He released injured players on the open market, waited till the opening bell ended, then once everyone else passed on them, brought those players back. The best example of this occurred with TE Brevin Jordan and DE Dominique Robinson. Both have been out for weeks due to lingering injuries. They were released from their contracts but not signed by another squad. Once the waiver period ended, Houston brought both back on identical contracts and placed Harsh and OT Braden Smith on IR. He kept all four and lost nothing. In the end, the Texans played their cards right. Their practice squad is loaded with viable options and their actual roster is among the most talented in the league. The one position where the Texans didn’t retain all its talent was the wide receiver position. The trio of veteran wide receivers Sterling Shepard, Zay Jones, and Justin Watson, still sit on the open market and could be added either to the 53-man roster at a later date. Houston Texans current Practice Squad : Player Position College Dominic Bailey DT Tennessee Lewis Bond WR Boston College Chris Braswell DE Alabama Ka’ena Decambra C Hawaii Bryce Hall CB Virginia Jamal Hill LB Oregon Alijah Huzzie CB North Carolina Jawhar Jordan RB Louisville Josh Kelly WR Texas Tech Zaire Mitchell-Paden TE Florida Atlantic James Neal III T Iowa State George Odum S Central Arkansas Daniel Sobkowicz WR Illinois State Mitchell Tinsley WR Penn State Noah Whittington RB Oregon There is still inherent risk involved in Caserio’s doings. The practice squad doesn’t fully protect players from being acquired by other franchises. Any team can take a player from another teams’ practice squad, but they must add them to their 53-man roster. That means Lewis Bond, Jawhar Jordan, Noah Whittington, and Alijah Huzzie could easily be stolen out from under Reliant Stadium. While the roster is still quite quirky with five tight ends and three running backs (including one fullback), it’s primed to make a run through the playoffs and lead Houston to another AFC South title.

title: The Colts roster is ready for the season!
summary: After this year’s draft, much of the conversation turned to what else the Colts needed. Unfortunately, it wasn’t asking the question, “What player or positional improvement puts us in the Super Bowl conversation” but more along the lines of “If we don’t get better at this position, how bad are we are going to suck?”. […]
full_text: After this year’s draft, much of the conversation turned to what else the Colts needed. Unfortunately, it wasn’t asking the question, “What player or positional improvement puts us in the Super Bowl conversation” but more along the lines of “If we don’t get better at this position, how bad are we are going to suck?”. Pierce being hurt saw the biggest area of concern shift from an Edge rusher, to a proven, dependable WR. Swing Tackle was a concern, as was a RB2. I was personally concerned with the inexperience at LB. Training camp came and eased some of the RB concerns. McGowan was able to impress in practices and looked good in preseason games as well, while showing he could contribute on STs when called upon. Some didn’t like the choice for #3 RB, but Giddens has also been in the building for two years and must have gained more confidence that Bentley. We saw some good play out of what will be depth or situational Edge play from our later rookies, even if we never got a glimpse of our starters on the outside. We may still be a pass rusher away from being the best that we can be. One unforeseen weakness did appear during camp. We discovered that the loss of Pinter left us without a Center who could handle snapping the football. Many tried, but all looked bad in their efforts. It was glaring enough that we had to make a low level deal to bring in an experienced backup. Given that OL players seldom get through a season unscathed, I feel better about our backup Center, without the benefit of ever seeing him play a snap. As camp ended, we did as hoped by bringing in an experience WR. Some of the shine came off of our new toy, when overserved, crossed paths with a bad choice, to result in an arrest. We may or may not lose Allen for a few games this year, but if it happens, it will likely be manipulated to minimize the loss. This leaves Swing Tackle as the last perceived deficiency to address. Tenuta was not as popular among the coaches as he was with fans, as he didn’t make the 53 man roster and had to clear waivers to remain on the practice squad. It looks like we are more willing to move our Guards to Tackle, than to have a true Swing Tackle. We may have to call that position a weakness. I didn’t see my desire to bring back Pratt materialize as a stabilizing force. With Allen missing time and the overall inexperience of the group, I thought having an adult in the room might be a good idea. There honestly isn’t really a good free agent or cut option out there, but my guess is that we have to live with some mistakes. I’ll will simply be happy if I see a LB (any LB) anywhere near a receiver, 15 yards downfield over the middle. It would also be great if they were battle tested by the stretch run. I expect us to take advantage of our deep defensive backfield and have a lot of two LB or even one LB defensive sets. Overall, I am happy going in. We got through the preseason without losing anyone for extended time. Our QB is legit and we have a lot of weapons for Shane to take advantage of. The offense has experienced success and knows what it looks like. I don’t think it was a fluke and I believe that it is repeatable. On defense, I’m not worried about the starters, but the rotational DLs do give me some concern. If the defense can raise their game in any number of ways, including better pass rush, better middle of the field coverage, or even causing a few more turnovers, I expect the team to be formidable. We get to find out early, with a tough stretch to start the season. Personally, I’m optimistic, but that should not be news to most of you. What do you think of the roster as we approach “For Real” games?

title: Colts Quenton Nelson listed as ‘Name to Watch’ for contract negotiations
summary: According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Indianapolis Colts star offensive guard Quenton Nelson is one of eleven NFL players to watch next offseason if they don’t sign a contract extension beforehand: Quenton Nelson, G, Indianapolis Colts Nelson is a candidate for another extension after maintaining his high level of play at age 30. But talks are stagnant […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - AUGUST 29: Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson (56) during a NFL preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Indianapolis Colts on August 29, 2026 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , Indianapolis Colts star offensive guard Quenton Nelson is one of eleven NFL players to watch next offseason if they don’t sign a contract extension beforehand : Quenton Nelson, G, Indianapolis Colts Nelson is a candidate for another extension after maintaining his high level of play at age 30. But talks are stagnant at the moment. Nelson preferred to sign a deal before training camp, which came and went. Though discussions haven’t intensified, the Colts could pursue a deal before Week 1 kicks off Sept. 13. Nelson will likely need to be the highest-paid interior offensive lineman, which means topping Las Vegas Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum’s three-year, $81 million deal ($27 million per year). The highest-paid guard is the Tennessee Titans’ Peter Skoronski at $25 million annually. A franchise tag for Nelson in 2027 would cost Indianapolis $29 million to $30 million. He is due $18 million in cash this season, the final season of his current deal. No other guards are set to get paid in the short term, clearing the runway for Nelson to do something now — or play it out. That comes with a caveat though. Although Nelson’s preference, as a pending 2027 free agent, was to sign a new mega-contract extension with the Colts before training camp, it’s possible that he and his representation could re-engage such talks with Indianapolis before the NFL’s 2026 regular season kicks off in a week. Even if those talks don’t consummate a new deal, the Colts should reignite those contract discussions when the 2026 regular season ends but before free agency begins for one of their longest tenured players at this point. Regardless of which regime is then in place for the Colts, it would be highly surprising if team ownership doesn’t intervene and make the future Hall of Fame left guard a member of the franchise for at least his remaining prime—if not for his entire career. The 30-year-old longtime Colts standout guard figures to have at least a handful of peak football seasons left, and could command a deal of around $25M per year—making him one of the highest paid guards in football yet again. Per Spotrac, Nelson is projected to command an annual salary of around at $24.1M.

summary: The latest Make sure you download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For more information, click here. The NFL season will start in less than a week. full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs yells before the game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest Make sure you download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For more information, click here . The NFL season will start in less than a week. It’s time to make predictions about how the conference standings and the divisions will play out. The Kansas City Chiefs will battle with the Denver Broncos , Los Angeles Chargers and Las Vegas Raiders in the AFC West, looking to reclaim the throne the team sat on from 2016 – 2024. AFC West Preview: Is Everyone Sleeping on the Chiefs? | The Ringer Reasons for Concern I just gave you the stats on how the offense performed with Mahomes last season. And there’s another important stat: Mahomes often carried the Chiefs with his legs, averaging a career-high 30.1 rushing yards per game. Given that he’s coming off of a knee injury, the scrambling option that got the Chiefs out of a bunch of jams last season might not be as available to him. L’Jarius Sneed is embracing nickel role in his second act on the Chiefs | The Kansas City Star Thus, Kansas City’s best cornerback lineup may include the young corners outside, with Sneed turning back the clock four seasons and manning the nickel. “L.J. and I talked about it a lot, and he’s comfortable in both,” defensive coordinator Spagnuolo said last week. “Here’s his response always when I ask him: ‘Wherever you need me.’ That’s what he says. And so a little bit of it will be determined by who else is out there and what they can do. “L.J. was always a lot like Trent (McDuffie). L.J. was always effective inside. But when we needed him to match up on somebody outside, that kind of dictated it. So that same thing might happen. We’ll see where the other guys are.” Kansas City Chiefs set to host discarded Denver Broncos wide receiver on a tryout, but it’s probably not for the reasons you might think | A to Z Sports Why Broncos WR Cam Ross could make sense on the Chiefs’ practice squad The Chiefs kept Nikko Remigio as their primary punt return specialist, and Brashard Smith as their primary kick return specialist. However, that doesn’t mean that Brett Veach isn’t on the hunt for upgrades. At 5-foot-10 and 190 pounds, Ross is thickly built and durable. He has the build, demeanor, and experience to be valuable as a reserve return specialist. Xavier Worthy’s message about Patrick Mahomes ahead of Chiefs season: ‘He’s back’ | KMBC 9 “He’s back,” Worthy said Wednesday. “It’s not potentially back.” Worthy told reporters Wednesday that he had an up-close look at Mahomes’ work and rehab during the offseason. He said Mahomes’ determination stood out. “His grind, his will and want-to is beyond anybody I’ve ever seen,” Worthy said. “Whatever he puts his mind to, that’s what he’s gonna do. He kind of leads the team in that way.” ‘I Cannot Stand’ — Jason Kelce Expresses Frustration With Chiefs Posting Viral Travis Kelce Practice Clip | Pro Football Sports Network But his brother isn’t a fan. On the latest episode of the “New Heights” podcast, which they host together, the legendary center laid into teams who constantly post clips from practice on the internet. “I liked watching this because you’re my brother and I thought it was great. I cannot stand when teams put these clips online. The Eagles do it too. And I love the Philadelphia Eagles. And I love watching the clips, but they put out a clip of Jalen Carter beating the [expletive] out of a guy who’s trying his hardest to make the team. It’s like, dude, can we just let practice be its own thing? We don’t need to show everything.” Around the NFL New York Jets work out Justin Tucker, two other kickers: Source | The Athletic Tucker is the biggest name the Jets have brought in since the departure of last year’s kicker, Nick Folk, who signed with the Atlanta Falcons in March. Tucker, 36, is an eight-time All-Pro but hasn’t kicked in an NFL game since 2024 and hasn’t been on an NFL roster since the Ravens released him in May 2025. While a free agent last year, Tucker served a 10-game suspension for violations of the NFL’s personal conduct policy after multiple massage therapists accused him of sexually inappropriate behavior. Raiders name Kirk Cousins starting QB for Week 1 over Fernando Mendoza | ESPN Mendoza will be the first quarterback drafted with the first overall pick to not start in Week 1 since Baker Mayfield in 2018. Playing for the Cleveland Browns at the time, Mayfield didn’t start until Week 4 after Tyrod Taylor started the first three games that season. Kubiak didn’t comment on whether there’s an expectation for Mendoza to play this year. “[Cousins] played really good football,” Kubiak said. “I’m happy with all three of our quarterbacks. Kirk’s had a really good offseason, very [training] camp and he’s earned it.” Cowboys’ Stephen Jones on Pickens, Lamb: Not sure any team can pay two WRs at top of market | NFL.com “George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another so it’ll help his market,” Jones said. “And certainly, I know at some point — as does every player in this league — will want to be rewarded with a long-term contract. So that certainly puts pressure on us to have a unique situation there at wide receiver.” There are some instances with teams paying two receivers. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins come to mind. A.J. Brownand DeVonta Smith just were broken up in Philly. However, it’s far from the norm and takes some juggling. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs Mailbag: What is Kansas City’s most concerning position group? EPF Asks Outside of injuries to certain position groups (which are impossible to predict), who do you see as first up for any practice squad elevations? I think the answer is fullback Ben VanSumeren. The Chiefs do not have a fullback on the roster, and none of their four tight ends stand out as strong run game blockers. With a significant portion of the offense being put on Kenneth Walker’s legs, VanSumeren’s skills may be needed. I suspect he chose Kansas City’s practice squad after being sold on the potential to carve out a significant role, despite not attending training camp with the team. title: Andy Reid explains left tackle Josh Simmons’ back ‘flared up’
summary: There are under two weeks to go until the Kansas City Chiefs open the 2026 regular season. Next Thursday, the team will get together for its first game-week practice ahead of “Monday Night Football” against the Denver Broncos in Week 1. The list of lingering training-camp injuries has died down since the Chiefs left St. […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Josh Simmons #71 walks to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There are under two weeks to go until the Kansas City Chiefs open the 2026 regular season. Next Thursday, the team will get together for its first game-week practice ahead of “Monday Night Football” against the Denver Broncos in Week 1. The list of lingering training-camp injuries has died down since the Chiefs left St. Joseph, Missouri, but one is still heavy on the minds of coaches, fans, and all stakeholders. Left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) did not practice on Wednesday, the first practice of the week, and has not participated on the field since the injury was first announced during the last week of practice at Missouri Western State University. Head coach Andy Reid has shared little about the severity of the injury that has kept Simmons off the field for weeks, but on Wednesday he provided the local media pool with more information. “He had the back checked, and there’s a spot in there that flared up,” Reid said. “Now, you have to sit here and wait until that thing calms down. He has been here working out and doing the rehab stuff, so we’ll see where it goes.” When it comes to professional athletes’ backs, it’s uneasy to hear the words ‘flared up’ accompanied by it, especially for offensive linemen. At 31 years old, two years removed from first-team All-Pro honors, former Chiefs right tackle Mitchell Schwartz exited a regular-season game with a back injury, eventually retiring because of it. At 23 years old, there’s reason to believe Simmons is in a positive position to overcome an injury, but back discomfort is especially difficult to leave in the rearview mirror. Especially as an offensive lineman, whose job is to run into 300-pound defensive linemen 50-60 times a game. In Simmons’ absence, it’s unclear to the public how the offensive line will shake out. However, Reid told reporters he had “a pretty good idea” about how a starting five would look without Simmons. “The other guys are doing a nice job in there,” Reid said. “It was good to see our guys roll without Josh in there, but it was also good to see the new guys get practice in too.” The anxiety surrounding Simmons’ availability needs to be held in, waiting until the practice report comes out after next Thursday’s practice. Until then, it’s entirely plausible that a minor back injury is treated with extreme precaution with no game coming up this weekend. Andy Reid said Kingsley Suamataia left midway throught practice with an illness. Chris Jones missed today's practice with a back injury. "He'll be all right," Reid said. — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) September 2, 2026 Other injury updates Left guard Kingsley Suamataia (Illness) left practice early. Defensive tackle Chris Jones (Back) did not practice.

title: Chiefs Mailbag: What is Kansas City’s most concerning position group?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! The Chiefs have now revealed their 53-man roster (and adjusted it further). Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds. Papajazz asks: Is the offensive line still the biggest concern? […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; St. Joseph, MO, USA; Kansas City Chiefs guard Trey Smith (65) walks down the hill to the practice fields during training camp at Missouri Western State University. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The Chiefs have now revealed their 53-man roster (and adjusted it further). Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds. Papajazz asks: Is the offensive line still the biggest concern? I would say yes, although that is probably true for most squads. There are simply not nearly enough NFL-caliber offensive linemen for every squad to stock themselves with nine or ten options. Other than quarterback, offensive line is the position group where you can’t scheme around weakness. Many are concerned about the Chiefs’ linebacker depth, for example, but I expect them to account for light numbers in the middle of their defense with frequent three-safety packages. Little can be done to mitigate blocking woes. The Chiefs clearly were unhappy with what they saw in their own depth options because they traded for two backups last week. With left tackle Josh Simmons dealing with back pain (on top of right guard Trey Smith’s earlier consultation with a hip specialist), the Chiefs needed to know they could at least finish a game with their depth options. In our last mailbag, I predicted the Chiefs could not afford more than one injury along the offensive line and still keep their season afloat. I believe the trade for veteran Josh Ezeudu — who brings experience at both guard and tackle — is sufficient for the team to account for a second starter missing time. If everything works out this season with Simmons and Smith — and Jaylon Moore holds up acceptably at right tackle — there is a world where Patrick Mahomes enjoys best overall offensive line play of his career in 2026. However, the floor could still bottom out very quickly with even below-average injury luck. mainstream asks: Was this offseason the first step of a two year rebuild? I do not think the Chiefs have any eyes on a traditional rebuild process that ends with a mountain of future cap space and a high draft pick. Surprisingly, the same teams seem to begin this path over and over. Tight end Travis Kelce probably isn’t taking a month off of his celebrity lifestyle for his 14th training camp spent in the Missouri Western dorms if he is not convinced the team is all in. Head coach Andy Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo — both closing in on 70 years old — probably have no intention of being part of a slow process. The pair also appears to have no priority in training up young coaches (other than running backs coach DeMarco Murray). Returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy is 57. New wide receiver coach Chad O’Shea is 53. Spagnuolo’s new safeties coach Andre Curtis will turn 50 during the season. This is a staff built to win now. For 2026, Reid and Spags appear to legitimately be embracing radically different paths to hopefully quickly get to the mountain one more time. On offense, the scheme will clearly be more centered on a rushing attack than in the past. On defense, Spagnuolo appears set to rely on rookie pass rusher R Mason Thomas — who falls well outside of the coach’s historical preferences — to bring back Kansas City’s defensive swagger. Whether the moves will pan out remains to be seen. But I don’t get the sense expectations in the building are diminished. TBT asks: Defensive tackle Marcus Harris was constantly in the backfield blowing up plays. Can Bryson Eason do the same consistently or is he only here to plug holes? Harris was dealt one of the toughest breaks in the NFL on Monday after he was waived to add a different option at his position a day after being told he’d made the initial roster. Harris cleared waivers, and on Wednesday morning, the team announced his return to the organization by signing him and releasing defensive tackle Cole Brevard. The initial decision probably came down to girth. Harris had an outstanding preseason and deserved his spot on the roster. Unfortunately, at under 300 pounds, the former Kansas Jayhawk is better suited to a role that the Chiefs have largely spoken for between veteran Chris Jones and rookie Peter Woods. Former first-round pick Felix Anudike-Uzomah also looks like a legitimate option to kick inside on obvious passing downs. Harris showed willingness in run support, but he would likely struggle if asked to step in as a one-tech in relief of Khyiris Tonga. Eason also had a great preseason. At 323 pounds, he better fits the profile of what Kansas City needed to fill out the defensive tackle rotation. Plugging holes will sound like the more boring option, but that is more the job the Chiefs were looking to hire. CoachJA asks: So my UDFA crush, wide receiver Jeff Caldwell is on IR. Gehrig Dieter was on IR in 2019, but he got back onto the practice squad. If Caldwell is a project, won’t they want to do the same with him? He can’t practice with the team while his on IR, but can rehab, correct? Going back to that magical 2019 NFL season (ending with a moment I never thought I would see), Dieter was placed on the Reserve/Injured list on the August 31 cutdown day. He was released from IR with an injury settlement on September 7. Dieter returned to Kansas City’s practice squad in October and later appeared in two games. Caldwell officially reverted to the Chiefs’ IR on August 26 because he was waived with an injury designation. The stated injury of “hyperextended knee” has a wide range of possible scenarios, and the severity of Caldwell’s is completely unknown. Injury settlements are supposed to be negotiated within five days for a player to be released from IR, but it is not always apparent (or seemingly consistent) when the clock for negotiation begins. At any rate, the Chiefs and Caldwell would probably have agreed to a settlement by now if one was coming, though it is possible we could still see the move happen. The Chiefs will probably reach multiple settlements in the coming days after waiving three players on Sunday with injury designation. Injury settlements aren’t really a negotiation over money, since the player is paid his prorated base salary for any weeks covered. The negotiation is in finding common ground on how long recovery from the injury will take. I would say Caldwell is likely to stay on IR at this point and try camp again next year. He wouldn’t be able to practice, but he could benefit from having the team in control of his rehab. Any players who reach an injury settlement to be waived from IR will be ineligible to return to the Chiefs’ active roster or practice squad for the duration of the weeks covered — plus an additional 21 days when they would be free to sign with the 31 other teams. EPF asks Outside of injuries to certain position groups (which are impossible to predict), who do you see as first up for any practice squad elevations? I think the answer is fullback Ben VanSumeren. The Chiefs do not have a fullback on the roster, and none of their four tight ends stand out as strong run game blockers. With a significant portion of the offense being put on Kenneth Walker’s legs, VanSumeren’s skills may be needed. I suspect he chose Kansas City’s practice squad after being sold on the potential to carve out a significant role, despite not attending training camp with the team. That answer probably disappoints fans of wideout Andrew Armstrong. I never saw Armstrong as a likely candidate to be lost on waivers due to age, lack of special teams versatility, and failing to stick on a practice squad in 2025. Wide receivers are also rarely claimed on roster deadline cut waivers because every team has its own project at the position it’s trying to protect. No wideouts were claimed this week as teams tinkered with their…

Rookie Garrett Nussmeier overtook Chris Oladokun on the depth chart, even earning a spot on the 53-man roster because he performed well enough to keep. After Oladokun went unsigned through the initial wave of practice-squad headlines, the veteran also lost his jersey number to his competitor. Kansas City Chiefs Make Telling Change After Chris Oladokun Is Removed From Active Roster | Yahoo! Sports Kansas City waived Oladokun with an injury designation Sunday, opening a spot in a quarterback room that includes Patrick Mahomes, Justin Fields and rookie Garrett Nussmeier. The Chiefs then made another change involving the quarterback: They reassigned his jersey number. Nussmeier, who wore No. 14 throughout training camp and the preseason, has now been given Oladokun’s No. 19. 2026 NFL roster cuts: Biggest moves, more for all 32 teams | ESPN Kansas City Chiefs Biggest move: Although the Chiefs didn’t have any major surprises, the biggest trend with their roster is just how many young players are featured throughout. Because the Chiefs are relying on a large rookie class, the defense has just two veterans who are older than 30: pass rusher Chris Jones (32) and linebacker Drue Tranquill (31). The same is true for the offense, with just Patrick Mahomes (30) and Travis Kelce (36). Much of the season will be about how much the rookies and fellow young players improve. — Nate Taylor Ben VanSumeren might be a bigger part of the Kansas City Chiefs’ plans than a practice squad signing would typically suggest | A to Z Sports The Chiefs want to run the ball more, and VanSumeren could be a part of that plan It’s no secret that the Chiefs want to run the ball more effectively and efficiently during the 2026 NFL season. Training camp showed this with an increased emphasis on the under-center run game with Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson now in the fold. The addition of VanSumeren, with only three running backs on the 53-man roster, is an eyebrow-raiser. He can block from any alignment, not just as a true fullback, but as an H-Back on the wing. Kansas City Chiefs and Hunt Family Foundation Release 2025-2026 Kingdom Impact Report | The Mothership The report features many details and highlights, including: The annual Chiefs Charity Game, the Chiefs annual preseason philanthropic initiative benefiting Kansas City-based charities and nonprofit organizations. The Hunt Family Foundation 50/50 Raffle, the Chiefs gameday fundraising initiative allowing fans the opportunity to purchase raffle tickets with half of the proceeds donated to local charities. The Hunt Family Foundation Spring Grant Cycle, which aids local organizations across the Kansas City region creating a more sustainable environment to live in for children and families. Red Friday tradition, which has benefited Ronald McDonald House Kansas City since 2014. Why Chiefs looked around country — and other sports — to get ideas for new stadium | The Kansas City Star The Tennessee Titans’ new stadium is scheduled to open next season. The Jacksonville Jaguars, Cleveland Browns, Washington Commanders, Denver Broncos and Chicago Bears also are in line for new stadiums — or, in the case of the Jaguars, a major renovation. “With all of these things, you learn from them,” Donovan said. “Some of them are really inspirational. We are in discussions with the Bears, the Broncos, the Commanders and the Browns. “We’ve spent three days at various points over the past two years in Nashville, just looking. I’ve seen that building in various stages and sort of learned what they went through, and tried to learn from mistakes and the things they discovered and incorporated.” Around the NFL Colts GM on NFL players going back to college: ‘That’s the stupidest (thing) I’ve ever heard’ | The Athletic Longtime Clemson coach Dabo Swinney, who faces LSU on Saturday, called this an “embarrassing” moment for college football. “Rarely am I at a loss for words … it’s kind of embarrassing, honestly,” Swinney said Tuesday. “It’s just embarrassing that that’s where we are. I don’t blame the kids, trying to take advantage of the system. But it’s embarrassing for college football. … “It’s a joke. We’ve got zero rules. And when you enforce rules, somebody just goes and finds a judge to say you can’t enforce those rules. Never did I feel like I’d be playing in an era like that, but that’s where we are right now.” Linebacker Kyle Van Noy, 35, signs with Vikings, reports say | ESPN Van Noy, 35, played the last three seasons with the Baltimore Ravens. He followed up a career year in 2024 with one of his most disappointing seasons last year, struggling to generate consistent pressure. He finished last campaign with just two sacks, ending a run of six straight seasons with at least five. But with the Vikings, he should provide some needed depth and experience at the edge rusher position, where Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner give Minnesota a dynamic set of starters but the rest of the depth chart is largely unproven. Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. leaves door open to sit out season opener without new deal | NFL.com With a strong training camp and preseason, Daniels leapfrogged Jake Browning and Connor Bazelak for the No. 2 QB gig behind Baker Mayfield. “I’m proud of Jalon,” Mayfield said from his charitable event at Topgolf on Sunday, via the Tampa Bay Times. “I think he’s shown tremendous steps from the first time I met him in the offseason until now. He played his tail off. Worked hard. Worked on the things the coaches wanted to get done out of him and for him to progress with.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride The 5 biggest takeaways from the Chiefs’ 53-man roster reveal Kansas City currently has 12 rookies on the roster: Yes, over one-fifth of the Chiefs are first-year players, which alludes to the first bullet point of this list. This team isn’t just going young; it’s relying on many first-year players to fill out the team’s depth. It speaks to the exciting, long-term prospects of the roster — but also the fragility of the team in 2026. summary: Good morning, Chargers fans! It is everyone’s expectation that the Chargers offense will be explosive under Mike McDaniel. full_text: San Diego, California - August 05: Quentin Johnston, Ladd McConkey and KeAndre Lambert-Smith of the Los Angeles Chargers look on during an NFL football training camp at Torero Stadium on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) Good morning, Chargers fans! It is everyone’s expectation that the Chargers offense will be explosive under Mike McDaniel. Over the last four seasons in Miami, at least two players recorded 880+ receiving yards apiece. That’s a wild stat and something the Chargers did zero times during the same span. The two wideouts expected to benefit the most from McDaniels’ system are Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston due to their complementary skillsets. And for fun, I peaked at where both players sit in franchise history for career receiving yards and it turns out they are legitimately right next to each other. McConkey is 33rd with 1,938 yards while Johnston is 34th with 1,877. If both of them record at least 813 yards (specifically the total Johnston needs), they’d each end the 2026 season inside the top 20 right in front of receiver Curtis Gonway. The jump from 20th to 18th is roughly 750 yards so it’d take a massive season for either to advance much farther, but it would nonetheless set the two up for another big push up the team annals in 2027. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers scouting department is beginning to pay more attention to the 2027 NFL Draft class as the college football season is now underway. The draft is still eight months away, but the chargers have a general idea of what needs to be improved going into the 2027 season. Bleacher Report conducted a recent mock draft, where the team selected Iowa interior lineman Trevor Lauck. “Lauck is a tough, hard-nosed left tackle with good in-line power as a run blocker, fitting the traditional Iowa archetype,” Bleacher Report scout Brandon Thorn said. “He also appears a bit sawed-off for left tackle consideration at the next level, though he has the movement skills to make it work if needed. Similar to previous Iowa tackles Riley Reiff, Brandon Scherff and Bryan Bulaga, Lauck has the play-strength and competitive toughness to signal a high-floor NFL starter, with the potential to seamlessly slide inside and excel.” The Chargers have Kayode Awosika as the starting left guard on the initial depth chart, suggesting that the team does not have a long-term solution at the position. Putting Lauck in the left guard spot would give the Chargers three first-round picks in the trenches, joining Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt. The Chargers will need to see how they perform in the 2026 season before figuring out which positions to prioritize going into the next draft. Adding a left guard who could be one of the better interior lineman prospects going into next year is definitely a smart choice for a team like the Chargers.

title: What happened to past DPOY winners who changed teams?
summary: This offseason, Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett became the third player to win Defensive Player of the Year and play the next season with a new team. Deion Sanders and Dana Stubblefield were the other two, but both moved as free agents, rather than via trade like Garrett, according to ESPN. Garrett is coming […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 26: Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams rushes the edge during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 26, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images This offseason, Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett became the third player to win Defensive Player of the Year and play the next season with a new team. Deion Sanders and Dana Stubblefield were the other two, but both moved as free agents, rather than via trade like Garrett, according to ESPN . Garrett is coming off an NFL record season and faces heavy pressure to pan out in his new surroundings, as Sanders and Stubblefield once did. Both players couldn’t exactly recapture the magic of their stellar DPOY seasons, though one was noticeably more successful than the other. What does that mean for Garrett? Maybe nothing, but it’s still worth examining as he follows in their footsteps. Deion Sanders (1994) DPOY Season: Surprisingly, Sanders finished as Defensive Player of the Year once in his career, even though he set the gold standard for defenders. His 1994 campaign is the stuff of legends, as he finished with six interceptions, which he returned for a league-high 303 yards. A third of his nine career pick-sixes came in this season alone, including a 93-yard score. Sanders finished third in MVP voting and was the third 49ers player in line for the award that year alongside Steve Young (who won it) and Jerry Rice. The trio led the Niners to victory in a 49-26 demolition of the hapless Chargers. San Francisco couldn’t have asked for a better defensive season if they tried. Season after: From 1992-98, Sanders was named a first-team All-Pro in six of those seven seasons. The 1995 season, after winning DPOY, was the only time he didn’t receive All-Pro recognition or even a Pro Bowl nod in that span. He did see a dip in his numbers from the year before. Sanders finished with a then-career-low 26 combined tackles and two interceptions in nine games . Well, none of that seemed to matter as Sanders won his second straight Super Bowl title, this time with the Dallas Cowboys. Though Sanders wasn’t playing for the 49ers, he left his heart (and cleats) in San Francisco. That’s right, he was traded to the Giants in July 1995 and played in 52 games with the team. Let’s see Garrett do that! #49ers CB Deion Sanders (1994) didn't just play for one professional San Francisco team in his career. He was with #SFGiants in 1995. In 52 games with the Giants that season, he slashed .285/.346/.444 while hitting 9 2B, 5 3B, 5 HR & 18 RBI in 214 ABs. #Random49ers #MLB pic.twitter.com/7ergdYI2pA — #Random49ers (@Random49ers) May 8, 2020 While Sanders didn’t fare as well statistically with his new team after winning DPOY, he still helped the Cowboys hoist the Lombardi Trophy. The Rams would be fortunate if Garrett followed in that same path this season, even if he sees a slight drop in his sack totals. Should LA come away with another title, would that really matter? Dana Stubblefield (1997) DPOY Season: Stubblefield rattled opposing offenses in 1997 with the 49ers. He ended the year with a career-high 15 sacks, 14 more than the previous season! It also marked the second time he finished with double-digit sacks after his 1993 Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign. Stubblefield earned Pro Bowl honors for the third time in his career and was named a first-team All-Pro. He received 28 votes for DPOY, easily topping Hall of Famer Bruce Smith, who got a mere six votes after a 14-sack season with the Bills. Additionally, Stubblefield was tied with Steelers legend Jerome Bettis for fifth in MVP voting that season . The award went to Brett Favre and Barry Sanders, which is crazy to think that MVP honors used to go to non-quarterbacks. Either way, the sky was seemingly the limit for the star pass rusher, but he failed to capitalize. Season after: After arguably the greatest season of his career to date, Stubblefield became an unrestricted free agent. He ultimately bolted for Washington and never again found the success he had in the Bay Area. In 1998, Stubblefield finished with 1.5 sacks in seven games. Stubblefield had just 14 sacks in the final six seasons of his career during stops with Washington, a second stint with San Francisco and Oakland. The ‘97 campaign was certainly an outlier for his career.

title: Ty Simpson preseason film breakdown
summary: Ty Simpson was arguably the NFL’s biggest star of the preseason because he’s a quarterback, he’s a first-round pick, he’s a rookie, and he didn’t get as many bad results as Fernando Mendoza. In fact, Simpson’s biggest negatives on the box score were merely the incompletions, of which there were relatively few. The film will […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Ty Simpson #15 passes a touchdown to Brennan Presley #81 of the Los Angeles Rams tduring the first half of a preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ty Simpson was arguably the NFL’s biggest star of the preseason because he’s a quarterback, he’s a first-round pick, he’s a rookie, and he didn’t get as many bad results as Fernando Mendoza. In fact, Simpson’s biggest negatives on the box score were merely the incompletions, of which there were relatively few. The film will tell a different story. At times that story will be giving Simpson deserved credit for things that a 6-yard completion fails to convey, like play recognition or arm strength. Or an 8-yard run that may not seem like much, but displays how Simpson’s “dip and run” elusiveness could extend plays that Matthew Stafford couldn’t. At times the story will go deeper into mechanics and subpar footwork, and other things that would probably hold back Simpson from being a great starter until he develops and fixes those potential issues. Things that may have led Simpson to some errant throws. Sometimes also overlooking or missing better options to throw to than the ones he ended up choosing, or that coaches chose for him. If you welcome the good, can you also accept that there’s some bad? In a long breakdown of Simpson’s third and final preseason start against the Chargers, former NFL quarterback J.T. O’Sullivan objectively looks at every play by the Rams rookie quarterback. It’s a fair analysis that shouldn’t make any Rams fan less confident in Simpson’s ability to become a good quarterback knowing that these are the same types of things that Simpson should be hearing when he breaks down film with L.A.’s coaches. You’ll also hear some interesting thoughts on players like C.J. Daniels and Max Klare, at times doing more to take options away from Simpson than they were helping him.

A season where the Rams are heavily expected to make a run at the Super Bowl. How busy must you be to be Kroenke? The expectation is that Kroenke and the Angels will find success, as so many other of his teams (like the Rams) have. We’ll see. LA Rams owner Kroenke reaches agreement to buy Angels (mlb.com) “It ends Moreno’s 23-year tenure as owner since he bought the club in 2003, but he will remain a minority owner with an undisclosed share. The Angels had early success under his ownership, winning six division titles (2004-05, ’07-09 and ’14) but have struggled over the last decade. They haven’t had a winning record since 2015 and currently have a 53-85 record that’s tied for the worst mark in the AL. “The Angels are a storied franchise anchored in a great market,” Kroenke said in a statement released by both the Angels and Kroenke Sports & Entertainment. “We look forward to an exciting future with the Angels organization.” Mike Trout isn’t ditching Eagles fandom despite Rams owner buying Angels (sports.yah00) “ Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke has agreed to buy the Angels , with the monumental purchase going through Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for a valuation of $4 billion. Assuming Trout stays with the ballclub through the remainder of his contract — expires after the 2030 season — he will probably get to know the new man in charge pretty well. The three-time American League MVP has no intention of abandoning the Eagles, though. “Mike Trout said he’s too diehard of an Eagles fan to change allegiances and become a Rams fan with Stan Kroenke buying the team,” MLB.com’s Rhett Bollinger posted on X. “But said that he would go support the Rams at a home game as long as they weren’t playing the Eagles.” Why Your Team Sucks 2026: Los Angeles Rams (defector) “The Rams were SO CLOSE to winning the NFC West, getting a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs, and being served up a birthday cake of a Patriots team in the Super Bowl—only for the division-rival Seahawks to snatch all of that away from them and win the championship. Those seven weeks are collectively the most delighted I have ever been as a Seahawks fan. A Super Bowl win may be the mountaintop, but I am a hater first and foremost, and the combined late-season failures of the Rams and 49ers will keep my wicked black heart pumping poison long after my brain dies. Friends, I’m about to tell you all about how the Rams faceplanted, and I am GIDDY. I get to live it all again.“ The LA Rams are either winning the Super Bowl or facing a massive disappointment with almost no margin for error (atozsports) “As Ben Fox pointed out on X, every team over the past 30 years that entered Week 1 with +500 or better odds to win the Super Bowl outright has failed to hoist the Lombardi Trophy. That has happened 20 times. Those short favorites have gone 0-for-20 winning the ring. The list reads like a graveyard of dominant rosters. It includes the 2024, 2021, and 2020 Chiefs, the 2019 and 2017 Patriots, the 2015 and 2014 Seahawks, the 2011, 2009, 2008, and 2007 Patriots, a three-way tie in 2005 between Indianapolis, New England, and Philadelphia, the 2004 Eagles, the 2001 and 2002 St. Louis Rams, the 2000 St. Louis Rams, the 1999 Vikings, the 1998 and 1997 Packers, and the 1996 49ers.“ Rams rumors: Aaron Donald’s mysterious Rams Week 1 status less likely (sports.yahoo) “ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported Tuesday that a later debut currently appears more likely. “I would say, based on everything I’ve been told, a Week 2 or 3 debut looks more likely than Week 1,” Graziano said on “NFL Live.” “But again, it’s still on the table.” And keeping it on the table may have some value.“ Puka Nacua’s ex-girlfriend makes new abuse claim as Rams await suspension verdict: ‘What broke me’ (nypost) “Puka Nacua’s off-the-field worries could be getting worse. title: Cian Slone, Greedy Vance, players who deserved to make Las Vegas Raiders’ 53-man roster
summary: In my mailbag column after the NFL cutdown day, every year I get at least one question about which players I would have liked to see make the Las Vegas Raiders’ initial 53-man roster. So, I’m beating you all to the punch this time around! Of course, the Raiders can’t keep everyone, and the math […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders defensive end Cian Slone (48) celebrates after sacking Arizona Cardinals quarterback Kedon Slovis (12) in the second half at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In my mailbag column after the NFL cutdown day, every year I get at least one question about which players I would have liked to see make the Las Vegas Raiders’ initial 53-man roster . So, I’m beating you all to the punch this time around! Of course, the Raiders can’t keep everyone, and the math just didn’t work out for most of the guys below. But they are at least deserving of some recognition for the body of work they put together during training camp and the preseason over the summer, in my opinion. EDGE Cian Slone There’s no denying that Patrick Johnson had the better preseason, but I thought it would make more sense for the rebuilding Raiders to keep the promising rookie over the 28-year-old. Or roster five edges to ensure both Johnson and Slone stay in the building after Keyron Crawford suffered a season-ending injury during the final preseason. But it’s no harm, no foul since the NC State product cleared waivers and was added to the practice squad on Monday. DB Greedy Vance With so many young defensive backs in Las Vegas’ secondary, Vance is another guy who was waived likely because there just weren’t enough roster spots at his position. The 2025 UDFA made some noise in training camp by nabbing a couple of interceptions off Fernando Mendoza and had a pretty good game against the Arizona Cardinals in the preseason. Luckily, Vance is back on the practice squad, and it wouldn’t be surprising if he’s one of the first players called up this season. IOL Will Putnam To be clear, it was pretty slim pickings for the final spot on the offensive line between Putnam, Jordan Meredith and Atonio Mafi. That was one of the hardest decisions to make during my 53-man roster projections, and I did have Mafi making it over Putnam in my final prediction ahead of the game against the San Francisco 49ers. However, the former did struggle in pass protection throughout the preseason, and I probably would have flipped those two after the 49ers matchup. Plus, the latter has experience playing center, and the backup job behind Tyler Linderbaum is a question mark right now. Granted, Putnam is also back on the practice squad to potentially fill that role if Linderbaum were to get injured. LB Segun Olubi I wouldn’t pound the table for Olubi to make the team, but I was surprised he didn’t get a spot. He brings value as a special teamer and stood out defensively with a handful of tackles against the Houston Texans. However, the coaching staff opted to keep just four linebackers on the 53-man roster and originally had Cameron McGrone over Olubi on the practice squad. The latter was added on Monday to remain a call-up option, though. So, this one doesn’t quite fit with the overall theme, but it did catch my eye as something I wasn’t expecting to see. DT Brandon Cleveland To be fair, Cleveland was pretty quiet for the majority of the summer. But I thought he made things interesting with his performance in the final preseason game by tying for the team lead in total tackles (five) and having the outright lead in TFLs (two). However, Foley Fatukasi being a late addition and making an immediate impact in Houston likely sealed the rookie’s fate before San Francisco rolled into town. Cleveland still has a chance to make a name for himself on the practice squad, though. DT Gary Smith III Smith’s odds of making the team also took a hit with Fatuaski’s arrival. The nose tackle from UCLA didn’t make a ton of plays during the preseason, but he did a good job of holding his gap consistently, which is more than a lot of defensive tackles on the Raiders’ roster could say. Smith has a limited skill set, but he could potentially fill a need on Las Vegas’ defense and is just a practice-squad call-up away from getting an opportunity to prove himself during the regular season.

title: Thoughts on Kirk Cousins being Raiders Week 1 starting quarterback
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have named veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins the Week 1 starting quarterback over No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. Let’s look at the key aspects of this decision: Not a surprise: This has been the expected outcome for months. The Raiders had a plan and this was it. That’s why Cousins, 38, […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders watches as Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up before the preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have named veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins the Week 1 starting quarterback over No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. Let’s look at the key aspects of this decision: Not a surprise: This has been the expected outcome for months. The Raiders had a plan and this was it. That’s why Cousins, 38, was signed. They wanted a veteran to help bring along Mendoza and Cousins is perfect. The fact that he played under new Raiders’ coach Klint Kubiak made this an ideal fit. Kubiak, general manager John Spytek and part owner Tom Brady all wanted to have Mendoza on the bench to start the season. Cousins made that plan easy with a strong training camp. This was, in the end, an easy decision. How long will Cousins play? Well, it’s up to Cousins. If he plays well and the Raiders win, he will keep the job as deep into the season as possible. But if the Raiders go on a losing skid, Mendoza will hover. Also, it could be a matter of Cousins’ health. The 15-season veteran hasn’t played a full season since 2022, so his health could be a factor. Key for Mendoza now: As Kubiak recently said, Mendoza must get as many reps as possible. Of course, that will be difficult during the season as the starters get most of the practice reps. But Mendoza must work early and late in the day with quarterback coach Mike Sullivan to get as prepared as possible to make his NFL debut. Is there a perfect time for Mendoza to play? There are different theories. There has been some speculation the Raiders could wait until after their December bye and to get away from a stretch of tough defenses. I think the reality is it’s a fluid situation. It will depends on Cousins’ performance and health, the team’s record and Mendoza’s readiness. So, it will likely be something the team evaluates on a weekly basis and the production and the health of the offensive line will also playa role. Mendoza will not be thrown t0 the wolves behind a broken line. Will Mendoza start season as No. 2 or No. 3? This week, ESPN reported Aidan O’Connell could start the season as Cousins’ backup, making Mendoza the emergency quarterback to start the season. The report stated it would be part of Mendoza’s process. We probably won’t know the answer to this until the inactives are announced before the Miami game on September 13. NFL trend bucked: The last six quarterbacks drafted No. 1 overall were Week 1 starters as rookies. The last quarterback picked first not open the season as the starter when Baker Mayfield in Cleveland in 2018. He first played in Week 3 and made his first start in Week 4 against the Raiders.

title: Raiders optimistic Ashton Jeanty will be ready to play in Week 1
summary: While the Las Vegas Raiders’ big news of Wednesday was coach Klint Kubiak naming veteran Kirk Cousins the starting quarterback over No. 1 overall pick, Rookie Fernando Mendoza, there was other significant news offered by the coach that also affects the Week 1 season opener against Miami Dolphins on Sept 13. Asked if he is […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 20: Ashton Jeanty #2 of the Las Vegas Raiders attends a news conference after an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 20, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Las Vegas Raiders’ big news of Wednesday was coach Klint Kubiak naming veteran Kirk Cousins the starting quarterback over No. 1 overall pick, Rookie Fernando Mendoza, there was other significant news offered by the coach that also affects the Week 1 season opener against Miami Dolphins on Sept 13. Asked if he is optimistic that starting running back Ashton Jeanty will be ready for the opener that looms in 11 days, Kubiak simply said “yes.” Tuesday, Las Vegas Raiders general John Spytek said this of Jeanty’s return from injury : “I expect him to be back as quick as he can,” Spytek said. “Maybe quicker than some would expect, but we’ll see.’ Jeanty was working on the side Tuesday with a trainer as he recovers from suffering an ankle injury 10 days ago. He has not practice since the injury. Clearly, the team is hopeful he will be able to work next week prior to the Miami game. This is continued good news after the team was initially worried Jeanty suffered a serious injury. Meanwhile, the injury news isn’t as good regarding rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford. Kubiak said the third-round pick, who was put on the season-ending injured reserve Sunday, suffered an Achilles injury. Thursday night, the team said it was ankle injury. That is an important clarification because Achilles injury timelines are usually much longer than ankle injuries. Potentially, this injury could affect whether Crawford is ready for training camp next year. Meanwhile, Kubiak didn’t say whether Jackson Powers-Johnson or Caleb Rogers will start at right guard. He said they’re both starters and they both will play this season. Powers-Johnson has been working with the first-team offense mostly lately. Rookie running back Mike Washington is now wearing No. 4 and kicker Matt Gay is wearing No. 14.

title: Doubt in Dolphins; Can Miami prove everyone wrong?
summary: There are not many believers in the 2026 version of the Miami Dolphins in the national media. Ever since the hiring of new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and the subsequent mass exodus of talent across the roster, the talk has been more about Miami’s dead cap situation and the possibility of the organization “earning” the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 20: Head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins speask to the media during training camp at Baptist Health Training Complex on August 20, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are not many believers in the 2026 version of the Miami Dolphins in the national media. Ever since the hiring of new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and the subsequent mass exodus of talent across the roster, the talk has been more about Miami’s dead cap situation and the possibility of the organization “earning” the number one overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft than the team possibly winning actual football games on the field this upcoming season. In Week One, Miami will travel to Las Vegas to take on the Raiders — a team that won three games in 2025 and wound up picking first in the 2026 NFL Draft themselves. Still, heading into that game, the Dolphins are considered the underdogs according to most sportsbooks. In fact, in most places, the Raiders are favored by at least three points, with some sites favoring them by four points or more. Count the talking heads at NFL Network as those with the mindset that the Dolphins will be bad — like, really bad — in 2026. In fact, against the Raiders, not a single person has picked Miami to win that game, or even cover the spread. NFL Network makes picks for Week 1, Dolphins at Raiders pic.twitter.com/XML8k3Jnpf — Joe Schad (@schadjoe) September 3, 2026 In 2025, the Raiders defense gave up an average of 25.4 points per game — the 8th most in the National Football League. As you can see above, Brandon Perna thinks the Dolphins will score exactly three points against that defense. At the end of the day, what Dan Parr, Kevin Patra, Brooke Cersosimo and others think probably doesn’t matter all that much to the folks inside the buildings in Miami Gardens. The Dolphins can’t control the pessimistic predictions coming from outside of the organization. They can only control what happens when they take the field against the Raiders. And right now, seeing nearly every analyst around the league disrespect them should provide all the motivation Miami needs. The doubters have spoken. Now it’s up to the Dolphins to answer — not with words, but with toughness, heart… And hopefully, a win.

title: Dolphins vs. Raiders: Kirk Cousins named starter for Las Vegas in Week 1
summary: The Miami Dolphins face the Las Vegas Raiders in 11 days as the NFL 2026 regular season kicks off. As they game plan and prepare for the game, Miami now knows who they will be facing as the Raiders’ quarterback – and it really should not come as a surprise even if it does break […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders gestures while running off the field following the game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins face the Las Vegas Raiders in 11 days as the NFL 2026 regular season kicks off. As they game plan and prepare for the game, Miami now knows who they will be facing as the Raiders’ quarterback – and it really should not come as a surprise even if it does break a trend around the league. According to Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak, veteran Kirk Cousins will be the starter while first-overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza will begin the season as the backup. The Raiders opting to let Mendoza begin the season on the bench snaps a streak of six-straight quarterbacks selected number one overall to start in Week 1. Cousins signed a five-year contract with the Raiders in April. Going into his 15th season, Cousins was available on the free agent market after the Atlanta Falcons released him after just two years in a four-year deal they signed with him in 2024. Cousins has also played for the Minnesota Vikings and was a fourth-round pick of the Washington Commanders in 2012. Washington also selected quarterback Robert Griffin III that year, selecting him second-overall, and leading to a battle between the two rookies. Cousins eventually surpassed Griffin, taking over the full-time starters job in 2015 after replacing an injured Griffin in 2014. For his career, Cousins has 44,700 passing yards with 298 touchdowns and 131 interceptions. He has a career completion rate of 66.7 percent and a passer rating of 96.8. Mendoza won the Heisman Trophy and the National Championship last year at Indiana, his only seasons with the Hoosiers. He spent his first three years in college at the University of California. He will now wait for his opportunity to move into the starting position. For more on the announcement of Cousins as the starter in Las Vegas and for all things Raiders, check out Silver and Black Pride .

title: Vikings Make a Flurry of Practice Squad Moves
summary: Over the course of the last twenty-four hours, the Minnesota Vikings have been busy, particularly when it comes to their practice squad. Outside of the addition of Kyle Van Noy, whose signing to the practice squad became official this morning, the Vikings have brought in five more players to the practice squad over the past […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Jack Pyburn #58 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers tackles DeeJay Dallas #20 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during a preseason game at EverBank Field on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the course of the last twenty-four hours, the Minnesota Vikings have been busy, particularly when it comes to their practice squad. Outside of the addition of Kyle Van Noy, whose signing to the practice squad became official this morning, the Vikings have brought in five more players to the practice squad over the past couple of days. A couple of them are familiar, as they were waived on Monday to facilitate the players that the Vikings claimed on waivers, but there are others that we’ll get you acquainted with shortly. Here’s the short version. The Vikings have added the following players to the practice squad: WR Dillon Bell QB Max Brosmer RB Deejay Dallas TE Cam Grandy DL Naquan Jones OLB Kyle Van Noy In order to make room for those players on the practice squad, the Vikings have waived the following players: C Gavin Gerhardt G Joshua Gray TE Marshall Lang OT Tristan Leigh OLB Cam’Ron Stewart The Vikings had 15 players on the practice squad after their initial lot of signings on Monday, so with the signings and releases, they’re now at their full allotment of 16. As far as the additions are concerned, Bell and Brosmer spent training camp with the Vikings, and we’ve posted about Van Noy already a couple of times (which you can see here and here ). Let’s give you a bit about the other three new faces. Dallas has been in the league for a bit, as he was a fourth-round pick of the Seattle Seahawks in the 2020 NFL Draft. He played his college ball at Miami (FL), and spent his first four seasons with the Seahawks. He was a role player for Seattle, collecting 112 carries for 468 yards and four touchdowns while also getting 61 receptions for 396 yards and another score in those four seasons. In 2024, he moved on to the Arizona Cardinals, where he was used almost exclusively as a kick returner. He had a 96-yard kickoff return for a touchdown that season, becoming the first player to return one of the league’s new “dynamic kickoffs” for a score. In 2025, he only played in six games, appearing in three games for the Carolina Panthers and three more for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Jones has also been in the league for several seasons. He came into the league in 2021, signing with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent from Michigan State. He spent his first two and a half seasons with Tennessee, and then spent the last part of the 2023 season with the Arizona Cardinals. After a brief stint on the Miami Dolphins’ practice squad to start the 2024 season, Jones went back to Arizona in 2024, appearing in 12 games. Last season, he signed with the Los Angeles Chargers, playing eight games with them before being released in December and ending up with the Houston Texans, appearing in four games with them. He had signed a one-year deal with the Texans in the offseason but was released as part of their final cuts. Grandy, whose signing had been reported on Monday but not officially finalized until Tuesday, signed with the Cincinnati Bengals as an undrafted free agent after the 2024 NFL Draft. He spent his first two seasons with the Bengals and wound up on their practice squad to start the year. He was eventually elevated to their main roster, and over the past two seasons has appeared in 13 games for them, playing largely on special teams. He’s caught seven passes for 35 yards and a touchdown. So, with all the changes, the Vikings’ practice squad now looks like this: CB Da’Veawn Armstead WR Dillon Bell WR Michael Briscoe QB Max Brosmer G Henry Byrd RB DeeJay Dallas TE Cam Grandy S Kahlef Hailassie DL Naquan Jones LB Bangally Kamara OT Jack Nelson CB Bryce Phillips DL Jahvaree Ritzee WR Trayvon Rudolph S Tavierre Thomas OLB Kyle Van Noy Alright, now everybody should be caught up on everything. If the Vikings do make any more moves, we will bring them to you here as soon as we have them.

title: Patriots rookie found out he made the roster via Instagram
summary: Unlike 37 of his teammates, Quintayvious Hutchins was not asked to return his iPad ahead of the NFL roster cutdown deadline on Sunday. The New England Patriots had decided to keep the rookie outside linebacker on their 53-man roster. They just never actually told him. One of the quirks of cutdown day, after all, is […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Quintayvious Hutchins #45 of the New England Patriots lines up against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Unlike 37 of his teammates , Quintayvious Hutchins was not asked to return his iPad ahead of the NFL roster cutdown deadline on Sunday. The New England Patriots had decided to keep the rookie outside linebacker on their 53-man roster. They just never actually told him. One of the quirks of cutdown day, after all, is that only players to get released are typically informed of their fate. Others are not, which might come as a surprise to first-year players such as Hutchins. He instead found out that he had made the team by scrolling through social media. “[An] Instagram post, when they posted the 53-man roster, that’s how I really found out,” he told the media at his New locker this week. “I saw the 53-man roster and was like, ‘Oh damn, I really made it.’” Having spent his entire five-year college career at Boston College, Hutchins made the move to Foxborough as the 247th overall pick in this year’s draft. Given his late-round status and the competition in the room, his spot on the eventual roster was not guaranteed. However, the 23-year-old had a solid training camp and saw a steady uptick in quality reps along the Patriots’ defensive edge. This, plus a preseason performance that saw him register eight tackles and a sack as well as three special teams takedowns, set the stage for him to ultimately make the team. Together with Dre’Mont Jones, Elijah Ponder and fellow rookie Gabe Jacas, he now is one of only four outside linebackers on the team. With that first step now taken, Hutchins is already looking ahead. “The job is not done. Continue to prove myself to earn a role on the team and just be dominant every chance I get,” he said. “You have to come in, work, keep your head up, and keep going.”
