title: Kayshon Boutte opens up about trade from Patriots to Texans
summary: One week after getting traded from the New England Patriots to the Houston Texans, wide receiver Kayshon Boutte stood question and answer in front of the media for the first time. And while most of the questions during his press conference on Wednesday centered around his first impression of the Texans, there also was one […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 06: Kayshon Boutte #9 of the New England Patriots speaks to the media after New England Patriots training camp on August 6, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One week after getting traded from the New England Patriots to the Houston Texans , wide receiver Kayshon Boutte stood question and answer in front of the media for the first time. And while most of the questions during his press conference on Wednesday centered around his first impression of the Texans, there also was one about him leaving New England after three seasons. Boutte, who had requested a trade in the offseason, clearly laid out the eventual reason for his departure. “They did pay two guys to come in and do that job. Sadly, it is the way it is,” he explained. “Being that it’s a contract year for me, I sought a bigger role.” The two guys in question are free agency pickup Romeo Doubs and trade acquisition A.J. Brown. The former was given a four-year, $68 million contract on the open market, while the Patriots used a first- and fifth-round draft choices to acquire the latter from Philadelphia. Their arrival fundamentally changed New England’s wide receiver room, and ultimately Boutte’s outlook within it. Despite being a part-time starter in 2024, who finished with 42 receptions for 719 yards and seven touchdowns, he spent training camp as the Patriots’ WR4 behind Doubs, Brown and slot option DeMario Douglas — and that might not have been all. As head coach Mike Vrabel claimed after the preseason finale in Cleveland, Boutte “probably would have been inactive” on game days this season. While seemingly a harsh assessment, the 24-year-old himself will not use those remarks as extra motivation. “I feel like what Vrabes said in his media interview, it wasn’t anything bad,” Boutte pointed out. “I wouldn’t say I’ll use that as fuel. At the end of the day, he said that. It was an honest opinion. He said that, he spoke his truth, and pretty much move forward from it.”

full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - NOVEMBER 24: Detroit Lions Tight End Shane Zylstra (84) warms up for the NFL football game between the Detroit Lions and the Indianapolis Colts on November 24, 2024, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The practice squad has reached capacity in Foxborough. The New England Patriots announced the signing of tight end Shane Zylstra amid a series of moves on Wednesday, bringing the group to its 17-man limit entering the regular season. Zylstra, 29, originally entered the NFL with the Minnesota Vikings as an undrafted free agent out of Minnesota State in 2020. After being waived at the league’s roster deadline following his rookie training camp, the 6-foot-4, 244-pound former Division II All-American joined the Detroit Lions. He went on to spend five years between practice squad, active roster and injured reserve for head coach Dan Campbell in the NFC North before making an offseason stop with the Buffalo Bills. A veteran of 35 games, including six starts, Zylstra has caught 18 passes for 136 yards and four touchdowns. The tight end’s career spans 582 snaps on offense to go with 393 snaps on special teams. He now heads to a room that features captain Hunter Henry, rookies Eli Raridon and Tanner Arkin, as well as recent waiver claim Cameron Latu on the 53, while the Patriots had free agent Kenny Fletcher Jr. in for a workout on Wednesday. In additional midweek transactions, New England waived wide receiver Jimmy Kibble and safety Eric Butler from injured reserve. Both will be subject to the claiming period before officially becoming free agents. Kibble, 22, had been waived with an injury designation as training camp opened in July and subsequently reverted to injured reserve. The 6-foot-1, 199-pound wideout signed in Foxborough as part of the club’s 2026 undrafted class in May. A Georgetown product, Kibble caught 149 receptions for 2,642 yards and 16 touchdowns across 39 games. First-team All-Patriot League honors arrived as a Hoyas captain in 2025 after catching 63 passes for 1,002 yards and four touchdowns. Butler, 23, worked out in July and signed in August before being let go with an injury designation on the eve of the cutdown deadline . The 6-foot-2, 195-pound safety went undrafted out of San Diego State in 2026 en route to rookie minicamp invitations with the Las Vegas Raiders and New Orleans Saints. Butler appeared in 48 games, including 23 starts, during his collegiate career. He totaled 119 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, one interception returned a touchdown, plus two blocked punts for the Aztecs. Seven players remain on injured reserve at Gillette Stadium. The season-ending group includes running back Myles Montgomery, tight end Julian Hill, wide receiver Jeremiah Webb and defensive tackle Isaiah Iton. As for offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, linebacker Khalil Jacobs and punter Bryce Baringer, all three eligible for activation after missing a minimum of four games.

title: Patriots News: Don’t buy the depth doom
summary: Depth matters. I’m not going to make the argument that it doesn’t. What I will point out is that the Patriots aren’t the lone team where depth at certain positions is a concern. It’s the reality of limited rosters. How many clubs could lose their starters at key positions and remain contenders? Truth is, injuries […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Robert Spillane #14 of the New England Patriots reacts as he runs following an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Depth matters. I’m not going to make the argument that it doesn’t. What I will point out is that the Patriots aren’t the lone team where depth at certain positions is a concern. It’s the reality of limited rosters. How many clubs could lose their starters at key positions and remain contenders? Truth is, injuries would cripple most teams. Losing a top offensive lineman invites opponents to target the replacement, which affects quarterback play, which affects receivers and offensive productivity. More pressure is then put on the defense, and vice versa. The Patriots have experienced it, both as the wounded and the predator. Unlike Preseason Week 3, the regular season won’t be played with a roster of 2nd-3rd team depth players. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kyle Williams has a special trick as a wide receiver That was on display during the preseason, as the second-year wide receiver caught three touchdowns all on the same route: a go ball. But Williams knows his game has more than just that one trick. “I’ve been hearing that my whole life man, so I wouldn’t really say it’s a chip on my shoulder,” Williams said. “I know what I can do. I know I’m more than just a vertical guy. Whatever my role is that’s my role and I’m gonna accept it.” Williams’ elite release package and vertical speed make him a big-time threat along the outside. That was his role for much of last season, as one-third of his routes were go balls — one of the highest rates in football. Among the few players with a higher rate was recently traded wide receiver Kayshon Boutte. The 2025 third-round pick’s ability to win deep will continue to be an asset for the Patriots’ offense — especially with Boutte’s departure. While the team spent the offseason upgrading the wide receiver depth chart, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs are not specifically burners at the position. Quarterback Drake Maye is also one of the best deep-ball throwers in the NFL. Entering his second season, however, Williams is adding to his game. This offseason, the 23-year old spent time running more intermediate routes and moving around the formation after spending virtually all of last season outside and on the ball. “In college, I really wasn’t exposed to too many intermediate routes. So now I’m getting that opportunity to do it,” Williams said this summer. “So Year 1 to Year 2 it’s definitely been night and day. Now it’s just that ball finding me across the middle and everything so I can really showcase what I’ve been working on.” Mastering those route concepts in Josh McDaniels’ offense is no easy task for a wide receiver. Williams noted that the on-the-fly decision-making process was the biggest challenge, but was pleased looking back on his training camp with how his mindset developed throughout the process. “It’s time on task, right?,” wide receiver coach Todd Downing said. “And there are some things that collegiately, maybe Kyle was able to do, because he was just more physically talented than some of the defenses that he was going against. And you get it this league, and I’ve always said that the closer you are to the football, the faster things happen. “I think Kyle is starting to get more and more comfortable with that speed and that urgency that it takes to make the right decisions in there. So, I’m excited where he’s at and I love the approach that he’s taken — a do anything he’s asked approach, and he’s done well with his [opportunities].” As the Patriots are just a week away from their regular season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, Williams is ready to keep growing and find his footing in a talented wide receiver room. “I feel like I bring a lot, just as much as the other guys do,” Williams said. “So, I mean, I don’t really want to single myself out, but as a whole room, I feel like we nasty. I feel like we got a nasty group.”

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 15: Jeremiah Wright #65 of the New Orleans Saints against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Caesars Superdome on August 15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images WR Jordyn Tyson Did not play in preseason. DT Christen Miller It wasn’t surprising that Christen Miller was a standout in preseason, but it was a bit of a shock just how important he was to this defense. Miller was the Saints’ best run defender and dealt with double teams well. He dealt with some injuries throughout the preseason, and those are something to keep in mind, but it was clear he did everything he could to get back on the field. The Saints are going to have a hard time keeping him off the field this season. TE Oscar Delp Delp did not have a great preseason and was unable to stay healthy. He is still dealing with his injury, and his status for Week 1 is unknown. He’s still developing as a TE and will need time in general to make a significant impact on offense. OG Jeremiah Wright Wright was another one of the more developmental players in the Saints’ draft class, but unlike Delp, he played every game and improved each time. By the end of preseason, Wright looked like a standout player on the offensive line and looked solid in both run blocking. The Saints will not start Wright in Week 1, but just like they did with rookies last season, if Cesar Ruiz is struggling, Kellen Moore may not waste time making a change. WRs Bryce Lance and Barion Brown Game three against the Cowboys was an excellent performance by Lance and Brown, proving how important they are to the offense. Lance’s blocking was incredible, Brown’s athleticism made him a threat each time he was on the field, and Moore used them perfectly. This was the story of really the entire preseason, but game three was the cherry on top. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Another injured rookie, Styles Jr. will be starting the season on IR. Missing the first four games is never good for a rookie, but Styles Jr. was likely going to only play on special teams anyway. His preseason was a bit up and down. Styles Jr. made some nice plays but also got beat in coverage. Clearly, he was not ready to start on defense, but as I mentioned, that was never the plan for him this season. CB TJ Hall Jr. Hall Jr. did not survive the 53-man roster cuts, but was brought back to the practice squad. Hopefully, the rookie can stay there and develop this season. OT Mason Murphy Everyone, say hello to the Saints’ new rookie! Yes, one of the team’s signings after the 53-man roster deadline was former Chicago Bears offensive lineman Mason Murphy. He went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft, but the Saints clearly liked him as a depth piece for this offensive line. Murphy was also Wright’s teammate at Auburn and can step in at either tackle or center for the Saints if needed.

title: State of the NFC South: Preseason recap
summary: The preseason is (finally) over, and the start of the season is nearly here. With that being the case, let’s look at a quick NFC South preseason recap! Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Buccaneers had an overall productive preseason experience. QB Jalon Daniels looked like a long term option post Baker Mayfield, Reuben Bain Jr. had […]
full_text: The preseason is (finally) over, and the start of the season is nearly here. With that being the case, let’s look at a quick NFC South preseason recap! Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Buccaneers had an overall productive preseason experience. QB Jalon Daniels looked like a long term option post Baker Mayfield, Reuben Bain Jr. had great plays that made the Bucs feel confident about that draft pick, and the team was able to sign star DT Vita Vea to a contract extension. Also, Bain Jr.’s teammate Kieonte Scott had some really good plays as well, which may be the most important rookie performance of all. Tampa Bay’s pass defense is arguably their biggest weakness, so if Scott can be a quality CB, the defense could be much better. Getting production from the rookies was very important, especially with the injuries and turnover this team has had. Losing Mike Evans in the offseason was big, and in the draft, the Bucs drafted his “replacement”, Ted Hurst. Hurst didn’t have any massive performances, but Bucs media is high on the rookie. Carolina Panthers Entering the preseason, Carolina was faced with some massive injuries to their team. Nic Scourton, who was a standout rookie last year, tore his ACL, and rookie WR Chris Brazzell III also suffered a season-ending knee injury. Brazzell is a WR with all the potential in the world due to his athleticism and size, but is still in the developmental phase of his NFL career. A season-ending injury could really hurt that development, and the Panthers will miss his potential production this season. The good news for Carolina is that the two WRs from the preseason, John Metchie III and Jimmy Horn Jr., both had standout performances, leading to their making the roster. Both players are still considered depth options, but Metchie III did play with QB Bryce Young in college. Atlanta Falcons As of writing this, the Falcons have not named their starting QB for Week 1. Michael Penix Jr. is ramping up from his season-ending injury last season, but he may not be 100% healthy, and risking that makes little sense. Then, Tua Tagovailoa did not have a good end to the preseason, struggling against his former team, the Miami Dolphins. In the end, Jack Strand was the standout QB, and he made the roster, along with Penix, Tua, and Cooper Rush. Interestingly enough, the Falcons also only brought two RBs onto their 53-man roster. Having Bijan Robinson probably takes pressure off the need for depth at that position, but HC Kevin Stefanski knows RB injuries from his time in Cleveland. New Orleans Saints Last we have the Saints, and they had a very up-and-down preseason. The first game was a close loss, the second a horrible defeat, and the third a really good win. At times, the position battles looked lost and uninspiring, but game three against the Dallas Cowboys made everyone feel a bit better going into the season. Spencer Rattler ended up winning the backup QB job, Daniel Carlson won the kicker competition, and although Kevin Austin Jr. initially got the last WR spot, he ended up getting released soon after. The main question that still lingers from preseason is the WR room and TE room, because the Saints need to add at least one player in each of those groups. Going into the season with only 4 WRs with the injury luck the Saints have had, and 3 TEs eventhough the team wants to use more TEs this season, makes little sense.

title: 6 defensive linemen the NY Giants should consider signing
summary: The New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen addressed the media on Wednesday. He was asked about the roster and potential areas for improvement ahead of the Giants’ Week 1 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Schoen stated that the Giants are scouring available players and doing their due diligence, but then the topic of the […]
full_text: The New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen addressed the media on Wednesday. He was asked about the roster and potential areas for improvement ahead of the Giants’ Week 1 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Schoen stated that the Giants are scouring available players and doing their due diligence, but then the topic of the defensive line was addressed, and this was Schoen’s response: “We signed D.J. Reader, Shelby (Harris), we traded for C.J. Okoye, we’ve got DA (Darius Alexander). Bobby Jamison-Travis had a good camp. We’ve got a couple of vets on the practice squad, probably going to sign another one next week. So yeah, I feel good where we are right now. And again, we’ll continue, that’s something we’ll continue and see what opportunities are out there.“ Schoen mentioned that New York is interested in signing another veteran defensive tackle next week. The Giants had three defensive tackles and a big defensive end in for a workout on Wednesday: Benito Jones, David Blay, Aaron Graves, and Dawuane Smoot. Blay and Graves are both undrafted rookies this season, so they’re not veterans, but the Giants are certainly interested. Let’s explore Jones and Smoot, plus other available veteran defensive linemen that could help the Giants’ depth. Benito Jones Benito Jones is a 28-year-old 6-foot-1, 335-pound defensive lineman who went undrafted out of Mississippi in 2020. Jones started his career with Miami before playing two seasons in Detroit; he then returned to Miami for two seasons and spent the 2026 training camp on the Raiders’ practice squad. Jones only played 15 defensive snaps in preseason for the Las Vegas Raiders before being cut. Jones is a veteran with 59 pressures and four sacks to his name. He has 41 STOPs and has played 1,700 defensive snaps, with very poor PFF grades and a high missed-tackle rate. He has experience as a nose tackle and a 1-technique. Dawuane Smoot Smoot is much more of an edge defender than a defensive tackle, but he does align inside and has been used as a 4i-shade and a three-technique in certain situations. Smoot is entering his 10th season in the NFL, and all but one was spent in Jacksonville — he played 322 snaps for the Buffalo Bills in 2024 before returning to the Liam Coen-led Jaguars in 2025. Smoot has 203 pressures and 27 sacks throughout his career, while also earning 35 tackles for a loss and seven forced fumbles. He’s been a productive player with 3,725 defensive snaps to his name. He hasn’t had more than 20 pressures since 2022, but he did have a 50-pressure season in 2021. New York had him in for a workout this week, and he could give the Giants another physical edge with some inside pass-rushing ability, similar to Chauncey Golston. DaQuan Jones The 34-year-old played 424 snaps for the Buffalo Bills last season and recorded 13 STOPs and 21 pressures. He was an effective rotational player for Buffalo, and that would be his role with the Giants as well. Jones is long in the tooth but has not slowed down much from a productivity standpoint. He has 238 pressures and 25 sacks to his name. Adding Jones would give the Giants a geriatric defensive line room, but one filled with three reliable players that can allow Darius Alexander and Bobby Jameson-Travis to develop. Jihad Ward Is Jihad Ward coming back to New York? I have no clue, but the former Giant just had his best season with Dennard Wilson last year. The 32-year-old recorded an impressive 47 pressures and five sacks last season, operating as one of Wilson’s most effective twist-game players. Ward is more of a BIG defensive end, but he could be the veteran Schoen is referencing, for both Schoen and Wilson have experience with Jihad Ward. He is 6-5, 287 pounds, and has four consecutive seasons with more than 20 pressures, two of which were with the Giants. Elijah Garcia Hey, another familiar face! Garcia played well as a depth piece for the Giants in the final Brian Daboll years, but he was claimed by Atlanta late last season and spent this training camp in Christian Parker’s defense. Garcia did not make the final 53-man roster, but the 6-5, 302-pound former Giant could be a depth option. Eric Gregory Gregory is hardly a veteran, but I wanted to add him to the list. The 6-4, 320-pounder went undrafted in 2025 out of Arkansas and played 136 snaps for the Patriots last season. He earned two STOPS, three hurries, and had five tackles. Gregory recorded three consecutive seasons with 17 pressures in college, but was nearing Van Wilder status as a Razorback — he played six seasons of college football. He could be a depth piece for the Giants at a position of need.

title: How did NY Giants’ DT Darius Alexander really play this preseason?
summary: There is a lot of discussion surrounding the New York Giants as the regular season approaches. While much of the conversation has surrounded the offense, there are some storylines on the defense that demand our attention too. On the positive side, the Giants’ pass rush could be among the most formidable in the NFL (which […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 15: Darius Alexander #91 of the New York Giants tackles J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings during a preseason game at MetLife Stadium on August 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Mike Coppola/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is a lot of discussion surrounding the New York Giants as the regular season approaches. While much of the conversation has surrounded the offense, there are some storylines on the defense that demand our attention too. On the positive side, the Giants’ pass rush could be among the most formidable in the NFL (which remains a passing league), the linebacking corps looks deep and talented, and the Giants’ secondary could be primed to surprise skeptics. However, if there’s one area of concern it’s along the defensive line. In particular, 2025 third round pick Darius Alexander has been a frequent topic — and target — throughout the preseason. Giants’ great Carl Banks has said multiple times that the Giants need to see more from Alexander, while Pro Football Focus has pilloried him. But, did he play poorly? After all, the NFL is fast and the action along the defensive line can be messy to follow. Takes spawned in the moment can often prove to be somewhat less than accurate. So we’re going to go to the eye in the sky to get as accurate an assessment as we can. The bad Footing If there’s one issue that immediately stands out in Alexander’s game — and by “immediately” I mean on the very first play of the preseason — it’s that he can have bit of trouble staying on his feet. While I won’t go so far as to say that it’s a consistent problem, it does crop up multiple times. That said, there doesn’t seem to be a consistent issue with Alexander’s technique that leads to him being on the ground, and there seems to be several culprits. On the first play, a Vikings’ 18-yard prun, we see a good example of the issues that (should be) within Alexander’s ability to correct. We see Alexander lined up as the 5-technique on the outside shoulder of the Vikings’ left tackle. The Vikings execute a wide-zone run to that side, putting Alexander on the play-side. He starts off the play well, engaging the left tackle and bowing him back while giving up little ground. His hips are in the left B-gap, essentially closing the gap and helping to string the run laterally. That, however, is where things start to go wrong. As Alexander engages with the left tackle, his base begins to narrow and his pads rise. As that happens, the left guard gets piece of Alexander’s side, who isn’t able to absorb the block with a narrowed base while also moving laterally. That overbalances him, forces his pads up further, and allows the left tackle to put Alexander on the ground. From there, the guard is able to give Micah McFadden a shove, perhaps disrupting him enough that back is able to run through McFadden’s arms. Alexander generally does a very good job of playing half-man leverage and putting his hips in gaps to close them. However, he needs to do a better job of using his long arms to fend off blockers when he does so, as well as more consistently keeping a wide base to maintain his balance. This also showed up in a couple instances in Week 3 against the Jets. It seems to crop up most commonly when Alexander tries to run his feet and drive the blockers back, as opposed to keeping a wide base and simply eating the blocks. Notably, his hips rotate as he tries to drive the blocker, making it easier for the second linemen to move him laterally. There were also multiple instances of Alexander being tripped by his teammates as he either engaged blockers or penetrated into the backfield. It’s difficult to say whether that’s a “him” problem. For instance, we see Alexander against the Dolphins. Alexander is lined up in the right B-gap, between the right guard and right tackle. He engages the right guard with good leverage, also inserting his right arm into the A-gap to get a piece of the guard. Between squeezing the B-gap as well as putting his hips in the C-gap, Alexander is able to wall off the right side of the line and creates a path into the backfield for cornerback Nic Jones on a run blitz. That forces the back through the left A-gap. Alexander slows the right guard down well enough that Jack Kelly could insert himself into the left A-gap and blow up the play in the backfield. However, Kelly hesitates slightly which allows the back to work back to the right side. At the same time, Jones steps on Alexander’s leg, tripping him and allowing the right tackle to expand the gap and the back is able to pick up some dirty yards. Taken as a whole, we see that not only does Alexander need to continue to work on consistently playing with better technique, but also that his perceived level of play could improve when surrounded by starters. Anchor Alexander’s issues with consistency in his footing bleed into other areas of his game, and in particular his ability to consistently anchor against blockers. We got a good example early on against the Jets. Alexander is aligned as the 3-technique on the left guard’s outside shoulder. He makes an effort to stay low and play with a wide base off of the snap, which allows him to at least hold the guard. However Alexander fails to win inside leverage and gain control of the guard’s chest plate. Instead, the guard gains inside leverage on Alexander, using the grip on his chest plate to torque him laterally and prevent him from engaging with the center, who works up to the second level. This isn’t a huge loss for Alexander, particularly considering he’s able to occupy the guard well enough that that Micah McFadden is able to occupy the gap. The run itself, however, goes for a nice gain after Kelly attempts to occupy the same gap instead of flowing to the outside while Ar’Darius Washington is washed inside by a wide receiver who inserts into the box as a blocker. That said, this is a good example of how Alexander needs to become more consistent in his technique to fully take advantage of his athletic tools. The good Alexander’s tape is littered with flashes of impressive play, particularly as you begin to get a sense for what the Giants want to do on defense. Dennard Wilson’s scheme will likely depend heavily on living in nickel sets and attacking offenses with motion, the blitz, and the threat of the blitz. This isn’t the place to get into the weeds of how a defense can use stunts, twists, zone drops, simulated pressures, and blitzes to attack an offense — that’s for another piece. However, Alexander’s traits hold solid upside for helping to execute a modern defensive scheme. Athleticism Darius Alexander is a very good athlete, with a great first step and explosiveness. That showed up in flashes throughout the preseason. We’ll start with a play in run defense against the Vikings. Alexander begins the play lined up at 5-technique on the left tackle’s outside shoulder. The run is an outside zone to the right, putting Alexander on backside contain and pursuit. The Vikings attempt to account for him with a double-team from the tackle and tight end. However, Alexander is able to split the double team as the tackle releases to block at the second level. He runs the play down from behind as the back attempts to exploit a massive hole created when Josh Tupou gets washed out. This is the look just before Alexander closes on the play: There isn’t much between the back and the open field, and the run could have gone for another double-digit gain (if not much more). Instead, Alexander is able to discard the tight end’s block and close on the back quickly enough that this is only a 4-yard gain. Later in the game we get another good look at Alexander’s speed in space as he drops into a shallow coverage zone to create a path for Kelly on a zone blitz. Both Alexander and Chauncey Golston simulate a rush before dropping out in shallow coverage while linebackers Micah McFadden and Jack Kelly blitz, as well as…

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to including Joe Schoen’s yearly preseason address with the media. Every Division’s ‘Wild Card’ for the 2026 NFL Season | Bleacher Report NFC East: New York Giants. The Ceiling: There’s a world in which Jaxson Dart takes off in his second season and becomes a star with top-notch support from an exciting skill-position group, a promising offensive line, a defense that features massive talent up front and an incoming head coach with Super Bowl pedigree. In that world, the Giants can shock the unpredictable NFC East. The Floor: Ultimately, it remains low with so many questionable variables. The sample is small for Dart, and two key cogs (Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo) are coming back from major injuries. If the Eagles are the Eagles, a better defense helps Dallas bounce back, and Washington can rediscover what got it to the NFC title game in 2024, the Giants could be in for a third consecutive last-place campaign. The 2026 Giants Mission Statement "Our mission statement is to be the best team in the National Football League, and prove it." – John Harbaugh pic.twitter.com/74XGWOW875 — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 2, 2026 NFL execs rank NFC teams: Rams, Seahawks clear favorites. | The Athletic 14. New York Giants. The voter highest on the Giants pointed to their defense. “They have a lot of pieces on defense, and I really liked their draft,” this exec said. “(John) Harbaugh will play everything close, and they’ll be in a ton of one-score games, and we’ll see what happens in the moment of truth. They’re a candidate for those games to play out really well.” Questions at quarterback, running back and receiver persist. “I like the Giants’ potential on defense,” another exec said. “Abdul Carter, Arvell Reese, Brian Burns. But then I don’t know how good that secondary is at corner. They lost Dexter Lawrence in the middle. On offense, Jaxson Dart’s health, Cam Skattebo’s health and Malik Nabers’ health are all concerns. There’s a lot of unknown.” Darius Slayton isn’t done proving himself to Giants after latest roster cut survival | New York Post Slayton, the longest-tenured Giant, has gotten used to uncertainty over his standing and the need to repeatedly prove his worth. “That’s mostly kind of been exacerbated by the turnover [in coaching staffs],” Slayton said. “Anytime there’s new people, there’s going to be that. Just for me, I’ve just been fortunate to be here for four staffs. I don’t take it personally. I understand that you have to show and prove yourself whenever there’s new [coaches]. That’s what I plan to do this year.” Giants’ Greg Newsome: ‘I like our chances’ against ‘dynamic’ Cowboys receivers | New York Daily News As the Steelers’ final play Hail Mary soared incomplete, Pickens dragged Newsome out of the back of the end zone by his helmet as the players engaged. Newsome fought Pickens off. And that set off a full-blown fight as the clock hit zero. Security guards appeared to pull Pickens off Newsome as their tussle spilled into one of the front rows of the stands. After the game, Newsome called Pickens a “fake tough guy” and said Pickens’ behavior was “unnecessary.” “He’s great at the catch point,” Newsome said of Pickens. “That’s something he’s been great at since he got in the league is just being able to make the tough catches. You’ve got number 88, CeeDee [Lamb], he can line up anywhere, do a lot of great things. Definitely great players but I like our chances.” 2026 NFL bold predictions: Potential surprises for 32 teams | ESPN.com Don’t be surprised if … tight end Isaiah Likely is a breakout star in New York. What I’m hearing: Giants coaches light up when talking about Likely, the free agent signee who came over from Baltimore with coach John Harbaugh. They believe he’ll be a real asset for Jaxson Dart as a receiver and think he can win in both man and zone coverage. And they love the way he has embraced and evolved his relationship with Dart since he has been in New York. Likely is a regular visitor to the quarterbacks room, and the connection he has formed with Dart on and off the field could pay major dividends. Likely is a strong candidate to be the team’s second-leading receiver this season and could be even more than that if top wideout Malik Nabers needs time to get up to speed coming off his injury. title: NY Giants GM Joe Schoen expects ‘to be competitive week in and week out’
summary: There is tremendous optimism surrounding the New York Giants entering the 2026. They have an accomplished head coach in John Harbaugh who has raised the bar, and a roster that has been reshaped. This, though, is a still a franchise that has won seven games combined the past two seasons, and gone 13-38 over the […]
full_text: Joe Schoen | Getty Images There is tremendous optimism surrounding the New York Giants entering the 2026. They have an accomplished head coach in John Harbaugh who has raised the bar, and a roster that has been reshaped. This, though, is a still a franchise that has won seven games combined the past two seasons, and gone 13-38 over the past three seasons. The Giants should be better. The question is, how much better? FanDuel Sportsbook places the over/under at 7.5 wins. What is a realistic expectation? General manager Joe Schoen was not predicting a playoff berth or setting a targeted number of victories when he spoke to media on Wednesday in his season-opening press conference. Schoen did, though, set an expectation that the product on the field would be improved. “I feel good about the group that we have and expect us to be competitive week in and week out,” the GM said. “I really like the group, both sides of the ball, special teams. The cut down was very difficult this past weekend from a depth standpoint, some difficult decisions we had to make. And even the top 70 guys in terms of the practice squad, that was difficult for us. “Really competitive group, had a competitive camp and I like our team, I like where we are. And now really, we just got to go out and do it but I do like the roster, I like where we are. We had a competitive camp. And I’m looking forward to seeing how things go Sunday versus the Cowboys.” Joe Schoen's expectations for the Giants this season: "I expect us to be competitive week in and week out. I really like the group." pic.twitter.com/g33ld4V2RN — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 2, 2026 Harbaugh wasn’t about to be dragged into making any sort of prediction. “I know they’ll go out there and be the very best football team they can be,” Harbaugh said. “That’s my expectation. What that ends up being depends on how good we are. And that’s what you find out when you play the games, everything else is just talk.” Harbaugh does feel good about the roster the Giants have assembled in his first season in New York. “I do, I do. I mean, I’m optimistic,” Harbaugh said. “I feel good about our guys but that’s always something that has to be proven. That’s our mission, our mission statement is to be the best team in the National Football League and prove it because that’s what it requires.” Harbaugh, a Super Bowl-winnning coach with 180 regular-season victories (14th-most all all-time) on his resume, has established a standard, pushing players hard both physically and mentally. ‘He’s invested in it’ Schoen, in his fifth season as general manager, admitted that Harbaugh has had an impact on and off the field. “With Coach Harbaugh, he’s invested in it. He’s got a passion for not just coaching and X’s and O’s and schemes, but the personnel part of it. So, that helps a lot. If we all have the same vision when the player gets here, it’s going to be important because we’re all invested in the same vision that you see it out,” Schoen said. “That doesn’t always happen that way. When you bring a player in and there’s a vision, sometimes it can be pushed off to the side. I’ve got a couple different times I’ve seen that happen. But Coach is very invested in this, when we drafted this player, or signed this player, or hey, we got an idea, what, maybe move this player that plays center to guard, or whatever, maybe the versatility, he’s typically on board with that, and he’s, again, part of the process. “He knows the league, he pays attention to players around the league, and that’s helpful when you’re going through the process of acquiring players, whether it be free agency or the draft. So, to me, not only is he a really good coach, he’s immersed in the personnel, and he’s helpful, makes us think outside the box, challenges us. And that’s what has ultimately led to a lot of good conversations, communications, ultimately making the best decision for the New York Giants.” Schoen knows what to expect from Harbaugh’s teams when they line up each week. “We’re going to be prepared. We’re going to be prepared for the game,” Schoen said. “We’re going to be physical. You’re going to have to go 60 minutes to compete with us. And we’re going to be disciplined on both sides of the ball. And we’re going to be ready to go. I know we’re going to be ready to go. Week in, week out, we’ll be ready.” ‘There’s talent on the roster’ Asked to assess how far along the Giants are in building their roster, Schoen returned to the idea that this team has enough strengths to be competitive. “We have a young quarterback on a rookie deal, going into his second year. We’ve got a number one receiver in (wide receiver) Malik Nabers. Again, not to go position by position, I think we’ve got a strong defense, our offensive line we returned four of five starters, and the number 10 pick is being plugged in at right guard,” Schoen said. “So, should be able to protect the quarterback. So, I feel good about where we are. I feel good about the roster. “There’s talent on the roster to go out and win games and be competitive week in and week out.” The work, though, isn’t done The Giants found themselves in the unusual position of being able to trade two offensive linemen for draft capital before trimming the roster to 53 players. They have seen a few players they released already land jobs on 53-man rosters and practice squads across the league. That indicates league-wide recognition that Schoen isn’t simply trying to talk into existence the idea that the Giants have some talent. The interest from the rest of the league in their players says so. Schoen, though, knows there is still work to be done to bring the Giants to the top level of the NFC. The defensive line needs help. The cornerbacks appeared competent in the spring and summer, but there isn’t a No. 1 guy to match up with the top receivers the Giants will face. More home-run hitting playmakers are needed on offense. In the short term, Schoen admitted Wednesday that adding more talent at defensive tackle is a priority . The Giants will continue to try and improve the roster as much as they can during the season. “Without getting into specifics, but we had some of these conversations this morning,” Schoen said. “There are a few players out there that we are targeting or looking at, or does it make sense financially, or could we sign them? If we sign them, what’s the subsequent move? And some of those positions are positions we have really good depth. Like, hey, maybe an extra, whatever it is, last man on the roster at that position, can we upgrade that? “We’re going to continue to look to upgrade everywhere we can. And so, we’re still having those conversations, and we always will. If a player becomes available that’ll help the roster, help the 53, and help us go win, that’s what we’re here for. We’re always going to do that. Regardless of position, we’ll try to find a way, and we’ll continue to be aggressive in building the 53.” ‘Hope has turned into expectation’ That quote was uttered by Chris Mara during a recent appearance on ESPN New York. “The way I look at it we've used the word hope in the last 10 or 12 years. The hope now has turned into expectations. At least for me it has. I don't hope we win this year. I expect it. I think everybody else does, too." Giants owner Chris Mara on @ESPNNewYork pic.twitter.com/R0hCVWI9bz — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) August 21, 2026 The view here is that the expectation should not include a run to the Super Bowl, or even the NFC Championship Game. Yet. It should include fewer games in which the Giants are not competitive. It should include enough victories, including some over good teams, that Giants fans end the season feeling good about where the team is headed.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants GM Joe Schoen: Team not done addressing defensive tackle
summary: The New York Giants passed on an opportunity to fortify their defensive line this week by not making any waiver claims, despite sitting No. 5 in the waiver claim priority. That, though, does not mean the Giants are done adding players at the position. GM Joe Schoen said on Wednesday that the team will “probably” […]
full_text: The New York Giants passed on an opportunity to fortify their defensive line this week by not making any waiver claims, despite sitting No. 5 in the waiver claim priority. That, though, does not mean the Giants are done adding players at the position. GM Joe Schoen said on Wednesday that the team will “probably” add another veteran player before the Week 1 game against the Dallas Cowboys, at least to the practice quad. “We signed (defensive lineman) D.J. Reader, (defensive lineman) Shelby (Harris), we traded for (defensive lineman) C.J. Okoye, we’ve got DA (defensive lineman Darius Alexander). (Defensive lineman) Bobby Jamison-Travis had a good camp,” Schoen said. “We’ve got a couple of vets on the practice squad, probably going to sign another one next week. So yeah, I feel good where we are right now. And again, we’ll continue, that’s something we’ll continue and see what opportunities are out there.” The defensive linemen on the practice squad are veteran Josh Tupou, a 32-year-old nose tackle who played six games over the past two seasons for the Baltimore Ravens, and undrafted free agent rookie Ben Barten.

title: NY Giants add former NJ star offensive lineman to practice squad
summary: Just one day after filling their 17-player practice squad, the New York Giants have made a change there. General manager Joe Schoen announced during his Wednesday press conference that the Giants have added rookie offensive lineman Geno VanDeMark and dropped cornerback J.T. Woods. VanDeMark could provide interior offensive line depth after the Giants traded Daniel […]
full_text: Geno VanDeMark with the Colts during training camp. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Just one day after filling their 17-player practice squad, the New York Giants have made a change there. General manager Joe Schoen announced during his Wednesday press conference that the Giants have added rookie offensive lineman Geno VanDeMark and dropped cornerback J.T. Woods . VanDeMark could provide interior offensive line depth after the Giants traded Daniel Faalele and Josh Ezeudu before the cutdown from 90 to 53 players, and then saw Jake Kubas sign with the New England Patriots after dropping him from the roster. Evan Neal remains a free agent. VanDeMark, 6-foot-5, 326 pounds, played at Alabama the last two seasons after previously attending Michigan State. At Alabama last season, he played both right and left guard, and also started a game at center. For the Indianapolis Colts this preseason, the undrafted free agent played 80 snaps. He played 64 snaps at left guard, and 16 on the right side. Per his Alabama bio, VanDeMark was the top-rated offensive lineman in New Jersey coming out of high school

title: NY Giants’ QB Jaxson Dart says team’s defense is ‘best reps I could possibly get’
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart had the perfect answer on Tuesday when asked about the fact that the Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys will be his first game action in almost a month. How could the second-year quarterback be sharp? “Every day I’m going against (defensive coordinator) Dennard’s (Wilson) defense, the great […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart talking with Matt Nagy. | Getty Images New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart had the perfect answer on Tuesday when asked about the fact that the Sept. 13 season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys will be his first game action in almost a month. How could the second-year quarterback be sharp? “Every day I’m going against (defensive coordinator) Dennard’s (Wilson) defense, the great players that we have, the scheme that’s in place, and those are some of the best reps that I’m going to get going into Week 1,” Dart said. “So, I’ve been very grateful for those because I would say early on in camp there was a lot of things that maybe caught me by surprise, and against a defense that I haven’t really had a ton of experience playing against. But I think it’s just made myself and this team a lot better, and I don’t take those reps for granted. “So, I feel like those are the best reps I could possibly get each and every day.” Dart played 14 snaps in the Sept. 15 preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings, and did not appear in the final two preseason games. Head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged the concern about Dart’s lack of playing time in preseason. “We have to make sure the practices are the kind of practices that put pressure on him as much as possible,” Harbaugh said. “So, as game-like as we possibly can make them, so he’s ready to go.” Dart seems to think that is exactly what it happening. Here are more takeaways from Dart’s Tuesday media availability: On Odell Beckham making the team … “I would say it’s pretty nostalgic. Just, as a kid, that’s like an icon, in a way where you feel like he changed the game a little bit. You’re in your backyard as a young kid, talking about, ‘Odell,’ when you catch it one hand, or just things like that. So, that part, it’s a really cool experience. From a player standpoint, really just proud of him. He came in here, he earned it. He got better each and every week, and he’s playing his best ball since he got here right now, from just alignment, assignment, playing fast, getting open, making plays. So, really proud of him, and just the dedication that he’s put in to get into this point. And he’s a great teammate as well. So, there’s a lot that we, as younger guys, can learn from him. And he’s still a great player.” On when he knew Beckham could still play … “I think I started to realize that, probably like when you said, just the extra work that we put in in the offseason where – you hear stories like this and you don’t really know how dedicated somebody’s going to be when they walk into a situation like this because he’s damn near had it all, right? He’s experienced and had so much success. But I knew he was serious when he’s flying out across the country to come throw with me, to get those extra reps in. And when you just have that one-on-one time, you see his talent and the things that make him a special player. So, I think just from those experiences and him growing each and every week, you realize that he’s still got it.” On what he likes about the team’s new offense … “There’s just a lot of answers. There’s a lot of plays that you can get to. There’s a lot of options that you can get to, and it lets us just go out there and play football. It lets the creators that we have make plays, get open in space, and us just being on the same page and getting a ton of reps has really helped. And I definitely feel like we’ve taken a lot of really big strides.” On his progress from the spring … “I feel so much better. I feel in command. I feel confident. In this offense, there’s a lot that’s put on the quarterback’s plate, but it’s exactly how I want it. It’s exactly how I viewed this coming together. And we still have a lot of room to improve and grow as a unit, but I’m definitely feeling way better each and every day, continuing to learn, continuing to grow as a player, and just the comfort in the offense, seeing the defense and putting ourselves in great situations. On potentially having Malik Nabers in the lineup Week 1 … “He’s just a game-changing player. So, whenever he’s out there on the field, whenever his time is ready for us as a team, I think it’s going to change a lot, and I can’t wait for that time to come. But at the same time, I think that we’ve done a really good job of putting ourselves in position to be ready and be prepared for any situation that may come our way. “So, guys have stepped up and done a really good job, and like I said, whenever his time is to come back, we’re all going to be really excited, and he’s a game-changing player.”

full_text: Football: Los Angeles Rams Josh Karty (16) in action, kicks off vs Baltimore Ravens at M&T StadiumBaltimore, MD 10/12/2025CREDIT: Simon Bruty (Photo by Simon Bruty/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images/Getty Images) (Set Number: X164783) Earlier in the week, the Jets claimed kicker Blake Gruppe off waivers from the Indianapolis Colts. Veteran kicker Jason Sanders was released and subsequently signed to the practice squad. Per Ian Rapoport, the Jets are continuing to investigate answers at the position. Free agent kicker Joshua Karty, who has kicked the last two seasons for the #Rams , is working out for the #Jets today. pic.twitter.com/Zo10rdDjW4 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 2, 2026 During his collegiate career at Stanford, Karty was one of the best kickers in America and was twice selected as a First Team All American. This led to him become the rare kicker who was actually drafted. The Rams selected him in the sixth round in 2024. Karty had a solid rookie season but struggled in 2025, connecting on only 10 of 15 attempts. This led the Rams to replace him with Harrison Mevis (who spent training camp with the Jets in 2025). Karty signed with the Cardinals before being released in June. A week ago special teams coach Chris Banjo declared that the team’s kicking competition was over. Jason Sanders had won the job. Now just one week later, the Jets have a different kicker on the roster and are actively looking at alternatives. It seems possible that this team’s opening day kicker still isn’t on the roster.

(Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Howie Roseman: The bottom line is winning, Jalen Hurts and Nick Sirianni do that – PFT Roseman said on WIP that he doesn’t agree with the perception that quarterback Jalen Hurts is “on the clock” and is heading into a make-or-break year to remain the franchise quarterback. “No I don’t agree with that,” Roseman said. Roseman said Hurts and head coach Nick Sirianni are proven winners, and that’s what the franchise needs. In games started by Hurts since Sirianni became head coach, the Eagles are 56-22 in the regular season and 6-4 in the postseason, including winning a Super Bowl. “I think the bottom line for us, in the position we’re in, and really for all our fan base, is winning football games,” Roseman said. “And all [Hurts] does is win football games, and that includes our head coach as well. For me, the barometer is winning football games. In terms of what Jalen does, he’s another guy with a tremendous track record. All he does is go out and play good football. Really excited to have him as our quarterback, excited about this season and what we have going forward, and I know there are a lot of fan bases out there that would love the results we’ve had with him as our starting quarterback.” NFC East training camp recap – BGN The defense looks like it’s going to be very, very good. The offense? Eh. The starting QB is using ChatGPT for Stuart Smalley daily affirmations. I am not saying that I can throw a bowling ball farther than Andy Dalton can throw a football, but watching Dalton it feels like I can throw a bowling ball farther than Dalton can throw a football. Dalton doesn’t matter though, he’s either gone by the time the season starts or if he plays then things are going pretty poorly and there’s plenty of larger problems. Patience Needed – Iggles Blitz The Eagles are being patient with Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers. Both guys had limited summers. Lemon was hurt and Stowers struggled before getting hurt. The Eagles spent Top 60 picks on both players so they will get plenty of time as long as the players are making a good faith effort to improve. And both are doing that. The QB situation is trickier. The team says all the right things about Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton. The tape says all the wrong things. But tape can be tricky. NFL players, coaches, GMs under the most pressure in 2026 – ESPN Let’s touch on that offensive shift, which involves three young offensive assistants around the NFL. O’Connell is about to ask his quarterback the same question that these assistants will of theirs, but as a highly regarded head coach, he’s not on the same sort of hot seat that any coordinator is in a given season. The Commanders (Jayden Daniels), Ravens (Lamar Jackson) and Eagles (Jalen Hurts) have three successful quarterbacks who have thrived working out of the shotgun or pistol and made a meaningful impact moving the ball with their legs on designed quarterback runs. And to some extent, those three teams are going to ask their quarterbacks to do something different in 2026 by operating from under center. […] It’s a big bet by three teams with quarterbacks who have already proved themselves as successful without needing to go under center very often. If those bets work out, Blough, Doyle and Mannion could be in line to earn head-coaching consideration as early as next offseason. If not, well, the world isn’t very forgiving to young playcallers. Mannion is the fourth Eagles coordinator in four years. Klint Kubiak had three single-season stints as a coordinator before landing his head-coaching gig with the Raiders. If things go wrong, all three teams could be pursuing new options and moving their quarterbacks back out from under center in 2027. Jonathan Greenard’s availability is unknown, but his position coach says Eagles pass rusher has ‘been an A-plus’ – Inquirer At Sunday’s roster cutdown deadline, Howie Roseman decided that Jonathan Greenard would not start the year on the Physically Unable to Perform list after dealing with a pectoral strain throughout training camp. The Eagles general manager said that the veteran pass rusher would be “playing sooner rather than later,” but he added that he would keep Greenard’s exact timeline “close to the vest.” While Greenard’s availability for the Sept. 13 season opener against the Washington Commanders might be a mystery to the public, his potential impact among the Eagles edge rusher corps once he returns to action isn’t in doubt — /at least to his position coach, Jeremiah Washburn. “He’s what we thought he’d be,” Washburn said Wednesday. “And working really hard and staying engaged and been an A-plus in the meeting room and on the field.” How one book helped Eagles’ Saquon Barkley and inspired Nick Sirianni – The Athletic “The danger of comparison,” said Barkley, one season after entering NFL record books. “Comparison is stealing joy. There we go.” Seven months later, Barkley sat in a team meeting to begin the Philadelphia Eagles’ 2026 training camp. Standing in front of the room, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni shared summer reading with the team. It was the same book — Joshua Medcalf’s 2015 self-published self-help title. “I gave this book to some of you guys, have some extra copies in there if some of you are interested in this book, ‘Chop Wood Carry Water,’” Sirianni told the players, as documented by team footage. “Really good book. It’s about how to fall in love with the process. And my favorite chapter in this book was being faithful in the small things. …Here are the highlights of this chapter: Focus on the small things, focus on the things you can control.” Eagles TEs coach excited about Stowers’ development, but preaches patience – NBCSP “I think for every player coming into the NFL,” Mahaffey said, “I’m always extremely mindful of a rookie that they have the proper mindset in terms of, ‘What’s our point of focus each and every single day?’ And the most important thing is that you’re remaining process-driven. If your process is sound, you’re applying the coaching, you’re giving great effort, you’re being a good teammate, you’re doing things with physicality, ventually, those types of things are going to come. I think it’s always a matter of your standards vs. your circumstance. Obviously, your standards are always going to be extremely high, set by Coach (Nick) Sirianni and Howie (Roseman) and the rest of the coaching staff. And at the same time, there’s a process to that. Usually, growth is not going to be linear. You’re going to have to, for any player, for the whole entire tight end unit, we’re going to face some adversity at some point. But our process has to remain the same. And eventually, I think you just start to stack days, you get a little bit better, you get a little better and hopefully over the duration, you’re stacking those type of days, you’re building the proper habits that eventually you’ll get to where you want to be.” Suspect involved in burglary of Saquon Barkley’s house arrested, officials say – NBC10 A man involved in the attempted break-in of Saquon Barkley’s home has been taken into custody, a source told NBC10. The suspect has been identified as 24-year-old Jabir Parker, of Philadelphia, officials said. According to the Montgomery County District Attorney’s Office, Parker is facing charges for two home break-ins and the attempted break-in of a third home that occurred in both Montgomery and Chester counties. The 24-year-old will now look to get healthy and catch on with…

title: Howie Roseman explains why the Eagles kept 4 quarterbacks
summary: The Eagles GM filled the 53-man roster on Sunday and then worked on bringing guys back on the practice squad for most of Monday. He spoke with reporters several hours after the waiver wire results were revealed, and he talked about some of his decisions, such as keeping four quarterbacks and why he risked Uar […]
full_text: The Eagles GM filled the 53-man roster on Sunday and then worked on bringing guys back on the practice squad for most of Monday. He spoke with reporters several hours after the waiver wire results were revealed, and he talked about some of his decisions, such as keeping four quarterbacks and why he risked Uar Bernard and Joshua Weru on the wire. Here’s what the GM had to say: On keeping 4 QBs Roseman wouldn’t talk about who the No. 2 guy is at quarterback heading into Week 1, saying that they’re keeping everything close to the vest ahead of their season opener against the Commanders. As for why the Eagles kept four quarterbacks on the active roster, the GM explained that it’s the most important position in sports, and they think each guy has value for the team. He noted that some of that is short-term value, and some is long term, but they wanted to make the right decision for the the organization. “It’s just such a valuable position. From our perspective, last year, obviously we took someone in the fifth round [Kyle McCord], let him go. He left our practice squad to go somewhere else, traded for a sixth-round pick. These guys are valuable. They take time to develop at the same time. That position is so valuable to this organization over a long period of time.” Former Eagles draft pick Kyle McCord was traded by the Packers to the Dolphins just ahead of this year’s roster deadline for a sixth round pick. Roseman isn’t one to miss the lesson, and the lesson there was to protect quarterbacks from leaving for nothing. On the IPP players Roseman admitted that he’s never really comfortable that a guy they release ends up clearing waivers, because they don’t know what other teams are going to do. They do all the research they can, and try to consider what other teams are seeing from players and what might have been happening during closed practices. “Certainly didn’t want to get four guys claimed. That doesn’t feel great. But from our perspective, development is real. These guys [Uar Bernard and Joshua Weru] have tremendous ability to be developed. They want to be developed. They have tools in their body, they’ve got great character, but it’s new to them.” He was also careful with comparisons to Jordan Mailata, who started through the IPP, saying that people aren’t going to see another success story like Mailata in 30, 40 years. “[Mailata] had just a unique combination of size, strength, athleticism and pro experience as an athlete. I think sometimes we forget Uar has never played organized sports before. It’s a different bar. I think if we’re just judging everyone through the lens of Jordan Mailata, it’s going to be hard to give these guys a fair chance. Still very excited about them, really glad that they did get through. Certainly wasn’t certain about that, but I’m glad they’re back here.” The GM went on to emphasize that everything is all new to Bernard, but also gave the new player a lot of credit for the work he’s done and the effort he’s given. “Even the first preseason game, for [Bernard] to go play that game for the first time in front of that stadium. Tremendous work ethic, tremendous character. Obviously, he’s got some God-given ability there in terms of strength and power, but when you think about this game and blocking schemes and getting off the ball and all the things that guys have taken for granted, those are things that come with time and reps. He’s got a great coach in Coach [Clint] Hurtt there working with him.” He also mentioned that expectations need to be a little bit reasonable, and pointed to an example of an IPP player who came into the league in 2023 and just now made his first active roster in 2026. Not that he expects these guys to follow the same timeline, but Roseman said it’s a reminder that it can take time and patience. On keeping TE E.J. Jenkins “E.J. is a great story. When you talk about a receiver at Georgia Tech who transformed his body, he’s 260 pounds, he’s 6’6″, he’s got 34-inch arms. You see in this league where the position is going, where it’s trending. A lot of similar offensive systems to some of the things that we’re running where these wide tight ends, they’re highly valued in free agency, they’re highly valued in the draft. For us to be able to develop E.J. and his skillset, which as a former receiver has really not only turned to, obviously he’s a big target in the passing game, but a point of attack player. His pass protection — when we went over his pass protection, it is really, really good to have a tight end who’s able to pass protect like he is and then in the run game be able to help. It’s just being highly valued, and he contributed on special teams. Just E.J.’s body of work over time, sometimes you forget he played for us in the Super Bowl in 2024, but great developmental story for our organization, for the people who develop players, and really just excited about the role that he can have on this football team.” On reuniting with Zach Ertz “First, I’d say what an unbelievable player, what an unbelievable person, tremendous respect for him. At the same time, love what we have going in our tight end room, too. I would say, have talked to Zach over a period of time, obviously rehabbing his ACL and the relationship, just like a lot of our former players who’ve been here. But like anything else, wouldn’t get into any conversations about anything other than from a big picture perspective. In my opinion, one of the greatest tight ends to play the game and just tremendous respect for him, and also excited about the tight ends that we have here.” Other notables Roseman addressed not making any trades in August, and said that he would’ve loved to do something, but the timing wasn’t right and they didn’t feel like a move was right for the team. As for Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers and the expectations for them to contribute right away, the Eagles’ GM said that he has tremendous confidence in them, but also pointed out that in any other profession, people get time to develop. When asked about bringing RB Dameon Pierce back on the practice squad, Roseman said that with some guys, they just don’t have enough time for a full evaluation due to injuries. That was the case with Pierce, but they knew they wanted him on the team, and can trust that if he’s needed, the RB would be able to produce at a high level. The Eagles consider the first four weeks of the season another ramp up period, and with the team running their actual playbook, they’ll have a better sense of how players are developing in the new system. Roseman noted that the trade deadline is still months away, so there’s plenty of time to evaluate things and making changes, as needed. Roseman was very complimentary of WR Elijah Moore who he said had a great camp, was able to separate, and knowshow to get open. They had been following Moore’s career since Joe Douglas drafted him to the Jets, and they didn’t want to risk losing him to the waiver wire. The GM also really likes the receiver core as a whole. He mentioned that they really believe in DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks is exactly who they thought he would be, and everyone saw Darius Cooper’s growth and development to past year. He also said they have tremendous confidence in Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown, in addition to Elijah Moore. Roseman admitted that heading into camp he was really focused on the interior offensive line group, and he’s really really excited about where the young guys are at this point. He noted that the success of the group through training camp is a credit to new OL coach Chris Kuper.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: NFC East training camp recap
summary: For the first time in over two decades, the NFC East had back to back winners. Can the Philadelphia Eagles three peat? The rest of the division seems to be trying their best to help them. Washington Commanders Football Team It is basically impossible to make LSU football look sympathetic in 2026. Jayden Daniels did […]
full_text: For the first time in over two decades, the NFC East had back to back winners. Can the Philadelphia Eagles three peat? The rest of the division seems to be trying their best to help them. Washington Commanders Football Team It is basically impossible to make LSU football look sympathetic in 2026. Jayden Daniels did it. Adam Peters signed four 32 year olds, a 31 year old, and two 30 year olds in August alone . Last year the Commanders went 0-3 in the preseason, finishing with a 30-3 loss to the Ravens, and then went 5-12 (in honor of Jayden Daniels). This year they went 1-2 in the preseason, with their win being against a Dolphins team that is not even trying to look like they’re trying, and finished with a 41-3 loss to the Ravens. Their weak OL is already depleted. LT Laremy Tunsil is out for most of the year, and C Nick Allegretti got hurt on day one of camp and hasn’t practiced since. The Commanders have said that they have no plans to bring back the old Redskins name or logo, but last week started selling merchandise with the Redskins name and (part of the) logo. It sold out in two days. Most teams get better as training camp progresses. Washington got off on the wrong foot and went downhill from there. New York Giants Jaxson Dart doesn’t understand why every time he takes a hit that makes you wonder if he’s okay, which has become his signature move, that he has to go to the blue tent. Malik Nabers is totally fine, he just left practice early, which wasn’t planned, because he felt like it? He’s feeling good but we’ll see if he plays Week 1, he might have a schedule conflict or something? Nothing to see here. Cam Skattebo is getting penalized during practice. Practice. This is the year 2026 and Odell Beckham is on a roster. Speaking of, new boat pic just dropped: . @Giants album cover just dropped 💿 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pTlE5XLe1t — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 The Giants have some potentially fun players but the best entertainment they offer this year might be John Harbaugh’s exasperated reactions as his mediocre and dumb roster consistently fails him. Dallas Cowboys Dak Prescott said the Cowboys is “the Greatest Offense There Is.” They were 7th in scoring last year. He may not know what any of the words he said actually mean. The reaction to this proclamation was that people mostly laughed if off. That pretty much sums up the state of the Cowboys. It wasn’t that long ago that the Cowboys could sign some washed up depth player and then every screaming head TV show would spend half an hour asking themselves if this was the piece that would finally put the Cowboys over the top. Now we just shrug and move on to the next thing. It’s one thing to be mediocre, which, after back to back 7 win seasons, the Cowboys are. It’s another to be irrelevant. Philadelphia Eagles The defense looks like it’s going to be very, very good. The offense? Eh. The starting QB is using ChatGPT for Stuart Smalley daily affirmations. I am not saying that I can throw a bowling ball farther than Andy Dalton can throw a football, but watching Dalton it feels like I can throw a bowling ball farther than Dalton can throw a football. Dalton doesn’t matter though, he’s either gone by the time the season starts or if he plays then things are going pretty poorly and there’s plenty of larger problems. What does matter is that the Eagles have an AJ Brown sized hole to replace and no one has stepped up to fill it this summer. If the Cowboys, Giants, or Commanders were looking at Dontayvion Wicks, whose most productive season was his 39 catch, 581 yard rookie season three years ago; a 1st round pick who missed basically all of camp with injury; Hollywood Brown, who the Chiefs didn’t bring back; and a UDFA who caught nine passes last year… we’d be clowning them. Zach Ertz won’t fix anything . This time three years ago, Sean Mannion was sitting on his couch hoping someone would call him for a practice squad gig. Now he’s got to make this work.
